title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午秋八月天下例選
士於鄉監察御史劉思問奉
命按江西寔司監臨慎重斯舉爰
飭所司申科條杜弊竇冀得
真材以貢
天子屆期以大典曁學正吳譽聞
===
爲考試官敎諭鄭源洽陳明
表陳舜道潘龍唐宗正沈奎
燦廖元烺侯嘉祐張輅甫爲
同考試官而以布政司左布
政使馮惟訥左參議嚴大紀
司提調按察司副使張岳張
仲謙司監試簾內外罔有不
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午秋八月，天下例選士於鄉。監察御史劉思問奉命按江西，寔司監臨。慎重斯舉，爰飭所司，申科條，杜弊竇，冀得真材以貢天子。屆期，以大典曁學正吳譽聞爲考試官，敎諭鄭源洽、陳明表、陳舜道、潘龍、唐宗正、沈奎燦、廖元烺、侯嘉祐、張輅甫爲同考試官，而以布政司左布政使馮惟訥、左參議嚴大紀司提調，按察司副使張岳、張仲謙司監試。簾內外罔有不
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the gengwu year of the Longqing reign (1570), candidates throughout the realm were selected through Provincial Examinations according to established practice. Investigating Censor Liu Siwen, commissioned to inspect Jiangxi, served as Supervising Official. Treating this undertaking with great care, he directed the responsible offices to reaffirm the examination regulations and close avenues for malpractice, hoping to obtain truly talented men to present to the Son of Heaven.

When the appointed time arrived, Dadian and Instructor Wu Yuwen were appointed Examiners. Instructors Zheng Yuanqia, Chen Mingbiao, Chen Shundao, Pan Long, Tang Zongzheng, Shen Kuican, Liao Yuanlang, Hou Jiayou, and Zhang Lufu were appointed Associate Examiners. Feng Weine, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yan Daji, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, of the Provincial Administration Commission served as Proctors. Zhang Yue and Zhang Zhongqian, Surveillance Vice Commissioners of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, oversaw the examination. Among those inside and outside the curtain separating the examiners from the outer administration, there were none who were not…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
肅百執事罔有不虔乃合提
學副使陳萬言所選士三千
有奇三試之拔其儁得九十
有五人併錄其文二十一篇
以
獻遵
成制也錄成大典乃作而言曰斯
===
舉也庶幾得眞材以爲
國家用乎夫天之生材代不乏
人至需材以用則往往稱乏
焉何哉由選舉弗愼而士之
渝節窳行者衆也今之選士
以文耳乃若士之所以自效
者貴有其實孔子有曰不患
punctuated:
肅，百執事罔有不虔。乃合提學副使陳萬言所選士三千有奇，三試之，拔其儁，得九十有五人，併錄其文二十一篇以獻，遵成制也。
錄成，大典乃作而言曰：「斯舉也，庶幾得眞材以爲國家用乎？夫天之生材，代不乏人；至需材以用，則往往稱乏焉，何哉？由選舉弗愼，而士之渝節窳行者衆也。今之選士以文耳，乃若士之所以自效者，貴有其實。孔子有曰：『不患
translation_en:
…solemn, and all those carrying out their duties were without exception conscientious. They then assembled the more than three thousand candidates selected by Chen Wanyan, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, and examined them in three sessions. Selecting the outstanding among them, they obtained ninety-five men. They also compiled twenty-one of their compositions for presentation to the throne, in accordance with established regulations.
When the record was completed, Dadian wrote as follows: “May this examination have secured true talent for the service of the state? Heaven produces talented men in every age; yet when talent is needed for service, we repeatedly hear that it is scarce. Why is this? Because selection is conducted without due care, and many scholars compromise their principles and fall into corrupt conduct. Nowadays scholars are selected solely on their writing. Yet when it comes to how scholars prove themselves in service, what matters is that they possess genuine substance. Confucius said: ‘Do not worry …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
無位患所以立書稱學古入
官豈徒文云乎哉夫玉壺必
求其所以盛寶劔必求其所
以斷玉壺無盛雖赤瓊碧瑥
無取也寶劔不斷雖含影承
光無取也士徒以文而無其
實則雖咀華擷繡以競工妍
===
無取也維茲江右爲斗牛分
野廬嶽鍾秀彭蠡涵靈才賢
挺生自昔稱盛肆我
皇上
神聖御極
景命維新
際重熙累洽之運
punctuated:
無位，患所以立。」書稱：「學古入官。」豈徒文云乎哉？夫玉壺必求其所以盛，寶劔必求其所以斷。玉壺無盛，雖赤瓊碧瑥，無取也；寶劔不斷，雖含影承光，無取也。士徒以文而無其實，則雖咀華擷繡，以競工妍，無取也。
維茲江右，爲斗牛分野，廬嶽鍾秀，彭蠡涵靈，才賢挺生，自昔稱盛。肆我皇上神聖御極，景命維新，際重熙累洽之運，
translation_en:
…having no position; worry about what qualifies you to hold one.” The Book of Documents says, “Study antiquity and enter office.” Can this mean literary accomplishment alone? With a jade vessel, one must seek its capacity to hold something; with a precious sword, one must seek its capacity to cut. If a jade vessel holds nothing, even one of red jade or green wen-jade [?] is of no use. If a precious sword cannot cut, even Hanying or Chengguang [?] is of no use. If scholars possess literary accomplishment alone, without substance, then even if they savor blossoms and gather embroidery, competing in artistry and elegance, they are of no use.
This region of Jiangyou lies within the terrestrial domain corresponding to the Dipper and Ox celestial lodges. Mount Lu concentrates nature’s beauty, and Lake Pengli holds its numinous powers. Outstanding men of talent and virtue arise here, and their abundance has been celebrated since antiquity. Now our Emperor, in his divine sagacity, occupies the imperial throne; the glorious Mandate is renewed, in an age of successive splendor and accumulated peace…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
懷保邦制治之圖乃猶屢降
明詔皇皇求賢頃歲
命九卿臺諫各舉所知既又
命督學憲臣於額貢外特加掄拔
海內之士感激思奮莫不喁
喁嚮風願自效於
明盛之世以不負
===
聖天子菁莪棫樸之化今觀爾多
士之文氣閎而肆旨雋而遠
詞腴而則榷古苞道劑事摛
藻黜夸毗絕玄騖以湔其剽
竊支離之習學古有獲發爲
精華他日所以立乎其位而
適於用者在是斯乃埏埴乎
punctuated: 懷保邦制治之圖，乃猶屢降明詔，皇皇求賢。頃歲，命九卿臺諫各舉所知，既又命督學憲臣於額貢外特加掄拔。海內之士感激思奮，莫不喁喁嚮風，願自效於明盛之世，以不負聖天子菁莪棫樸之化。今觀爾多士之文，氣閎而肆，旨雋而遠，詞腴而則；榷古苞道，劑事摛藻，黜夸毗，絕玄騖，以湔其剽竊支離之習。學古有獲，發爲精華，他日所以立乎其位而適於用者在是。斯乃埏埴乎
translation_en:
…cherishing plans to secure the realm and establish good government, he nevertheless repeatedly issued enlightened edicts, earnestly seeking worthy men. In recent years, he ordered the Nine Chief Ministers and the censorial and remonstrance officials each to recommend men they knew. He then further ordered the education intendants to make special selections beyond the regular quota of tribute students. Scholars throughout the empire, moved by gratitude and eager to exert themselves, all looked expectantly toward his influence, wishing to offer their service in this enlightened and flourishing age, so as not to fail the sage Son of Heaven’s nurturing transformation, celebrated in the Odes “Luxuriant Southernwood” and “Oak and Thorn.”

Now, examining the writings of you assembled scholars, I find their spirit expansive and unrestrained, their meaning distinguished and far-reaching, and their language rich yet disciplined. You weigh antiquity and embrace the Way, assess affairs and display literary brilliance, reject boastful flattery, and renounce flights into abstruseness, thereby washing away habits of plagiarism and fragmentation. Your study of antiquity has borne fruit, finding expression in refined brilliance. Herein lies what will enable you in future to occupy your positions and meet the demands of service. This indeed is to be shaped, as clay is shaped, by…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天地之元氣漸濡乎
聖神之至化而所得於山川之助
者有自來矣夫大江以西水
所會也襟帶江湖浸浴天漢
汪濊淜湃莫可名狀然始於
習坎而進蓋自章萍盱饒澴
會城而東注瀦爲彭蠡雖千
===
氾萬派其發不同然入江以
濡潤萬物則同有源故耳豫
章諸山木所麗也岑翳林垠
蔽虧雲日藉土壤飽雨露雖
灌栵異品然自漸苞之始積
歲月以成干霄是爲碩材中
方𦓔繩墨之用爲旅楹爲烏
punctuated:
天地之元氣，漸濡乎聖神之至化，而所得於山川之助者有自來矣。夫大江以西，水所會也，襟帶江湖，浸浴天漢，汪濊淜湃，莫可名狀。然始於習坎而進，蓋自章、萍、盱、饒，澴會城而東注，瀦爲彭蠡。雖千氾萬派，其發不同，然入江以濡潤萬物則同，有源故耳。
豫章諸山，木所麗也。岑翳林垠，蔽虧雲日，藉土壤，飽雨露。雖灌栵異品，然自漸苞之始，積歲月以成干霄，是爲碩材，中方𦓔繩墨之用，爲旅楹，爲烏
translation_en:
…the primal vital force of Heaven and Earth, steeped in the consummate transforming influence of our sage and divine sovereign; and the benefits derived from the aid of mountains and rivers have deep roots. The region west of the Great River is where waters converge. Rivers and lakes gird it; the River of Heaven bathes it. Vast and surging, its waters defy description. Yet they begin by advancing through successive depths. From Zhang, Ping, Xu, and Rao, they circle the provincial capital [?] and flow eastward, gathering into Pengli Lake. Though their thousand streams and myriad branches arise in different places, they alike enter the Great River and moisten all things. This is because they have sources.
The mountains of Yuzhang are where trees take root. Shaded peaks and forest margins obscure clouds and sun. Drawing sustenance from the soil and drinking their fill of rain and dew, the trees, though differing in kind as shrubs and thickets, grow from their first emerging buds and, over accumulated months and years, come to reach the skies. They thus become great timbers, fit to be squared and worked to the carpenter’s line [?], to serve as ranks of pillars and as dark …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
桷而明堂清廟取焉其植本
固耳今多士稟榮光之氣通
茂遂之精炳然蔚然殆龍門
之瀾鄧林之植也以之膏澤
生民蔭覆下土磑磑乎經世
有用之文信乎山川之淵源
根本不可誣也苟汩其源撥
===
其本亦溷濁潢汙竅撓腐質
云耳奚取乎文哉孔子曰文
莫吾猶人也躬行君子則吾
未之有得言不貴於文也爾
多士盍亦思鄉之先哲有以
道德功業節義表見于世者
文獻具存典刑如在景行而
punctuated: 桷，而明堂清廟取焉，其植本固耳。今多士稟榮光之氣，通茂遂之精，炳然蔚然，殆龍門之瀾、鄧林之植也。以之膏澤生民，蔭覆下土，磑磑乎經世有用之文！信乎山川之淵源根本不可誣也。苟汩其源，撥其本，亦溷濁潢汙、竅撓腐質云耳，奚取乎文哉？孔子曰：「文莫吾猶人也，躬行君子則吾未之有得。」言不貴於文也。爾多士盍亦思鄉之先哲，有以道德、功業、節義表見于世者，文獻具存，典刑如在，景行而
translation_en:
…rafters, selected for use in the Hall of Enlightenment and the pure ancestral temple—all because their roots are firmly planted. Now you assembled scholars receive the vital breath of radiant glory and partake of the essence of flourishing growth. Brilliant and luxuriant, you are like the surging waters of Longmen and the trees of Denglin. Through these endowments you may bestow blessings upon the people and shelter the land below. How imposing [?] is such cultivated learning, useful for ordering the world! Truly, the deep sources and firm roots supplied by these mountains and rivers cannot be gainsaid. If their sources are muddied and their roots uprooted, they become merely turbid, stagnant pools and hollow, warped, rotten timber [?]. What value would their outward refinement then have?
Confucius said: “In literary cultivation, perhaps I am like other men; but as for putting the conduct of a gentleman into practice, I have not yet attained it.” This means that literary cultivation alone is not what is prized. You assembled scholars, why not also reflect upon the former worthies of your native region, who distinguished themselves before the world through moral virtue, meritorious achievements, integrity, and righteousness? Their writings and the testimony concerning them survive in full; their exemplary models seem still present. Revere their lofty conduct and…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
取衷焉斯躬行無愧庶幾學
古之實是主司今日求材之
意也雖然今日之舉大典藉
是以塞一時之責耳不能無
懼焉夫求金於沙簸而揚之
又從而汰之以爲精矣及洪
爐將熾飛廉煽之火烈金鎔
===
融液澄澈而飛者鉛錫沉者
瓦礫則又不能不致咎於簸
而揚之者之不精今日之與
是選者能保其不爲鉛錫與
瓦礫乎是宜需用輒有乏材
之憂而主司之所爲懼也夫
主司之選士也慎於其始而
punctuated:
取衷焉，斯躬行無愧，庶幾學古之實，是主司今日求材之意也。
雖然，今日之舉大典，藉是以塞一時之責耳，不能無懼焉。夫求金於沙，簸而揚之，又從而汰之，以爲精矣。及洪爐將熾，飛廉煽之，火烈金鎔，融液澄澈，而飛者鉛錫，沉者瓦礫，則又不能不致咎於簸而揚之者之不精。今日之與是選者，能保其不爲鉛錫與瓦礫乎？是宜需用輒有乏材之憂，而主司之所爲懼也。夫主司之選士也，慎於其始，而
translation_en:
…and draw from them a proper standard. Then your personal conduct will be beyond reproach, and you may approach the true substance of learning from antiquity. This is the intention of the examination officials in seeking talent today.
Nevertheless, conducting this great ceremony today serves merely to discharge the responsibility of the moment; we cannot be without apprehension. When seeking gold in sand, one shakes and winnows it, then washes it further, believing it to be pure. But when the great furnace is about to blaze, and Feilian, the wind god, fans it, the fire burns fiercely and the metal melts. The molten liquid becomes clear, yet what flies off is lead and tin, and what sinks is broken tiles and gravel. One then cannot help blaming those who shook and winnowed it for failing to refine it thoroughly. Can those selected today guarantee that they will not prove to be lead and tin, or broken tiles and gravel? Thus it is understandable that whenever talent is needed, there is anxiety over its scarcity. This is what the examination officials fear. In selecting scholars, the examination officials exercise care at the outset, and …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
後
國家之用人也能保之於其終
爾多士其亦思所以自效以
仰稱
聖天子求賢之
盛典哉是舉也巡撫江西右副都
御史今陞戶部右侍郎劉光
濟興學飭戎定經綏宇提督
南贛右僉都御史先任張翀
今殷從儉輯武宣猷聲敎丕
振若右布政使劉炌左參政
方攸績右參政施篤臣陳絳
左參議馮敏功副使徐學謨
僉事康憲徐時可參將張斌
punctuated:
後，國家之用人也，能保之於其終。爾多士，其亦思所以自效，以仰稱聖天子求賢之盛典哉！
是舉也，巡撫江西右副都御史、今陞戶部右侍郎劉光濟，興學飭戎，定經綏宇；提督南贛右僉都御史，先任張翀、今殷從儉，輯武宣猷，聲敎丕振。若右布政使劉炌、左參政方攸績、右參政施篤臣、陳絳、左參議馮敏功、副使徐學謨、僉事康憲、徐時可、參將張斌，
translation_en:
…then, when the state employs men, it can ensure their worthiness to the end. You assembled scholars should also consider how to prove yourselves in service, so as to live up to the august undertaking through which the sagely Son of Heaven seeks worthy men!
For this examination, Liu Guangji, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, fostered learning, put military affairs in order, established guiding principles, and brought peace to the region. Zhang Chong, the former holder of the post of Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and Yin Congjian, its current holder, brought military affairs into order and promulgated state policies, greatly enhancing the reach of imperial authority and instruction.
Among the other officials were Liu Kai, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Fang Youji, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Shi Duchen and Chen Jiang, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners; Feng Mingong, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Xu Xuemo, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Kang Xian and Xu Shike, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Zhang Bin, Assistant Regional Commander…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
蔡汝蘭署都指揮僉事王國
光陳大鵬郭堅則襄理於外
右布政使方弘靜按察使楊
守魯右參政王元春副使吳
道直僉事龔大器以遷秩行
戶科都給事中宋良佐戶部
主事田成法陳應春李應蘭
===
太常寺博士郭堵中書舍人
詹洪基以使事至皆樂觀盛
美者也于例得書
浙江紹興府儒學敎授顧大
典謹序
punctuated:
蔡汝蘭、署都指揮僉事王國光、陳大鵬、郭堅，則襄理於外。右布政使方弘靜、按察使楊守魯、右參政王元春、副使吳道直、僉事龔大器，以遷秩行。戶科都給事中宋良佐、戶部主事田成法、陳應春、李應蘭、太常寺博士郭堵、中書舍人詹洪基，以使事至，皆樂觀盛美者也，于例得書。
浙江紹興府儒學敎授顧大典謹序。
translation_en:
…Cai Rulan and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Wang Guoguang, Chen Dapeng, and Guo Jian assisted with affairs outside. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Fang Hongjing, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Yang Shoulu, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Yuanchun, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wu Daozhi, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Gong Daqi departed upon promotion.
Song Liangzuo, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; Tian Chengfa, Chen Yingchun, and Li Yinglan, Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue; Guo Du, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and Zhan Hongji, Central Drafting Office Secretary, arrived on official missions. All delighted in witnessing this splendid occasion, and their names may be recorded here according to established practice.
Preface respectfully composed by Gu Dadian, Prefectural School Instructor of Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史劉思問〔汝知河南孟縣人丙辰進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使馮惟訥〔汝言山東臨朐縣籍遼東廣寧左衛人戊戌進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議嚴大紀〔汝肅太醫院籍浙江餘杭縣人己未進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司副使張岳〔汝宗浙江餘姚縣人己未進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司副使張仲謙〔士益直隸上海縣籍華亭縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官
浙江紹興府儒學教授顧大典〔道行直隸吳江縣人戊辰進士〕
河南開封府許州儒學學正吳譽聞〔必修廣東順德縣人戊午貢士〕
同考試官

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰我未見好仁者惡不仁者好仁者無
以尚之惡不仁者其爲仁矣不使不仁
者加乎其身有能一日用其力於仁矣
乎我未見力不足者蓋有之矣我未之
見也
天地之道可一言而盡也
人皆可以爲堯舜有諸孟子曰然
===
易
乾始能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉
大哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也六爻發
揮旁通情也時乘六龍以御天也雲行
雨施天下平也
九五甘節吉往有尚
二篇之策萬有一千五百二十
物相遇而後聚故受之以萃萃者聚也聚
而上者謂之升故受之以升
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「我未見好仁者、惡不仁者。好仁者，無以尚之；惡不仁者，其爲仁矣，不使不仁者加乎其身。有能一日用其力於仁矣乎？我未見力不足者。蓋有之矣，我未之見也。」

天地之道，可一言而盡也。

「人皆可以爲堯舜，有諸？」孟子曰：「然。」

易

乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。六爻發揮，旁通情也。時乘六龍，以御天也。雲行雨施，天下平也。

九五，甘節，吉，往有尚。

二篇之策，萬有一千五百二十。

物相遇而後聚，故受之以萃。萃者，聚也。聚而上者謂之升，故受之以升。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “I have never seen anyone who loves benevolence or hates what is not benevolent. One who loves benevolence sets nothing above it. One who hates what is not benevolent, in practicing benevolence, allows nothing unbenevolent to touch his person. Is there anyone who can devote his strength to benevolence for a single day? I have never seen anyone whose strength was insufficient. Perhaps such a person exists, but I have never seen him.”

“The Way of Heaven and Earth can be fully expressed in a single phrase.”

“Everyone can become a Yao or a Shun—is this so?” Mengzi said: “It is.”

Book of Changes

“Qian, the Creative, brings things into being and benefits all under Heaven with its excellent bounty, without specifying what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian! Firm and strong, central and correct, it is pure, unmixed, and refined. Its six lines unfold and extend, comprehending the circumstances in every direction. In due season it rides the six dragons to govern Heaven. Clouds move and rain falls; all under Heaven is at peace.”

“Nine in the fifth place: Sweet limitation. Auspicious. Going forward brings esteem.”

“The yarrow-stalk counts of the two parts total eleven thousand five hundred and twenty.”

“Things gather together after encountering one another; therefore, Gathering Together (Cui) follows. Cui means gathering. Gathering and moving upward is called Ascending (Sheng); therefore, Ascending follows.”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
書
皐陶拜手稽首颺言曰念哉率作興事慎
乃憲欽哉屢省乃成欽哉乃賡載歌曰
元首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉
百里賦納總二百里納銍三百里納秸服
四百里粟五百里米
次九曰嚮用五福
哲人惟刑無疆之辭屬于五極咸中有慶
詩
===
遡洄從之道阻且長遡游從之宛在水中
央
瞻彼洛矣維水泱泱君子至止福祿如茨
韎鞈有奭以作六師
或舂或揄或簸或蹂釋之叟叟烝之浮浮
載謀載惟取蕭祭脂取羝以軷載燔載
烈
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
春秋
punctuated:
書
皐陶拜手稽首，颺言曰：「念哉！率作興事，慎乃憲，欽哉！屢省乃成，欽哉！」乃賡載歌曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉！」
百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。
次九曰：「嚮用五福。」
哲人惟刑，無疆之辭，屬于五極，咸中有慶。
詩
遡洄從之，道阻且長；遡游從之，宛在水中央。
瞻彼洛矣，維水泱泱。君子至止，福祿如茨。韎鞈有奭，以作六師。
或舂或揄，或簸或蹂，釋之叟叟，烝之浮浮。載謀載惟，取蕭祭脂，取羝以軷，載燔載烈。
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。
春秋
translation_en:
Book of Documents
Gao Yao bowed with his hands together and knocked his head to the ground. Raising his voice, he said: “Be mindful! In leading undertakings and initiating affairs, be careful about your rules. Be reverent! Repeatedly examine your accomplishments. Be reverent!” Then he continued the song: “When the head is enlightened, the arms and legs are worthy, and all affairs prosper!”
Within the first hundred li, the tax is delivered as grain with its stalks; within the second hundred li, as ears of grain; within the third hundred li, as grain with its awns; within the fourth hundred li, as unhusked grain; and within the fifth hundred li, as husked grain.
The ninth is called “Enjoying the Five Blessings.”
Take the wise as your models. These words of inexhaustible meaning pertain to the five supreme standards; all who attain the mean will receive blessings.
Book of Odes
I follow that person upstream: the way is difficult and long. I follow that person downstream: there they seem to be, in the middle of the water.
Look at the Luo River, its waters vast and deep. The lord has arrived; blessings and emoluments crowd thick as thatch. His reddish leather knee-covers gleam as he rouses the Six Armies.
Some pound the grain, some scoop it out; some winnow it, some rub it clean. They wash it with a rustling sound and steam it, the vapour rising thickly. They deliberate and reflect; they take southernwood to offer with fat, and take a ram for the sacrifice to the road. They burn offerings and roast the flesh.
Follow and emulate the statutes of King Wen, daily bringing peace to the four quarters.
Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
春王正月〔隱公元年〕春公會戎于潜〔隱〕
〔公二年〕
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男

===
〔年〕
禮記
天子建天官先六大
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉
子曰恭近禮儉近仁信近情敬讓以行此
雖有過其不甚矣夫恭寡過情可信儉
易容也以此失之者不亦鮮乎
夫昔者君子比德於玉焉
第貳場
punctuated:
春，王正月。〔隱公元年〕春，公會戎于潜。〔隱〕〔公二年〕
夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
春，王二月壬子，宋華元帥師及鄭公子歸生帥師戰于大棘。〔宣公二年〕
季孫行父如晉。〔文公十有五年〕季孫行父如齊。〔宣公十年〕十有二月乙丑，季孫行父及晉郤犨盟于扈。〔成公十有六〕〔年〕
禮記
天子建天官，先六大。
流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
子曰：「恭近禮，儉近仁，信近情。敬讓以行此，雖有過，其不甚矣。夫恭寡過，情可信，儉易容也。以此失之者，不亦鮮乎？」
夫昔者君子比德於玉焉。
第貳場
translation_en:
In spring, the first month of the royal calendar. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕 In spring, the duke met with the Rong at Qian. 〔Second year of Duke Yin.〕
In summer, the duke met at Kuiqiu with the Duke of Zhou, the chief minister; the Marquis of Qi; the Viscount of Song; the Marquis of Wei; the Earl of Zheng; the Baron of Xu; and the Earl of Cao. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕
In spring, on the renzi day of the second month of the royal calendar, Hua Yuan of Song, commanding an army, fought at Daji against Prince Guisheng of Zheng, who also commanded an army. 〔Second year of Duke Xuan.〕
Jisun Xingfu went to Jin. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.〕 Jisun Xingfu went to Qi. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan.〕 In the twelfth month, on the yichou day, Jisun Xingfu and Xi Chou of Jin made a covenant at Hu. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
When the Son of Heaven establishes the offices of Heaven, he gives precedence to the six great officers.
They flow without ceasing, unite in harmony and bring about transformation; thus music arises.
The Master said: “Respectfulness approaches ritual propriety; frugality approaches benevolence; trustworthiness approaches sincerity. If one practices these with reverence and deference, any faults one commits will not be very serious. Respectfulness brings few faults; sincerity can be trusted; frugality makes one readily accepted. Are not those who go astray while practicing these few indeed?”
In ancient times, the gentleman found in jade an analogy for virtue.
Second Session

Discourse

Edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials [one topic from this category [?]]

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
策五道
問帝王治天下文以經之武以緯之陶唐
而降未之有改也攷之詩序所稱文王
作辟雝以譽髦武王臨鎬京而講學其
後宣王脩文武之業選徒蒐狩赫然稱
中興焉車攻吉日可攷而知也洪惟我
太祖
成祖文武聖神再造區夏學校之教兵戎之治
兼總百王矣
===
皇上纘承丕緒首
視太學進儒紳聽講頃者
嘉納輔臣之議
親御六飛
大閱萬甲章縫武弁懾目易心思以稱塞
上意未能也
聖學淵邃
神武昭宣所以振德弁髦飭勉將士載在
臨雍
punctuated:
策五道

問：帝王治天下，文以經之，武以緯之，陶唐而降，未之有改也。攷之《詩序》，所稱文王作辟雝以譽髦，武王臨鎬京而講學，其後宣王脩文武之業，選徒蒐狩，赫然稱中興焉。《車攻》《吉日》可攷而知也。洪惟我太祖、成祖，文武聖神，再造區夏，學校之教、兵戎之治，兼總百王矣。皇上纘承丕緒，首視太學，進儒紳聽講。頃者，嘉納輔臣之議，親御六飛，大閱萬甲。章縫武弁，懾目易心，思以稱塞上意，未能也。聖學淵邃，神武昭宣，所以振德弁髦、飭勉將士，載在臨雍
translation_en:
Five Policy Questions

Question: In governing All under Heaven, emperors and kings have used civil accomplishments as the warp and military strength as the weft. From Taotang onward, this has never changed. Examine the Prefaces to the Odes: they speak of King Wen constructing the Biyong academy to foster outstanding men, and King Wu coming to Haojing to hold lectures. Later, King Xuan continued the work of Kings Wen and Wu, selecting troops and conducting seasonal hunts, and won illustrious recognition for restoring the dynasty. This can be ascertained by examining “Chariot Attack” and “Auspicious Day.” We reverently reflect that our Taizu and Chengzu, accomplished in civil and military affairs, sagely and divinely discerning, reestablished the Chinese realm. In education through schools and the administration of military affairs, they united in themselves the achievements of a hundred kings.

His Majesty inherited this great undertaking and first visited the Imperial University, summoning Confucian scholars and officials to hear lectures. Recently, graciously accepting the counsel of his assisting ministers, he personally rode in the imperial carriage drawn by six horses and held a grand review of a myriad armored troops. Scholars in their pleated caps and officers in their military caps were awestruck by the sight and transformed in heart. They sought to fulfill His Majesty’s intentions but felt themselves unequal to the task. His Majesty’s sagely learning is profound, and his divine martial prowess shines forth. The means by which he nurtures the virtue of the students and admonishes and encourages commanders and soldiers are recorded in the account of the imperial visit to the Imperial University…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
大閱二錄首簡者可繹思而揚厲之歟夫太學
養士係關人才南北未靖計先勦撫爼
豆軍旅之事爾諸士宜究心者其備言
之以光賛
皇上謨烈之盛
問治天下者必先於端大本大本旣端則
天命人心攸繫皇圖固而國祚昌治道
可幾而理自古聖帝明王貽謀燕翼享
有道之長率由此也有周家法可攷而
===
知世子保傅諸篇章章具在三代而下
立法寖備互有得失亦可指而言與我
國朝創業垂統獨觀化原
太祖御極之初首建
大本堂延訪名儒以充輔導編輯
皇明祖訓垂裕後昆如嚴
命詹同申
敕李善長可謂萬世法程矣
成祖貽謨丕揚
punctuated:
《大閱》二錄首簡者，可繹思而揚厲之歟？夫太學養士，係關人才；南北未靖，計先勦撫。爼豆軍旅之事，爾諸士宜究心者，其備言之，以光賛皇上謨烈之盛。
問：治天下者，必先於端大本。大本旣端，則天命人心攸繫，皇圖固而國祚昌，治道可幾而理。自古聖帝明王，貽謀燕翼，享有道之長，率由此也。有周家法，可攷而知，《世子》《保傅》諸篇，章章具在。三代而下，立法寖備，互有得失，亦可指而言與？我國朝創業垂統，獨觀化原。太祖御極之初，首建大本堂，延訪名儒，以充輔導，編輯《皇明祖訓》，垂裕後昆。如嚴命詹同，申敕李善長，可謂萬世法程矣。成祖貽謨，丕揚
translation_en:
…and the Grand Review, as set forth at the beginning of these two records: might you ponder their meaning and further proclaim their significance? The Imperial University’s nurturing of scholars bears directly upon the cultivation of talent. With neither north nor south yet pacified, planning must give priority to suppression and conciliation. Matters of ritual vessels and military affairs are what you scholars should study attentively. Discuss them fully, thereby helping to glorify the grandeur of His Majesty’s plans and achievements.
Question: Those who govern All under Heaven must first set right the great foundation. Once this foundation is rightly established, Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts have that upon which to rest; the imperial dominion is secure and the dynasty’s fortunes flourish; orderly government may be attained [?]. Since antiquity, sage emperors and enlightened kings have left plans to secure their descendants’ welfare and long enjoyed possession of the Way: all have followed this principle. The house rules of Zhou can be examined and understood; the chapters “The Heir Apparent” (Shizi), “Protectors and Tutors” (Baofu), and others remain clearly extant. After the Three Dynasties, institutional provisions gradually became more comprehensive, with varying successes and failures. Can these, too, be identified and discussed? In founding its enterprise and transmitting its succession, our reigning dynasty discerned with exceptional insight the source of moral transformation. At the beginning of his reign, Taizu first established the Hall of the Great Foundation (Dabentang), invited and consulted renowned Confucian scholars to serve as advisers and instructors, and compiled the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming (Huang Ming Zuxun), bequeathing blessings to later descendants. His stern commands to Zhan Tong and reiterated injunctions to Li Shanchang may indeed be called standards for ten thousand generations. Chengzu bequeathed his plans and greatly exalted…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
休烈集成
文華寶鑑以
賜青宮如
勅學士楊榮
諭翰林胡廣惓惓以問學聖功爲本
二祖立訓盡善盡美迨我
列聖益隆繼述
宣宗則有
帝訓
===
憲宗則有
文華大訓
聖聖相承恪遵
成憲其詳可得聞與恭惟
皇上膺
天眷命早建
元良寰宇宣播捧誦
綸音
出閤伊邇海內顒顒嚮風忻覩
punctuated:
休烈，集成《文華寶鑑》，以賜青宮。如勅學士楊榮、諭翰林胡廣，惓惓以問學聖功爲本。二祖立訓，盡善盡美。迨我列聖，益隆繼述：宣宗則有《帝訓》，憲宗則有《文華大訓》。聖聖相承，恪遵成憲，其詳可得聞與？
恭惟皇上膺天眷命，早建元良，寰宇宣播，捧誦綸音。出閤伊邇，海內顒顒嚮風，忻覩
translation_en:
…glorious achievements, compiling the Precious Mirror of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua baojian) and bestowing it upon the crown prince. In such acts as his injunction to Academician Yang Rong and his instructions to Hanlin Academician Hu Guang, he earnestly made inquiry and learning—the work of attaining sagehood—the foundation. The instructions established by the two founding emperors were perfect in goodness and beauty. Our succeeding sage emperors further advanced the continuation of their legacy: Xuanzong produced the Imperial Instructions (Di xun), and Xianzong the Great Instructions of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua daxun). Sage emperor succeeded sage emperor, reverently observing the established precedents. May we hear the particulars?
We respectfully consider how His Majesty received Heaven’s gracious mandate and early designated an heir apparent. The announcement spread throughout the realm, and all reverently received and recited the imperial words. The crown prince’s departure from the inner palace is now near; throughout the realm, people eagerly look to his example and joyfully behold…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛典億萬年無疆之慶端在于此爰稽
列聖祕典瑶函載在
天府茂隆
聖學之傳固非臣子所能仰賛若乃輔翼訏謨
雖已詳而益致其詳不爲過也草茅芹
曝豈無懷忠欲獻可爲
青宮毓德萬一之助者乎其悉心以對將轉
而聞之於
上
===
問八卦九疇古聖人默契于天神明斯道
故作而闡之以垂世教其曰河出圖洛
出書聖人則之蓋有感於河洛之祥而
推明畫卦敘疇若天授焉後世惑其説
遂謂天實有以畀聖人紛紛拘泥有謂
龍馬出河遂以畫卦者有謂伏羲繼天
而王受河圖而畫八卦者有以七前六
後八左九右爲河圖之文者宋儒亦謂
圓者河圖之數羲文因之而造易第不
punctuated:
盛典，億萬年無疆之慶，端在于此。爰稽列聖祕典，瑶函載在天府，茂隆聖學之傳，固非臣子所能仰賛。若乃輔翼訏謨，雖已詳，而益致其詳，不爲過也。草茅芹曝，豈無懷忠欲獻，可爲青宮毓德萬一之助者乎？其悉心以對，將轉而聞之於上。

問：八卦九疇，古聖人默契于天，神明斯道，故作而闡之，以垂世教。其曰：「河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。」蓋有感於河洛之祥，而推明畫卦敘疇，若天授焉。後世惑其説，遂謂天實有以畀聖人，紛紛拘泥。有謂龍馬出河，遂以畫卦者；有謂伏羲繼天而王，受河圖而畫八卦者；有以七前六後、八左九右爲河圖之文者。宋儒亦謂圓者河圖之數，羲文因之而造易。第不
translation_en:
…this grand ceremony. The boundless blessings of countless ages have their very foundation here. Accordingly, we examine the treasured records of the successive sage emperors, preserved in precious cases in the imperial archives. The flourishing transmission of sagely learning is indeed beyond the capacity of subjects to praise adequately. As for the great plans for assisting and guiding the heir apparent, although already detailed, it would be no excess to make them still more thorough. Among scholars in humble circumstances, might there not be those who, moved by loyalty, wish to present their modest offerings—like celery or the warmth of the sun—and thereby contribute even the slightest assistance to nurturing the virtue of the crown prince? Answer with all your heart; your answers will be forwarded for the Emperor’s hearing.

Question: As for the Eight Trigrams and the Nine Categories, the ancient sages were in tacit accord with Heaven and possessed a spiritual understanding of this Way. Thus they created and elucidated them to hand down instruction to the world. The saying, “The Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing; the sages took them as models,” presumably means that, inspired by the auspicious signs of the Yellow and Luo Rivers, they developed and clarified their insights by drawing the trigrams and arranging the categories, as though instructed by Heaven. Later generations, misled by this account, consequently claimed that Heaven had actually bestowed something upon the sages, and became entangled in literal interpretations. Some said that a dragon-horse emerged from the Yellow River and that the trigrams were consequently drawn from it. Some said that Fuxi succeeded Heaven as sovereign, received the River Chart, and drew the Eight Trigrams. Some took seven in front, six behind, eight on the left, and nine on the right to be the markings of the River Chart. Song Confucian scholars also said that the circular arrangement represented the numbers of the River Chart, on which Fuxi and King Wen based their creation of the Book of Changes. Yet we do not…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
知聖人畫卦之初果如是規倣否乎有
謂神龜負文而遂成九類者有謂禹治
洪水賜洛書而陳九疇者有以九前一
後三左七右爲洛書之文者宋儒亦謂
方者洛書之文禹箕敘之而作範第不
知聖人敘疇之始果如是參合否乎且
易隨代異名夏曰歸藏殷曰連山周曰
周易視伏羲所作果有異歟世之傳圖
學者別爲二曰先天伏羲之易後天文
===
王之易旣規橫爲圓又塡圓爲方前列
六十四卦後列一百二十八卦不知上
古無言之敎果若是否也近世著日抄
者極論天地定位一章必非先天卦位
何所信而然歟洪範一書說者謂九疇
竝陳意義聯貫其大旨何謂休徵咎徵
天人感應常理世之傳五行者乃一一
取證遂流而爲災異之學然則念用之
言抑有不足盡信者歟近代儒者作皇
punctuated: 知聖人畫卦之初，果如是規倣否乎？有謂神龜負文而遂成九類者，有謂禹治洪水，賜洛書而陳九疇者，有以九前一後、三左七右爲洛書之文者。宋儒亦謂方者洛書之文，禹箕敘之而作範。第不知聖人敘疇之始，果如是參合否乎？且易隨代異名，夏曰歸藏，殷曰連山，周曰周易，視伏羲所作，果有異歟？世之傳圖學者，別爲二，曰先天伏羲之易、後天文王之易。旣規橫爲圓，又塡圓爲方，前列六十四卦，後列一百二十八卦，不知上古無言之敎，果若是否也？近世著日抄者，極論天地定位一章必非先天卦位，何所信而然歟？洪範一書，說者謂九疇竝陳，意義聯貫，其大旨何謂？休徵咎徵，天人感應常理，世之傳五行者，乃一一取證，遂流而爲災異之學。然則念用之言，抑有不足盡信者歟？近代儒者作皇
translation_en: …know whether, when the sage first drew the trigrams, he really modeled them in this way? Some say that a divine tortoise bore markings on its back and that the nine categories were thereby completed; some say that when Yu controlled the flood, he was granted the Luo Writing and set forth the nine divisions; and some identify the markings of the Luo Writing as nine in front, one behind, three on the left, and seven on the right. Song Confucians likewise said that the square arrangement was the pattern of the Luo Writing, which Yu and Jizi ordered to produce the Great Plan. Yet we do not know whether, when the sages first arranged the nine divisions, they really combined and correlated them in this way. Moreover, the Changes had different names in successive dynasties: in the Xia it was called Return to the Hidden (Guicang), in the Yin, Linked Mountains (Lianshan) [the usual dynastic attributions are reversed here], and in the Zhou, the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi). Were these actually different from what Fuxi produced? Those who transmit the study of diagrams distinguish two forms: the Earlier Heaven Changes of Fuxi and the Later Heaven Changes of King Wen. They turn a horizontal arrangement into a circle, then fill out the circle into a square, displaying sixty-four hexagrams first and one hundred and twenty-eight afterward. We do not know whether the wordless teaching of high antiquity was really like this. A recent author of Daily Notes (Richao) argues emphatically that the passage beginning “Heaven and earth establish their positions” certainly does not describe the Earlier Heaven positions of the trigrams. On what grounds does he hold this conviction? Commentators on the Great Plan say that its nine divisions are set forth together and linked in meaning. What is its central purport? Auspicious and baleful signs belong to the regular principle of mutual response between Heaven and humankind. Yet those who transmit the teachings of the Five Phases seek corroboration in each individual case, thereby drifting into the study of disasters and anomalies. Does this mean that the injunction to “attend to and employ” contains something that should not be entirely trusted? A Confucian scholar of recent times composed the Huang…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
極內篇謂得洪範不傳之數然歟否歟
凡此皆經學大旨諸士明經有素盍詳
說之
問生民之休戚係吏治之臧否吏治不修
古道難復三代而上治出於一降自叔
世有賢知者出於其間則各以其才能
之相近隨世以就功名良足嘉尚未可
枚舉然有循良異稱者如治東阿而政
道易行治蜀郡而化行俗美遷南陽則
===
出入阡陌遷北海則反歸桐鄉或以良
舉或以循名古今稱循良者常互言之
之數吏者果有異同否又有廉能異稱
者如守會稽而却百錢守上洛而還騶
犢投巫漳水則鄴郡震驚捕吏美陽則
吏民慴服或以廉著或以能名古今稱
廉能者常對舉之之數吏者果有優劣
否自古求治者未嘗借才異代何善類
之稱盛也今時則不然收錄愈廣考核
punctuated:
極內篇》，謂得《洪範》不傳之數，然歟？否歟？凡此皆經學大旨，諸士明經有素，盍詳說之？

問：生民之休戚，係吏治之臧否。吏治不修，古道難復。三代而上，治出於一；降自叔世，有賢知者出於其間，則各以其才能之相近，隨世以就功名，良足嘉尚，未可枚舉。然有循良異稱者，如治東阿而政道易行，治蜀郡而化行俗美，遷南陽則出入阡陌，遷北海則反歸桐鄉，或以良舉，或以循名。古今稱循良者，常互言之。之數吏者，果有異同否？又有廉能異稱者，如守會稽而却百錢，守上洛而還騶犢，投巫漳水則鄴郡震驚，捕吏美陽則吏民慴服，或以廉著，或以能名。古今稱廉能者，常對舉之。之數吏者，果有優劣否？自古求治者，未嘗借才異代，何善類之稱盛也！今時則不然，收錄愈廣，考核
translation_en:
…Inner Chapters on the August Ultimate, claiming to have recovered the numerical principles of the Great Plan that had ceased to be transmitted. Is this so, or not? All these matters concern the central principles of classical learning. You gentlemen have long studied the classics: why not explain them in detail?

Question: The well-being and suffering of the people depend upon the quality of local administration. Unless administration is put in order, the ancient Way can hardly be restored. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, government proceeded from a unified source. In the declining ages thereafter, worthy and wise men appeared from time to time, each adapting to his age and achieving distinction through work suited to his talents. Such men certainly deserve admiration; they are too numerous to enumerate individually. Yet some are distinguished by the different designations “dutiful” (xun) and “benevolent” (liang). One governed Dong’e, where the principles of government were readily put into practice; another governed Shu Commandery, where his transforming influence spread and customs improved. One, transferred to Nanyang, went about among the field paths; another, transferred to Beihai, returned to Tongxiang [?]. Some were recommended as benevolent, others became known as dutiful. From antiquity to the present, those praising dutiful and benevolent officials have regularly used these terms interchangeably. Were these several officials [?] actually different or alike?

There are also the distinct designations “incorruptible” and “capable.” One, serving as governor of Kuaiji, refused a hundred cash; another, governing Shangluo, returned an attendant’s calf [?]. When one cast the shamans into the Zhang River, Ye Commandery was shaken; when another arrested an official at Meiyang, officials and commoners alike submitted in fear. Some were renowned for integrity, others for ability. From antiquity to the present, those praising integrity and ability have regularly paired the terms. Were these several officials [?] actually superior or inferior to one another? Since ancient times, those seeking good government have never borrowed talent from another age. How abundant were those acclaimed as worthy! Today, however, things are otherwise: recruitment grows ever broader, and scrutiny of performance…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
愈精而吏治愈不古若銓衡掄選之外
復有明揚彙薦之條誠收錄廣矣夫擇
官不擇人朋昵者競奔走焉積薪臥治
政拙催科寧無遺憾乎玆欲搜羅眞才
野罔攸伏其何道以致之三載大計之
外復有不時黜陟之典誠考核精矣夫
採名不採實智巧者爭速化焉損名郡
治擅誅掾吏寧無過舉乎玆欲考憑政
績朝無倖位其何術以致之夫吏治脩
===
而後民生遂民生遂而後理道隆轉移
風動之機自有端本澄源者在諸生學
古入官行將膺民社之司以觀
盛治願詳著其繇
問儒者抱藝求自見于世其於當時之務
未有不究心者試舉江藩一二最急者
與諸士商之夫屯田以稟軍制也今江
藩屯粒無慮八萬有奇然名存實亡者
近半議者欲一清覈其敝而或謂滋擾
punctuated:
愈精，而吏治愈不古若。銓衡掄選之外，復有明揚彙薦之條，誠收錄廣矣。夫擇官不擇人，朋昵者競奔走焉。積薪臥治，政拙催科，寧無遺憾乎？玆欲搜羅眞才，野罔攸伏，其何道以致之？三載大計之外，復有不時黜陟之典，誠考核精矣。夫採名不採實，智巧者爭速化焉。損名郡治，擅誅掾吏，寧無過舉乎？玆欲考憑政績，朝無倖位，其何術以致之？夫吏治脩而後民生遂，民生遂而後理道隆。轉移風動之機，自有端本澄源者在。諸生學古入官，行將膺民社之司，以觀盛治，願詳著其繇。

問：儒者抱藝求自見于世，其於當時之務，未有不究心者。試舉江藩一二最急者，與諸士商之。夫屯田以稟軍，制也。今江藩屯粒，無慮八萬有奇，然名存實亡者近半。議者欲一清覈其敝，而或謂滋擾。
translation_en:
…more exacting, yet the administration of officials falls ever further short of antiquity. Besides selection through the regular personnel procedures, there are provisions for publicly advancing worthy men and recommending them collectively: recruitment is indeed extensive. Yet when offices rather than individuals determine selection, those with friends and intimate connections compete to secure advancement. Worthy men are left beneath the pile of firewood, though capable of governing while reclining; others govern well but are inept at collecting taxes [?]. Can there be no cause for regret? If we now wish to seek out true talent, leaving none hidden outside official service, by what means can we accomplish this? Beyond the triennial Grand Review, there are also provisions for demotion and promotion at irregular intervals: scrutiny is indeed exacting. Yet when reputation rather than actual performance is taken into account, the cunning compete to transform their fortunes rapidly. Men lose their reputations through commandery administration, or execute subordinate functionaries without authorization [?]. Can there be no mistaken actions? If we now wish to base evaluations on administrative achievements, so that no one at court holds office through undeserved good fortune, by what method can we accomplish this?

Only when official administration is well ordered can the people secure their livelihoods; only when their livelihoods are secure can good government flourish. The means of bringing about change and moving people as the wind moves grass necessarily lie in rectifying the root and clearing the source. You students study antiquity in preparation for entering office and will soon assume responsibility for the people and their local altars of soil and grain, thereby displaying the flourishing governance of our age. Please set out in detail how this may be achieved.

Question: Confucian scholars possess cultivated learning and seek to make themselves known in the world. None fail to give careful thought to the affairs of their own time. Let us raise one or two of the most urgent matters in Jiangxi for discussion with you gentlemen. Agricultural colonies were established to provision the troops: this is the prescribed system. Today, the grain revenue from these colonies in Jiangxi amounts in all to more than eighty thousand, yet nearly half exists in name alone, with nothing actually forthcoming. Those discussing the matter wish to undertake a thorough audit of these abuses, while others say that this would cause harassment…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不則軍民俱困而聽其乾沒非法也古
有新墾代北閑屯得田三千八百餘里
者茲欲一覈故額輒尼不行何歟隄防
以利農制也今列郡陂塘不下數萬餘
處然旋脩旋壅者頗仍議者謂專責成
其人又慮應空文不則膏腴盡汙而委
諸湮塞非利也古有觀察江西築隄溉
田萬有二千頃者茲乃屢飭脩築竟鮮
實效何歟水旱災傷民無菜色以儲蓄
===
豫也邇積穀之令以殿最課長吏嚴矣
至歲稽積數曾不及例限之半吏民且
告病焉茲欲使郡邑之粟各足賑恤不
盡取責于贖鍰法將安在昔有不俟有
司請白而先奏行有擇公正察災傷而
易守宰者不識有足採者歟鄉遂丘甸
皆有甲兵故姦宄息也邇保甲之法以
功過程捕吏密矣顧鼠伏乘間尚不無
藪澤之逋士庶恒中怛焉茲欲俾環堵
punctuated: 不則軍民俱困，而聽其乾沒，非法也。古有新墾代北閑屯，得田三千八百餘里者，茲欲一覈故額，輒尼不行，何歟？隄防以利農，制也。今列郡陂塘不下數萬餘處，然旋脩旋壅者頗仍。議者謂專責成其人，又慮應空文；不則膏腴盡汙，而委諸湮塞，非利也。古有觀察江西，築隄溉田萬有二千頃者，茲乃屢飭脩築，竟鮮實效，何歟？水旱災傷，民無菜色，以儲蓄豫也。邇積穀之令，以殿最課長吏，嚴矣。至歲稽積數，曾不及例限之半，吏民且告病焉。茲欲使郡邑之粟各足賑恤，不盡取責于贖鍰，法將安在？昔有不俟有司請白而先奏行，有擇公正察災傷而易守宰者，不識有足採者歟？鄉遂丘甸皆有甲兵，故姦宄息也。邇保甲之法，以功過程捕吏，密矣。顧鼠伏乘間，尚不無藪澤之逋，士庶恒中怛焉。茲欲俾環堵
translation_en:
…Otherwise, soldiers and commoners alike are reduced to hardship; yet to allow these resources to be misappropriated is contrary to proper regulation. In antiquity, there was someone who newly reclaimed idle military-colony land in Daibei, obtaining more than 3,800 li of farmland. Now, when we wish merely to audit the original quota, the effort is invariably obstructed and never carried out. Why is this?

Dikes were instituted to benefit agriculture. In the prefectures today, there are no fewer than tens of thousands of ponds and reservoirs, yet repeated silting immediately after repair is quite common. Some propose holding designated individuals fully responsible for completing the work, but others fear that this will produce only compliance on paper. Otherwise, fertile land becomes entirely waterlogged; yet to abandon these works to silting and blockage brings no benefit. In antiquity, there was someone who, while serving as Surveillance Commissioner in Jiangxi, built dikes that irrigated 12,000 qing of farmland. Now, despite repeated orders for repairs and construction, there are scarcely any tangible results. Why is this?

When floods and droughts caused devastation, the people showed no signs of hunger because stores had been laid up beforehand. Recent orders to accumulate grain are stringent, grading senior local officials as inferior or superior according to their performance. Yet when the accumulated quantities are audited annually, they do not reach even half the prescribed amount, and officials and commoners alike complain of hardship. If we now wish the grain held in each prefecture and county to suffice for relief, without relying entirely on payments made to redeem punishments, what method should we use? In the past, some submitted memorials and took action without waiting for the responsible authorities to report and request approval; others selected impartial men to investigate disaster damage and replaced prefects and county magistrates. Might any of these precedents be worth adopting?

The ancient territorial units—the xiang, sui, qiu, and dian—all maintained armed forces; thus wrongdoing and disorder ceased. The recent baojia system of mutual household responsibility is meticulous in assessing arresting officers according to their merits and faults. Yet fugitives still lurk in marshes and wilds, hiding like rats and exploiting opportunities, and gentlemen and commoners remain inwardly fearful. If we now wish to make those dwelling within humble walls…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之衆互相聯比不待督責于所司義將
安出昔有尚招徠而爲理絲之喻有專
摘發而設鉤鉅之術者不識可竝行者
歟凡此皆諸士抱先憂之志必有槩於
中矣試各攄所見當事者固願聞也
punctuated: 之衆互相聯比，不待督責于所司，義將安出？昔有尚招徠而爲理絲之喻，有專摘發而設鉤鉅之術者，不識可竝行者歟？凡此，皆諸士抱先憂之志，必有槩於中矣。試各攄所見，當事者固願聞也。
translation_en: …the inhabitants to link themselves together in mutual association without waiting for supervision and demands from the responsible authorities: by what principle might this be achieved? In former times, some favored drawing people in, using the analogy of untangling silk; others concentrated on uncovering wrongdoing, devising techniques of probing and entrapment [?]. Might these approaches be practiced together? On all these matters, you gentlemen, who cherish the resolve to take concern before others do, must surely have reflections in your hearts. Let each of you set forth his views; those responsible for these affairs are indeed eager to hear them.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰我未見好仁者惡不仁者好仁者無
以尚之惡不仁者其爲仁矣不使不仁
者加乎其身有能一日用其力於仁矣
乎我未見力不足者蓋有之矣我未之
見也
孫希夔
同考試官教諭廖批講好仁惡不仁親切有味
===
必能用力於爲仁者
考試官學正吳批認理真切敷詞典實發夫
子反覆望人之意殆盡可式
考試官教授顧批明暢典雅是文之足式者
宜冠多士
聖人以仁望天下而深責其爲之不力焉夫仁
本心德而爲之不外乎好惡也一用力焉而仁
在我矣人亦何憚而不爲哉夫子所以嘆其未
見而反覆以致望也若曰純乎理而爲人心之
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「我未見好仁者、惡不仁者。好仁者，無以尚之；惡不仁者，其爲仁矣，不使不仁者加乎其身。有能一日用其力於仁矣乎？我未見力不足者。蓋有之矣，我未之見也。」
孫希夔
同考試官教諭廖批：講好仁、惡不仁，親切有味，必能用力於爲仁者。
考試官學正吳批：認理真切，敷詞典實，發夫子反覆望人之意殆盡，可式。
考試官教授顧批：明暢典雅，是文之足式者，宜冠多士。
聖人以仁望天下，而深責其爲之不力焉。夫仁本心德，而爲之不外乎好惡也。一用力焉，而仁在我矣，人亦何憚而不爲哉？夫子所以嘆其未見，而反覆以致望也。若曰：純乎理而爲人心之
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
The Master said: “I have never seen anyone who loves benevolence or hates what is not benevolent. One who loves benevolence places nothing above it. One who hates what is not benevolent practices benevolence by allowing nothing unbenevolent to affect his person. Is there anyone who can devote his strength to benevolence for a single day? I have never seen anyone whose strength was insufficient. There may be such a person, but I have never seen him.”
Sun Xikui
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “His discussion of loving benevolence and hating what is not benevolent is intimate and full of savor. He must be someone capable of exerting himself in the practice of benevolence.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Director: “His grasp of principle is true and precise, and his language is classical and substantial. He brings out almost fully the Master’s repeatedly expressed hopes for others. This may serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: “Clear, fluent, classical, and elegant: this essay is worthy to serve as a model and should rank first among the candidates.”
The sage hopes that all under Heaven will attain benevolence and sternly reproaches them for their lack of effort in practicing it. Benevolence is fundamentally the virtue of the mind, and its practice consists simply in what one loves and hates. Once one exerts oneself in this, benevolence lies within oneself. What, then, should people fear that would keep them from practicing it? This is why the Master laments that he has never seen such a person and repeatedly expresses his hopes. title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
公者是仁也拂乎理而為人欲之私者是不仁
也於此而用力於好惡焉則仁矣何今之好仁
惡不仁者我未之見乎夫所謂好仁者非徒好
之已也所好惟仁而凡物之可以易吾心者皆
無得以尚焉斯為天下之真好矣所謂惡不仁
者非徒惡之已也所為在仁而凡事之可以累
吾仁者不使加乎身焉斯為天下之真惡矣是
謂成德之事而吾之所未見者此也然是仁也
非由於外鑠也本之為吾心之實德非假於外
===
求也體之為吾心之實功人但不為耳有能一
日之間知仁之可好而用力以好之則仁本固
有一擴充焉足矣未見其不足於好也知不仁
之可惡而用力以惡之則不仁本無一克治焉
足矣未見其不足於惡也蓋雖天之賦質不齊
而分量所拘容有不能充其所好者矣就我所
見而言實未嘗好之焉耳豈有心誠好之而力
不足繼者哉人之受材不一而精神所限容有
不能充其所惡者矣就我所見而言實未嘗惡
punctuated: 公者，是仁也；拂乎理而為人欲之私者，是不仁也。於此而用力於好惡焉，則仁矣。何今之好仁惡不仁者，我未之見乎？夫所謂好仁者，非徒好之已也，所好惟仁，而凡物之可以易吾心者，皆無得以尚焉，斯為天下之真好矣。所謂惡不仁者，非徒惡之已也，所為在仁，而凡事之可以累吾仁者，不使加乎身焉，斯為天下之真惡矣。是謂成德之事，而吾之所未見者此也。然是仁也，非由於外鑠也，本之為吾心之實德；非假於外求也，體之為吾心之實功。人但不為耳。有能一日之間，知仁之可好而用力以好之，則仁本固有，一擴充焉足矣，未見其不足於好也；知不仁之可惡而用力以惡之，則不仁本無，一克治焉足矣，未見其不足於惡也。蓋雖天之賦質不齊，而分量所拘，容有不能充其所好者矣，就我所見而言，實未嘗好之焉耳，豈有心誠好之而力不足繼者哉？人之受材不一，而精神所限，容有不能充其所惡者矣，就我所見而言，實未嘗惡
translation_en: …the impartiality of the human heart: this is benevolence. What runs counter to principle and constitutes the selfishness of human desires is lack of benevolence. If one exerts oneself in loving and hating accordingly, one will attain benevolence. Why, then, have I yet to see anyone today who loves benevolence or hates its absence? What is meant by loving benevolence is not merely loving it: one loves benevolence alone, allowing nothing capable of diverting one’s heart to rank above it. This is true love in the world. What is meant by hating the absence of benevolence is not merely hating it: one’s actions aim at benevolence, and one allows nothing that might impair one’s benevolence to affect one’s person. This is true hatred in the world. Such is the work of perfected virtue, and this is what I have yet to see. Yet this benevolence is not infused into us from outside: in its root it is the true virtue of our own hearts. Nor does it depend on seeking outside ourselves: embodying it is the true work of our own hearts. People simply fail to undertake it. If anyone could, for a single day, recognize that benevolence deserves love and exert himself in loving it, then, since benevolence is inherently present, all that would be needed is to extend and develop it. I have never seen anyone whose strength was insufficient to love it. If anyone recognizes that lack of benevolence deserves hatred and exerts himself in hating it, then, since it is inherently absent, all that would be needed is to overcome and eliminate it. I have never seen anyone whose strength was insufficient to hate it. Although Heaven endows people with unequal constitutions, and the constraints of their capacities might conceivably prevent some from fully realizing what they love, in my experience they have simply never loved it. How could anyone sincerely love it in his heart yet lack the strength to sustain that love? People receive differing endowments, and the limits of their mental energies might conceivably prevent some from fully realizing their hatred of what they hate. Yet in my experience they have simply never hated…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之焉耳豈有心誠惡之而力不足副者哉是知
仁非易也自奮焉則易矣仁非難也自諉焉則
難矣夫子反覆以慨嘆之也其望於天下者深
乎雖然求仁未易言也心齋坐忘庶幾三月不
違矣自顏而外篤信者見悅于紛華穎悟者游
心於高遠此其不免于日月之至也然其機始
于一念而其功在于不欺故孟子之論仁必歸
之求放心而大學之論好惡必先于慎獨學者
合而觀之始得
===
天地之道可一言而盡也
萬國欽
同考試官教諭唐 批 詞約而意盡中庸義無如
此篇
同考試官教諭鄭 批 明暢精確無一浮泛語宜
錄
考試官學正吳 批 順暢
考試官教授顧 批 明爽
善言造化者該於至約而至誠可知矣甚矣造
punctuated:
之焉耳，豈有心誠惡之而力不足副者哉？是知仁非易也，自奮焉則易矣；仁非難也，自諉焉則難矣。夫子反覆以慨嘆之也，其望於天下者深乎！雖然，求仁未易言也。心齋坐忘，庶幾三月不違矣。自顏而外，篤信者見悅于紛華，穎悟者游心於高遠，此其不免于日月之至也。然其機始于一念，而其功在于不欺。故孟子之論仁，必歸之求放心；而大學之論好惡，必先于慎獨。學者合而觀之，始得。

天地之道，可一言而盡也。
萬國欽
同考試官教諭唐批：「詞約而意盡，中庸義無如此篇。」
同考試官教諭鄭批：「明暢精確，無一浮泛語，宜錄。」
考試官學正吳批：「順暢。」
考試官教授顧批：「明爽。」

善言造化者，該於至約，而至誠可知矣。甚矣，造
translation_en:
…it, that is all. How could anyone sincerely hate it in his heart yet lack the strength to match that hatred? Thus we know that benevolence is not easy, yet becomes easy if one rouses oneself to pursue it; benevolence is not difficult, yet becomes difficult if one makes excuses for oneself. The Master repeatedly lamented this: how profound were his hopes for all under Heaven! Nevertheless, seeking benevolence is no simple matter to discuss. Through fasting of the mind and sitting in forgetfulness, one might approach the state of not departing from benevolence for three months. Apart from Yan Hui, those of firm conviction find themselves captivated by worldly splendor, while those of keen understanding let their minds wander among lofty abstractions. Hence they inevitably attain benevolence only for a day or a month at a time. Yet the impulse begins in a single thought, and accomplishment lies in not deceiving oneself. Thus Mencius, in discussing benevolence, invariably returns to recovering the lost mind; and the Great Learning, in discussing liking and disliking, necessarily gives priority to vigilance when alone. Only by considering these together can students attain understanding.

“The Way of Heaven and Earth can be fully expressed in a single word.”
Wan Guoqin
Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: “Concise in wording yet complete in meaning. No essay on the Doctrine of the Mean equals this one.”
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Clear, fluent, refined, and precise, without a single vague or superficial expression. It should be included in the record.”
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Smooth and fluent.”
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: “Clear and lucid.”

Those who speak well of creation and transformation encompass it with the utmost brevity, and thereby perfect sincerity can be understood. Vast indeed is creation…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
化之大也而其道可盡于一言則至誠之合德
不可以識其微哉中庸以此言天道也若曰大
哉至誠之道固上下與天地同流矣然豈無所
本哉觀天地則知至誠也夫天覆物而成之固
浩乎不可窮矣然必有主宰之眞爲覆物之原
而所以爲天者在也地載物而成之固廓乎不
可極矣然必有綱維之實爲載物之基而所以
爲地者在也涵於沖漠無朕之表非必極其形
容而後能洩天之精也得其要而乾元之至理
===
可推寓于廣博無垠之中非必盡其擬議而後
能發地之蘊也執其樞而坤元之能事可畢雖
兩儀對待高下有散殊之迹而要之萬殊者其
一本者也由其一本者言之而健順之大德盡
于是矣雖二氣流行動靜有所乘之機而要之
兩在者其合一者也卽其合一者言之而易簡
之妙用盡于此矣是天地未判而道之以清以
寧者固已寓于無言之中天地旣分而道之司
覆司載者實不出乎一言之外善言天地者當
punctuated: 化之大也！而其道可盡于一言，則至誠之合德，不可以識其微哉？中庸以此言天道也，若曰：「大哉，至誠之道！固上下與天地同流矣，然豈無所本哉？觀天地則知至誠也。夫天覆物而成之，固浩乎不可窮矣；然必有主宰之眞爲覆物之原，而所以爲天者在也。地載物而成之，固廓乎不可極矣；然必有綱維之實爲載物之基，而所以爲地者在也。涵於沖漠無朕之表，非必極其形容而後能洩天之精也；得其要，而乾元之至理可推。寓于廣博無垠之中，非必盡其擬議而後能發地之蘊也；執其樞，而坤元之能事可畢。雖兩儀對待，高下有散殊之迹，而要之，萬殊者其一本者也；由其一本者言之，而健順之大德盡于是矣。雖二氣流行，動靜有所乘之機，而要之，兩在者其合一者也；卽其合一者言之，而易簡之妙用盡于此矣。是天地未判，而道之以清以寧者，固已寓于無言之中；天地旣分，而道之司覆司載者，實不出乎一言之外。善言天地者當
translation_en: …vast is the work of transformation! Yet its Way can be fully expressed in a single word. Can we not, then, discern the subtlety of how utmost sincerity accords with its virtue? The Doctrine of the Mean speaks here of the Way of Heaven, as if to say: “Great indeed is the Way of utmost sincerity! Above and below, it flows together with Heaven and Earth. Yet could it lack a foundation? By observing Heaven and Earth, we come to understand utmost sincerity. Heaven covers things and brings them to completion: its vastness is indeed inexhaustible. Yet there must be a governing truth that is the source of its covering things; therein lies what makes it Heaven. Earth bears things and brings them to completion: its breadth is indeed boundless. Yet there must be a sustaining reality that is the foundation of its bearing things; therein lies what makes it Earth. Enfolded in the realm of empty stillness without perceptible trace, Heaven’s essence need not be revealed only after its forms have been exhaustively described. Grasp its essential point, and the ultimate principle of Qian, the creative origin, can be inferred. Lodged within a breadth without bounds, Earth’s hidden riches need not be disclosed only after every comparison and deliberation has been exhausted. Grasp its pivot, and the capacities of Kun, the receptive origin, can be fully comprehended. Although the Two Modes, Heaven and Earth, stand opposite each other, displaying distinct manifestations above and below, in essence their myriad differences have a single root. Speaking from the standpoint of that single root, the great virtues of strength and compliance are fully encompassed here. Although the two vital forces circulate, with movement and stillness each having the impulse on which it proceeds, in essence what exists in two is united as one. Speaking from the standpoint of their unity, the wondrous workings of ease and simplicity are fully encompassed here. Thus, before Heaven and Earth had separated, the Way by which one becomes clear and the other tranquil was already lodged within the wordless. After Heaven and Earth had divided, the Way governing their covering and bearing of things truly remained within the compass of a single word. Those who speak well of Heaven and Earth ought to…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
知所本矣一言者何曰誠也誠之時義大矣哉
至誠所以配天地而垂無疆之業者可例知矣
抑斯言也子思得統於聖而聖人之得統于天
者何也道原天地太極渾淪何至一也運而五
行化而萬物斯二之矣而一者未漓也聖人與
天合德爲精一爲一貫闡太乙之精而立道統
治統之原者萬古一心焉耳吾獨怪乎天下之
道一而後世之多支離也噫
人皆可以爲堯舜有諸孟子曰然
萬邦獻
同考試官教諭陳批詞意簡古文氣悠揚非苟
作者取之
同考試官教諭陳批諸士講問答處類襲下文
此篇說理明盡詞復醇雅邃養之士也允宜高薦
考試官學正吳批精確
考試官教授顧批得旨
時人疑希聖之言而大賢因信之也甚矣聖人
與人同也堯舜可學理則然耳夫何疑哉昔孟
punctuated:
知所本矣。一言者何？曰誠也。誠之時義大矣哉！至誠所以配天地而垂無疆之業者，可例知矣。抑斯言也，子思得統於聖，而聖人之得統于天者何也？道原天地，太極渾淪，何至一也！運而五行，化而萬物，斯二之矣，而一者未漓也。聖人與天合德，爲精一，爲一貫，闡太乙之精而立道統、治統之原者，萬古一心焉耳。吾獨怪乎天下之道一，而後世之多支離也。噫！
人皆可以爲堯舜，有諸？孟子曰：「然。」
萬邦獻
同考試官教諭陳批：「詞意簡古，文氣悠揚，非苟作者，取之。」
同考試官教諭陳批：「諸士講問答處，類襲下文。此篇說理明盡，詞復醇雅，邃養之士也，允宜高薦。」
考試官學正吳批：「精確。」
考試官教授顧批：「得旨。」
時人疑希聖之言，而大賢因信之也。甚矣，聖人與人同也！堯舜可學，理則然耳，夫何疑哉？昔孟
translation_en:
…should understand its foundation. What is this one word? It is sincerity. Great indeed is the significance of sincerity in its proper time! By analogy, one may understand how utmost sincerity matches Heaven and Earth and establishes an enduring achievement without limit. Yet concerning this saying: Zisi received the succession from the sage; how, then, did the sage receive the succession from Heaven? The Way has its source in Heaven and Earth. The Supreme Ultimate, undifferentiated and whole—how perfectly one it is! In its movement it becomes the Five Phases; through transformation it becomes the myriad things. Thus it becomes two, yet its unity remains undispersed. The sages unite their virtue with Heaven, keeping their minds refined and single, threading all things together with one principle. In revealing the essence of the Great Unity and establishing the source of the succession of the Way and of governance, theirs is but one mind throughout the ages. What I find strange is that the Way throughout the world is one, yet later generations have fragmented it so greatly. Alas!
“Everyone can become a Yao or a Shun—is this so?” Mengzi said: “It is.”
Wan Bangxian
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The wording and ideas are spare and antique; the flow of the prose is expansive and graceful. This is no careless composition. Accept it.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “When expounding the question and answer, the candidates generally borrow from the text that follows. This essay explains the principles clearly and fully, and its language is also pure and elegant. Its author is a man of profound cultivation and truly deserves a high recommendation.”
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: “Precise and sound.”
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: “Grasps the essential meaning.”
People of the time doubted the assertion that one could aspire to sagehood, and the great worthy therefore affirmed it. How completely the sages share what is common to all people! That Yao and Shun can be emulated is simply what principle dictates. What cause is there for doubt? Formerly, Meng…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
子言必稱堯舜當時未之信也故曹交問之曰
天下之事有能有不能而吾人之分有及有不
及人皆可以為堯舜交嘗聞其語矣夫堯舜開
道之先其得天也獨厚立人之極其為聖也獨
隆人固有仰之無能名為之弗可及矣今不徒
曰可為而曰人皆可為信斯言也是以堯舜非
絶德也而媲美乎前脩者無分於聖凡之别為
堯舜非難事也而比隆乎往聖者不限於古今
之殊不識此語誠然乎哉交之為問蓋未敢信
===
其言之易而深疑其為之難也孟子據理以答
之曰然意以天下無不可為之事聖人無不可
至之理堯舜何以異於人哉特人視之為不可
為耳孰知堯之所已能固天下之可與能也而
謂皆可為堯者誠非無稽以立論舜之所優為
固天下之所能為也而謂皆可為舜者誠非大
言以誣人聖凡之分雖不同矣而其歸同焉堯
何人也舜何人也蓋不必賢智其人而凡我同
類者均之可入於聖人之域矣此其言之有足
punctuated:
子言必稱堯舜，當時未之信也。故曹交問之曰：「天下之事，有能有不能；而吾人之分，有及有不及。人皆可以為堯舜，交嘗聞其語矣。夫堯舜開道之先，其得天也獨厚；立人之極，其為聖也獨隆。人固有仰之無能名，為之弗可及矣。今不徒曰可為，而曰人皆可為。信斯言也，是以堯舜非絶德也，而媲美乎前脩者，無分於聖凡之别；為堯舜非難事也，而比隆乎往聖者，不限於古今之殊。不識此語誠然乎哉？」交之為問，蓋未敢信其言之易，而深疑其為之難也。
孟子據理以答之曰：「然。」意以天下無不可為之事，聖人無不可至之理。堯舜何以異於人哉？特人視之為不可為耳。孰知堯之所已能，固天下之可與能也，而謂皆可為堯者，誠非無稽以立論；舜之所優為，固天下之所能為也，而謂皆可為舜者，誠非大言以誣人。聖凡之分雖不同矣，而其歸同焉。堯何人也？舜何人也？蓋不必賢智其人，而凡我同類者，均之可入於聖人之域矣。此其言之有足
translation_en:
…Mencius invariably invoked Yao and Shun when he spoke, but people of his time did not believe him. Thus Cao Jiao asked him: “Among the affairs of the world, some things can be accomplished and others cannot; within our human capacities, some things lie within reach and others beyond it. I have heard the saying that everyone can become a Yao or a Shun. Now Yao and Shun were the first to open the Way, and their endowment from Heaven was exceptionally rich; they established the highest standard for humanity, and their sagehood was exceptionally exalted. People have indeed looked up to them without being able to find words to describe them, and striven to emulate them without being able to reach their level. Yet now you say not merely that one can become like them, but that everyone can. If these words are true, then Yao and Shun possessed no virtue beyond all others: those who equal the excellence of these earlier worthies are not divided by the distinction between sage and ordinary person. Becoming a Yao or a Shun is no difficult matter: those who match the greatness of the sages of the past are not constrained by the difference between antiquity and the present. I wonder, is this saying really true?” In asking this, Cao Jiao did not dare believe that it was as easy as the words suggested, and deeply doubted it because of the difficulty of putting it into practice.
Mencius answered on the basis of principle: “Yes.” His meaning was that there is nothing in the world that cannot be accomplished, and no principle embodied in a sage that others cannot attain. How were Yao and Shun different from other people? It is only that people regard becoming like them as impossible. Who recognizes that what Yao was able to accomplish is precisely what everyone in the world can share in accomplishing? To say that everyone can become a Yao is certainly not to advance an unfounded argument. What Shun excelled in doing is precisely what everyone in the world is capable of doing; to say that everyone can become a Shun is certainly not to deceive people with extravagant claims. Though sages and ordinary people differ in their standing, the ultimate attainment open to them is the same. What sort of person was Yao? What sort of person was Shun? One need not be an exceptionally worthy or wise person: all who belong to our human kind can equally enter the realm of the sages. Thus there are sufficient grounds for his words to…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
信者而豈欺我也哉古今之時雖不一矣而其
致一焉希之則堯也希之則舜也蓋不必親炙
其盛而凡有興起者均之可追於千載之上矣
此其言之有足徴者而豈强人也哉吁孟子以
是語曹交所以啓其作聖之機而勵其必爲之
志者至矣奈何交之徒以形體求也雖然堯舜
豈易能哉祖述而宗之孔子也畎畝而樂之伊
尹也其所宗所樂自有精神心術之祕而不可
語人者曹交不足以與此故孟子直指孝弟以
===
示之此作聖之標的也噫兢兢業業堯舜猶且
難之况其下者乎學者必知其難斯得其易矣
易
九五甘節吉往有尚
孫希夔
同考試官教諭廖批精透整潔甘吉有尚處挑剔尤明
考試官學正吴批清順
考試官教授顧批典實
punctuated:
信者，而豈欺我也哉？古今之時雖不一矣，而其致一焉。希之則堯也，希之則舜也，蓋不必親炙其盛，而凡有興起者，均之可追於千載之上矣。此其言之有足徴者，而豈强人也哉？吁！孟子以是語曹交，所以啓其作聖之機，而勵其必爲之志者至矣。奈何交之徒以形體求也！雖然，堯舜豈易能哉？祖述而宗之，孔子也；畎畝而樂之，伊尹也。其所宗所樂，自有精神心術之祕而不可語人者。曹交不足以與此，故孟子直指孝弟以示之，此作聖之標的也。噫！兢兢業業，堯舜猶且難之，况其下者乎？學者必知其難，斯得其易矣。
易
九五，甘節，吉，往有尚。
孫希夔
同考試官教諭廖批：精透整潔，甘吉有尚處挑剔尤明。
考試官學正吴批：清順。
考試官教授顧批：典實。
translation_en:
…worthy of belief; how could these words deceive me? Though ancient and present times differ, their ultimate purport is one. Aspire to this, and one may become Yao; aspire to this, and one may become Shun. One need not have personally received instruction amid their flourishing age: anyone stirred to action can follow in their footsteps across a thousand years. These words have sufficient corroboration; how could they impose an unreasonable demand? Ah! In saying this to Cao Jiao, Mencius did all he could to open the way for him to become a sage and strengthen his resolve to do so. Why, then, did Jiao seek the answer merely in bodily stature? Even so, how could attaining the accomplishments of Yao and Shun be easy? It was Confucius who transmitted their teachings and took them as his masters; it was Yi Yin who delighted in their Way while working in the fields. What they revered and delighted in held inward subtleties of spirit and the workings of the mind that could not be conveyed to others. Cao Jiao was not capable of participating in this, so Mencius pointed directly to filial devotion and fraternal respect to instruct him. These are the target at which one aims in becoming a sage. Alas! Even Yao and Shun found it difficult to remain ever vigilant and conscientious; how much more so those below them! Students must understand its difficulty before they can find its ease.

Book of Changes
Nine in the fifth place: Sweet restraint. Auspicious. To go forward brings esteem.
Sun Xikui
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “Incisive and penetrating, orderly and polished. The distinctions drawn in the passages on ‘sweet,’ ‘auspicious,’ and ‘brings esteem’ are especially clear.”
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial.”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
五爻盡節之善而聖人深嘉其治焉甚矣節以
盡善爲難也五爻以之其治之吉而有尚也宜
哉周公所以繫其象占者如此且夫人君之圖
治也固貴有節以一其情尤貴善節以立其極
自夫德位未備而欲節之善也難矣惟九五當
位而有中正之德是其爲節也裁成以盡利而
章程之立適協乎天理之宜變通以趨時而藝
極之陳允合乎人心之當制之度數則制節以
謹度者莫非因分以嚴其防焉而非所以拂民
===
也議之德行則撙節以明禮者莫非緣性以秩
其等焉而非所以强世也其殆甘節而非過於
苦矣占者如此吾知紀綱布之朝廷而倫制兼
該有以建天地而不悖軌物頒之邦國而美善
咸備可以考帝王而不違百官莫不受成焉庶
民不敢私議焉惟皇建極而節之所以稱盛典
者在是矣其吉也何如以是而往也吾知聲敎
敷於四海而動無不化皆遵之爲定保之謨典
則垂於萬世而推無不準皆守之爲明徵之訓
punctuated: 五爻盡節之善，而聖人深嘉其治焉。甚矣，節以盡善爲難也！五爻以之，其治之吉而有尚也宜哉！周公所以繫其象占者如此。且夫人君之圖治也，固貴有節以一其情，尤貴善節以立其極。自夫德位未備，而欲節之善也，難矣！惟九五當位而有中正之德，是其爲節也，裁成以盡利，而章程之立適協乎天理之宜；變通以趨時，而藝極之陳允合乎人心之當。制之度數，則制節以謹度者，莫非因分以嚴其防焉，而非所以拂民也；議之德行，則撙節以明禮者，莫非緣性以秩其等焉，而非所以强世也。其殆甘節，而非過於苦矣！占者如此，吾知紀綱布之朝廷，而倫制兼該，有以建天地而不悖；軌物頒之邦國，而美善咸備，可以考帝王而不違。百官莫不受成焉，庶民不敢私議焉。惟皇建極，而節之所以稱盛典者在是矣。其吉也何如？以是而往也，吾知聲敎敷於四海，而動無不化，皆遵之爲定保之謨；典則垂於萬世，而推無不準，皆守之爲明徵之訓。
translation_en:
The fifth line realizes all the excellence of moderation, and the sage deeply commends the governance it produces. How difficult it is to attain complete excellence in moderation! Since the fifth line achieves this, it is fitting that its governance should bring good fortune and that advancing should earn esteem. Thus did the Duke of Zhou append his account of its image and prognostication.

When a ruler plans his government, he certainly values moderation as a means of unifying the dispositions of his people; still more, he values skill in moderation as a means of establishing the supreme standard. Where virtue and position are not both fully attained, achieving excellence in moderation is difficult indeed! Only the Nine in the Fifth occupies its proper position and possesses the virtue of centrality and correctness. In its moderation, it shapes and completes things to realize their full benefit, establishing regulations that accord precisely with what heavenly principle requires; it adapts to changing circumstances to meet the needs of the time, setting forth standards that truly accord with what is fitting to the human heart. In establishing measures and numerical limits, its regulation and careful observance of bounds invariably follow allotted distinctions to maintain strict safeguards, rather than thwarting the people. In deliberating upon virtue and conduct, its restraint and clarification of ritual invariably follow human nature to order the gradations of rank, rather than coercing the world. This is surely sweet moderation, not moderation carried to excessive bitterness!

If one who consults the oracle acts thus, I know that the guiding principles will be spread throughout the court, comprehending all ethical relationships and institutions, and may be set before Heaven and Earth without contradiction. Norms will be promulgated throughout the realm, complete in beauty and goodness, and may be tested against the ancient emperors and kings without discrepancy. All officials will receive the established directives, and the common people will not dare privately to dispute them. The sovereign establishes the supreme standard: herein lies the reason moderation is called a magnificent institution. How great is its good fortune!

Proceeding on this basis, I know that the ruler’s moral influence and instruction will extend throughout the Four Seas: every action will transform the people, and all will follow them as plans for securing lasting stability. Canons and standards will be handed down through ten thousand generations: wherever applied, they will serve as the measure, and all will preserve them as teachings whose efficacy is manifest…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
行而世爲法也言而世爲則也惟民歸極而節
之所以稱盛治者在是矣不亦有尚乎是則於
甘節也見治道之善於吉而往有尚也見治功
之隆五爻之象占如此謂非立節之準也哉雖
然節亦未可易言也欲成甘節之治固貴有善
節之德而尤必有安節之臣故周禮一書品式
備至大經大法在焉周公之以節致太平者如
此而嘉成周之治者莫不誦周公之功不衰然
不有關雎麟趾之意何以行周官之法度乎此
===
當位以節中正以通而君臣爲萬化之原也
物相遇而後聚故受之以萃萃者聚也聚
而上者謂之升故受之以升
龍宗武
同考試官教諭廖 批 萃升以治道立格良是且
引用本文發揮殊覺親切宜錄以式多士
考試官學正吳 批 平正
考試官教授顧 批 純暢
善類集而治道隆易卦相承之義見矣夫治必
punctuated:
行而世爲法也，言而世爲則也。惟民歸極，而節之所以稱盛治者在是矣，不亦有尚乎？是則於甘節也，見治道之善；於吉而往有尚也，見治功之隆。五爻之象占如此，謂非立節之準也哉？雖然，節亦未可易言也。欲成甘節之治，固貴有善節之德，而尤必有安節之臣。故《周禮》一書，品式備至，大經大法在焉。周公之以節致太平者如此，而嘉成周之治者，莫不誦周公之功不衰。然不有《關雎》《麟趾》之意，何以行《周官》之法度乎？此當位以節，中正以通，而君臣爲萬化之原也。
物相遇而後聚，故受之以萃。萃者，聚也。聚而上者謂之升，故受之以升。
龍宗武

translation_en:
…His actions become a model for the world, and his words become its rule. The people turn to the supreme standard: herein lies the reason that regulation is acclaimed as flourishing government. Is this not worthy of esteem? Thus, in “sweet regulation” we see the excellence of the Way of government; in “auspicious; to go forward brings esteem,” we see the greatness of its achievements. Such are the image and prognostication of the fifth line. Could one deny that they provide a standard for establishing regulation? Nevertheless, regulation must not be spoken of lightly. To achieve government through sweet regulation, one certainly needs the virtue of regulating well, but above all one must have ministers who rest content in regulation. Thus the Rites of Zhou comprehensively sets out ranks and prescribed forms, containing the great guiding principles and laws. Such was the Duke of Zhou’s use of regulation to bring about supreme peace; all who admire the government of the Zhou in its maturity never cease to praise his accomplishments. Yet without the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hoofs” (Linzhi), how could one put into practice the statutes and standards of the Offices of Zhou? This is to regulate from one’s proper position and to achieve free passage through centrality and correctness: ruler and ministers are the source of all transformation.
“Only after things encounter one another do they gather; therefore Gathering (Cui) follows. Gathering means coming together. Gathering and moving upward is called Ascending (Sheng); therefore Ascending follows.”
Long Zongwu

Moreover, the quotations from the original text and the exposition of them feel especially pertinent. This should be recorded as a model for the many scholars.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: “Balanced and correct.”
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: “Pure and fluent.”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
待人而成也今惟相遇以聚而治斯隆焉萃升
之相承也有以哉且夫君子之用世也固以類
聚爲心而尤以昇平爲願自夫相遇之疎而上
進之阻是以欲其聚而升也難矣夫惟物之旣
決而相遇也則合渙以成萃而君子有大同之
會矣由是同道以爲朋而聲氣之感召自聯之
爲盍簪之交同德以相與而精神之潛通自孚
之爲和衷之益以弼一人則致主之忠同焉而
引萃以利見大人者此也以經庶政則體國之
===
誠一焉而萃如以利有攸往者此也是物不自
聚而聚於相遇萃之次姤者以此萃者正言乎
聚之義也惟物未上聚而治無由以升矣今旣
相遇而聚於上焉則合聚以同升而世道有順
治之機矣但見庶明之勵翼自庶績之其凝而
升斯世於大猷之盛百工之承弼自百度之惟
貞而致天下於上治之隆協恭於朝則天工由
之以亮焉而時升以成升階之化者此也和鳴
於國則帝載由之以熙焉而允升以行南征之
punctuated: 待人而成也。今惟相遇以聚，而治斯隆焉，萃升之相承也有以哉！且夫君子之用世也，固以類聚爲心，而尤以昇平爲願。自夫相遇之疎，而上進之阻，是以欲其聚而升也難矣。夫惟物之旣決而相遇也，則合渙以成萃，而君子有大同之會矣。由是同道以爲朋，而聲氣之感召，自聯之爲盍簪之交；同德以相與，而精神之潛通，自孚之爲和衷之益。以弼一人，則致主之忠同焉，而引萃以利見大人者此也；以經庶政，則體國之誠一焉，而萃如以利有攸往者此也。是物不自聚，而聚於相遇。萃之次姤者以此，萃者正言乎聚之義也。惟物未上聚，而治無由以升矣。今旣相遇而聚於上焉，則合聚以同升，而世道有順治之機矣。但見庶明之勵翼，自庶績之其凝，而升斯世於大猷之盛；百工之承弼，自百度之惟貞，而致天下於上治之隆。協恭於朝，則天工由之以亮焉，而時升以成升階之化者此也；和鳴於國，則帝載由之以熙焉，而允升以行南征之
translation_en:
…depends upon worthy men for its accomplishment. Now, only when they encounter one another and gather together does good government flourish. There is indeed a reason why Gathering (Cui) and Ascending (Sheng) follow one another! When gentlemen enter public service, they certainly set their hearts on gathering with their own kind, but still more they aspire to an age of peace. When encounters are infrequent and advancement is obstructed, it is difficult to bring about their gathering and ascent. Only when things, once decisively separated, encounter one another do the scattered unite to form a gathering, and gentlemen enjoy a meeting in great concord. Thus those who share the same Way become companions: through the mutual attraction of their voices and vital energies, they naturally form the fellowship described as “gathering hairpins.” Those who share the same virtue associate with one another: through the unspoken communion of their minds and spirits, they naturally establish the mutual trust that brings the benefits of harmonious purpose. In assisting the One Man, the sovereign, they share the same loyalty in bringing their ruler to perfection: this is what is meant by drawing others into the gathering, so that “it is beneficial to see the great man.” In administering the many affairs of government, they are united in their sincerity of devotion to the state: this is what is meant by gathering, so that “it is beneficial to have somewhere to go.” Things, then, do not gather of themselves; they gather through encountering one another. This is why Gathering follows Encountering (Gou). Gathering precisely expresses the meaning of coming together.

So long as worthy men have not gathered above, at court, government has no means of ascending. Now that they have encountered one another and gathered above, they unite in a gathering to ascend together, and the affairs of the age have an opportunity to proceed toward orderly government. We see the many enlightened men exerting themselves in support, thereby bringing the various achievements to completion and raising this age to the flourishing realization of the great plan; the many officials supporting and assisting, thereby setting all institutions aright and bringing all under Heaven to the fullness of the highest order. When they unite in reverence at court, Heaven’s work is thereby accomplished: this is what is meant by ascending at the proper time to achieve the transformation figured by “ascending the steps.” When they sound in harmony throughout the realm, the sovereign’s undertakings thereby flourish: this is what is meant by “ascending with confidence” to carry out the southward expedition’s …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
志者此也是治不自升而升於上聚升之次萃
者以此是則物遇而聚也見朝廷正而善人多
焉物聚而升也見賢才輔而天下治焉二卦相
承之義如此不亦可爲世道慶哉噫此唐虞成
周之所以爲盛也故元愷並舉卒成風動之休
十人同心竟致永清之治然非有堯舜文武之
君又豈能純心以用賢而得人以成化乎故書
曰元首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉而克艱之言
尤惓惓致意也
===
書
皐陶拜手稽首颺言曰念哉率作興事慎
乃憲欽哉屢省乃成欽哉乃賡載歌曰
元首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉
萬邦獻
同考試官教諭陳批詞理精到深得賡歌本旨
非素懷忠愛者不能形容至此佳哉
同考試官教諭陳批理明詞暢意足句工而氣
勢順猶出大成宜錄以式
punctuated:
志者此也。是治不自升，而升於上聚，升之次萃者以此。是則物遇而聚也，見朝廷正而善人多焉；物聚而升也，見賢才輔而天下治焉。二卦相承之義如此，不亦可爲世道慶哉？噫！此唐虞成周之所以爲盛也。故元愷並舉，卒成風動之休；十人同心，竟致永清之治。然非有堯舜文武之君，又豈能純心以用賢，而得人以成化乎？故《書》曰：「元首明哉！股肱良哉！庶事康哉！」而克艱之言，尤惓惓致意也。

書
皐陶拜手稽首，颺言曰：「念哉！率作興事，慎乃憲。欽哉！屢省乃成。欽哉！」乃賡載歌曰：「元首明哉！股肱良哉！庶事康哉！」
萬邦獻

同考試官教諭陳批：詞理精到，深得賡歌本旨。非素懷忠愛者，不能形容至此。佳哉！

同考試官教諭陳批：理明詞暢，意足句工，而氣勢順猶出大成，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…this is what fulfills that aspiration. Good government does not ascend of itself: it ascends through gathering at the top. This is why Ascending (Sheng) follows Gathering (Cui). Thus, when things encounter one another and gather, we see an upright court with many good men; when things gather and ascend, we see worthy and talented men assisting the ruler, and the realm well governed. Such is the meaning of the succession of these two hexagrams. Is this not cause to rejoice for the course of the world? Ah! This is what made the ages of Tang, Yu, and the established Zhou so flourishing. Thus, when the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai were all raised to office, they ultimately achieved the splendid transformation that spread like the wind; when the ten ministers were of one mind, they finally brought about enduring peace. Yet without rulers such as Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu, how could one employ worthy men with an undivided heart and obtain the right men to accomplish moral transformation? Hence the Book of Documents says: “When the head is enlightened, the limbs are good, and all affairs prosper!” Its words about mastering the difficulties of rulership express this concern with particular earnestness.

Book of Documents
Gao Yao bowed with his hands joined and his forehead to the ground, and proclaimed: “Be mindful! In leading undertakings and initiating affairs, be careful of your laws. Be reverent! Repeatedly examine your accomplishments. Be reverent!” He then continued with a responding song: “When the head is enlightened, the limbs are good, and all affairs prosper!”
Wan Bangxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The language and reasoning are refined and exact, profoundly grasping the original intent of the responding song. Someone who did not habitually cherish loyalty and devotion could not portray it so fully. Excellent!

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The reasoning is clear, the language fluent, the meaning fully expressed, and the sentences skillfully crafted. Its force and movement flow smoothly, seemingly displaying consummate mastery [?]. It should be selected for inclusion as a model.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正吳批雅健
考試官敎授顧批精邃
大臣致敬以述作歌之意而因咏其詞焉夫興
事考成則君明而臣良事康因之矣大臣賡歌
而責難于君也有以哉昔皐陶因舜之歌而欲
賡歌以復于舜也故拜手稽首而颺言曰勅天
之道君爲之主而臣爲之輔帝其念哉毋徒責
之臣也彼事起于勵精而或失之紛更非勅天
也必操振作之權而一惟成憲之監道揆是總
===
也法守必信也欽哉惟敬以存治體可焉事成
于課功而或失之廢弛非勅天也必嚴覈實之
典而屢計羣吏之治三載考績也三考黜陟也
欽哉惟敬以崇治功可焉一敬立而勅天之道
盡矣乃從而歌之曰臣賴君以爲倡猶股肱須
元首以爲運也故爲君者大觀在上而不昧總
率之宜秉哲馭下而不爽省成之柄元首其明
哉則見紀法彰而人心奮濟濟羣工莫不奉法
脩職而副明作之望矣股肱其良哉由是職業
punctuated:
考試官學正吳批：雅健。
考試官敎授顧批：精邃。
大臣致敬以述作歌之意，而因咏其詞焉。夫興事考成，則君明而臣良，事康因之矣。大臣賡歌而責難于君也，有以哉！昔皐陶因舜之歌，而欲賡歌以復于舜也，故拜手稽首而颺言曰：「勅天之道，君爲之主，而臣爲之輔。帝其念哉！毋徒責之臣也。彼事起于勵精，而或失之紛更，非勅天也。必操振作之權，而一惟成憲之監，道揆是總也，法守必信也。欽哉！惟敬以存治體可焉。事成于課功，而或失之廢弛，非勅天也。必嚴覈實之典，而屢計羣吏之治，三載考績也，三考黜陟也。欽哉！惟敬以崇治功可焉。一敬立，而勅天之道盡矣。」乃從而歌之曰：「臣賴君以爲倡，猶股肱須元首以爲運也。故爲君者，大觀在上而不昧總率之宜，秉哲馭下而不爽省成之柄。元首其明哉！則見紀法彰而人心奮，濟濟羣工莫不奉法脩職，而副明作之望矣。股肱其良哉！由是職業
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous.”
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: “Refined and profound.”
The great minister paid his respects to explain his intention in composing a song, and thereupon sang its words. When undertakings are initiated and their accomplishments assessed, the ruler is enlightened and his ministers worthy; the flourishing of affairs follows from this. The great minister had good reason to continue the song and demand difficult things of his ruler!
Formerly, Gao Yao wished to continue Shun’s song in reply to him. Thus, bowing with hands joined and touching his head to the ground, he declared aloud: “In carrying out Heaven’s commands, the ruler takes the leading role and his ministers assist him. Let the emperor keep this in mind! Do not lay the responsibility solely upon your ministers. Undertakings begin with resolute exertion, but they may go astray through incessant changes; this is not carrying out Heaven’s commands. You must exercise your authority to spur action, taking established statutes alone as your guide. You must oversee the guiding principles of government, and adherence to the laws must be dependable. Be reverent! Only through reverence can the fundamental order of government be preserved. Undertakings reach completion through the assessment of achievements, but they may go astray through neglect and laxity; this is not carrying out Heaven’s commands. You must rigorously enforce the procedures for verifying actual performance, repeatedly assessing the administration of all officials: evaluate their achievements every three years, and after three evaluations demote or promote them. Be reverent! Only through reverence can the accomplishments of government be enhanced. Once reverence is established, the way of carrying out Heaven’s commands is fully realized.”
He then continued in song: “Ministers depend upon their ruler to lead, just as the limbs depend upon the head to move. Thus the ruler must stand above as a great exemplar, clearly understanding the proper way to provide overall direction; he must govern his subordinates with wisdom, never failing in his exercise of authority to scrutinize accomplishments. How enlightened the head must be! Then laws and discipline will be manifest, and people’s hearts will be stirred to action. The assembled officials will all uphold the laws and attend to their duties, fulfilling the expectation that they work with discernment. How worthy the limbs must be! As a result, official duties …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
脩而品式備綜綜庶政莫不振綱肅紀而成精
明之治矣庶事其康哉蓋明即為起而勅天之
道立故良也康也即為喜為熈而勅天之治成
帝可徒責諸臣為哉噫臯陶賡歌而責之舜者
意深切矣抑考之易曰天道下濟而光明明非
用察之謂也彼漢宣綜核名實曾何得于考成
之治而宋神宗更制紛紛于愼憲之道又大戾
焉以是為明明斯舛矣後之欲求大舜之明者
當求之問察之實
===
次九曰嚮用五福

經學者也允宜高薦

而平正中自有人不及處宜冠本房
考試官學正吳批瑩潔
考試官敎授顧批通暢
聖人第疇之九而先之以勸天下者焉蓋福以
punctuated:
脩而品式備，綜綜庶政，莫不振綱肅紀而成精明之治矣。庶事其康哉！蓋明即為起，而勅天之道立；故良也，康也，即為喜、為熈，而勅天之治成。帝可徒責諸臣為哉？噫！臯陶賡歌而責之舜者，意深切矣。抑考之《易》曰：「天道下濟而光明。」明非用察之謂也。彼漢宣綜核名實，曾何得于考成之治？而宋神宗更制紛紛，于愼憲之道又大戾焉。以是為明，明斯舛矣。後之欲求大舜之明者，當求之問察之實。

次九曰嚮用五福
湯顯祖

translation_en:
…duties are fulfilled and prescribed forms are complete. In the manifold affairs of government [?], guiding principles are upheld and discipline made rigorous, bringing about clear and discerning government. “May all affairs prosper!” For being discerning is precisely what is meant by “rousing oneself,” whereby the Way of attending reverently to Heaven is established. Thus, being good and prospering are precisely what is meant by “rejoicing” and “flourishing,” whereby government that attends reverently to Heaven is accomplished. Could the emperor merely demand action from his ministers? Ah! Profound and earnest was Gao Yao’s intention in continuing the song and laying this responsibility upon Shun.

Moreover, examining the Book of Changes, we find: “The Way of Heaven descends to bestow aid and shines brightly.” Discernment does not mean scrutinizing others. Emperor Xuan of the Han comprehensively checked names against actual performance, but what did he truly attain of government through assessing accomplishments? Emperor Shenzong of the Song made a bewildering succession of institutional changes, departing still further from the Way of treating established statutes with care. To call this discernment is to misconstrue discernment. Those in later ages who wish to seek the discernment of the great Shun should seek it in the substance of his questioning and examination.

“Ninth is turning toward and using the five blessings.”
Tang Xianzu
