title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
章善也勸人以福則人有不樂于爲善者哉宜
大禹以之第次九之疇也且夫書之數有所謂
九者位列于離而天地之祕以顯數成于金而
陰陽之用已全禹乃以序于次八之後而第之
曰嚮用五福焉蓋人之爲善必有所慕而後其
趨莫禦君之作善必有所勸而後其機自神惟
天眷德固有福以厚之也而以德先天下者則
緣是以妙化導之術惟德動天福固自已求之
也而以道化斯民者則藉是以昭勸相之權方
===
其未嚮于善也則示之五福以興起之使天下
之相率于善而不敢悖者用此道也及其既嚮
于善也則錫之五福以固結之使天下之益力
于善而不敢怠者用此道也天子立臣之極固
以福自嚮矣亦以之而嚮其臣即應感之不誣
者以誘其進而百官之羞行者翕如也其諸王
者激勸臣工之典乎天子立民之極固以福自
勸矣亦以之而勸其民即天人之不爽者以决
其趨而黎民之敏德者勃如也其諸王者鼓舞
punctuated:
章善也。勸人以福，則人有不樂于爲善者哉？宜大禹以之第次九之疇也。且夫書之數有所謂九者，位列于離而天地之祕以顯，數成于金而陰陽之用已全。禹乃以序于次八之後，而第之曰「嚮用五福」焉。蓋人之爲善，必有所慕而後其趨莫禦；君之作善，必有所勸而後其機自神。惟天眷德，固有福以厚之也；而以德先天下者，則緣是以妙化導之術。惟德動天，福固自已求之也；而以道化斯民者，則藉是以昭勸相之權。

方其未嚮于善也，則示之五福以興起之，使天下之相率于善而不敢悖者，用此道也。及其既嚮于善也，則錫之五福以固結之，使天下之益力于善而不敢怠者，用此道也。天子立臣之極，固以福自嚮矣，亦以之而嚮其臣，即應感之不誣者以誘其進，而百官之羞行者翕如也，其諸王者激勸臣工之典乎？天子立民之極，固以福自勸矣，亦以之而勸其民，即天人之不爽者以决其趨，而黎民之敏德者勃如也，其諸王者鼓舞
translation_en:
…to make goodness manifest. If people are encouraged by blessings, could anyone fail to delight in doing good? It was fitting that the Great Yu placed this as the ninth category. Now, among the numbers of the River Luo Writing, there is what is called nine: its position corresponds to the trigram Li, thereby revealing the mysteries of Heaven and Earth; its number reaches completion in Metal, so that the workings of yin and yang are fully realized. Yu therefore arranged it after the eighth category and designated it “Encouraging through the Five Blessings.” For people to do good, they must have something to aspire to; only then does their pursuit become irresistible. For the ruler to foster goodness, there must be something with which to encourage it; only then does the process become wondrously effective. Heaven cherishes virtue and assuredly bestows blessings to enrich it; one who leads the world through virtue accordingly draws upon this to perfect the art of transforming and guiding people. Virtue alone moves Heaven, and blessings must indeed be sought through oneself; one who transforms these people through the Way accordingly draws upon this to make manifest the power of encouragement and assistance.

Before they have turned toward goodness, he presents the Five Blessings to awaken them. This is the means by which all under Heaven lead one another toward goodness and dare not act perversely. Once they have turned toward goodness, he bestows the Five Blessings to strengthen their commitment. This is the means by which all under Heaven exert themselves still more in goodness and dare not slacken. The Son of Heaven establishes the highest standard for his ministers. He certainly directs himself toward blessings, but he also uses them to guide his ministers. Drawing upon the unfailing correspondence between stimulus and response, he induces them to advance, and the hundred officials unite in cultivating their conduct. Is this not the king’s established practice for inspiring and encouraging his officials? The Son of Heaven establishes the highest standard for the people. He certainly encourages himself through blessings, but he also uses them to encourage his people. Drawing upon the unfailing correspondence between Heaven and humanity, he gives firm direction to their pursuits, and the common people rise vigorously to exert themselves in virtue. Is this not how the king inspires…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
萬民之術乎要之書終于九數而神道以成疇
勸以五福而治道斯備大禹取而配之其旨深
矣夫是則皇極行而何彝倫之不敘哉雖然嚮
用之說聖人爲凡民言之也君子無所爲而爲
善豈待福而後勸邪是故上下無交孔子之脩
德如故也居於陋巷顏子之好學不改也何者
其中之所自嚮者定也明于自嚮而可以免幸
福之咎矣
詩
===
瞻彼洛矣維水泱泱君子至止福祿如茨
鞸琫有奭以作六師
萬國欽
同考試官教諭唐批周王講武振揚之意發揮
殆盡而詞更典雅是善說詩者宜錄
同考試官教諭鄭批理明詞暢而講末歸束處
辟庶邦尤出人意表佳哉
考試官學正吴批典麗得體
考試官教授顧批莊雅
punctuated:
萬民之術乎？要之，書終于九數而神道以成，疇勸以五福而治道斯備。大禹取而配之，其旨深矣夫！是則皇極行而何彝倫之不敘哉？雖然，嚮用之說，聖人爲凡民言之也。君子無所爲而爲善，豈待福而後勸邪？是故上下無交，孔子之脩德如故也；居於陋巷，顏子之好學不改也。何者？其中之所自嚮者定也。明于自嚮，而可以免幸福之咎矣。
詩
瞻彼洛矣，維水泱泱。君子至止，福祿如茨。鞸琫有奭，以作六師。
萬國欽
同考試官教諭唐批：周王講武振揚之意，發揮殆盡，而詞更典雅，是善說詩者，宜錄。
同考試官教諭鄭批：理明詞暢，而講末歸束處，辟庶邦尤出人意表，佳哉！
考試官學正吴批：典麗得體。
考試官教授顧批：莊雅。
translation_en:
…the means by which a king inspires the myriad people? In sum, the Book of Documents concludes with the number nine, and the Way of the spirits is thereby completed; its category encourages people through the Five Blessings, and the Way of governance is thereby fully provided. Great Yu adopted these and paired them: how profound his purpose was! Thus, when the August Norm is put into practice, what constant human relationships could fail to be properly ordered? Nevertheless, the sages spoke of turning toward and enjoying blessings for the sake of ordinary people. The gentleman does good without an ulterior purpose: how could he wait for blessings before being encouraged? Thus, even when those above and below had no dealings with one another, Confucius continued cultivating virtue as before; though living in a humble lane, Master Yan remained unchanged in his love of learning. Why? Because the direction toward which each inwardly turned was firmly settled. By understanding this inward orientation, one can avoid the fault of seeking blessings through mere good fortune.
Book of Odes
“Look upon that Luo River, its waters vast and flowing. The lord has arrived; blessings and emoluments are thick as thatch. His knee covering and scabbard ornaments gleam red, as he rouses the Six Armies.”
Wan Guoqin
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The Zhou king’s intention in practicing military exercises and displaying martial vigor is expounded almost exhaustively, while the language is moreover classically elegant. This is someone skilled in explaining the Odes; the essay merits selection.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The reasoning is clear and the language fluent. In particular, the concluding treatment of ‘the rulers of the various states’ [?] is quite unexpected. Excellent!”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Classically elegant and appropriate in form.”
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: “Dignified and elegant.”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
王者之涖東都集大福而奮大武也夫安不忘
危則福可保矣東都會而六師作焉其知此道
者乎諸侯所以美之也若謂我周之營洛也以
聯天下之志固在于脩文以防天下之危尤在
于講武焉萬世深長計者均之不可廢也今日
之會殆躬逢其盛而人心爲之快覩者矣瞻彼
洛水瀍澗之所瀠也而有以擅朝宗之勢伊黎
之所合也而有以萃風氣之交泱泱然誠天造
地設之宏規而宅中圖大之勝槩也我君子之
===
至止也藉累世發源之深協萬國冠裳之會上
爲天之宗子天所助順者也而清時之純嘏綏
矣下爲民之元后民所助信者也而昭代之休
徵集矣若是乎福祿之如茨也而君子之心豈
恃此而忘備也哉知武事不可以廢弛也釋袞
冕之儀而身親夫甲胄之飾知人心不可以玩
愒也御靺鞈之服而儼示乎神武之威于以比
其什伍則伍兩軍師之衆聚焉是雖有司徒以
籍之而臨之以萬乘之尊則威嚴之下所以壯
punctuated: 王者之涖東都，集大福而奮大武也。夫安不忘危，則福可保矣。東都會而六師作焉，其知此道者乎！諸侯所以美之也。若謂我周之營洛也，以聯天下之志，固在于脩文；以防天下之危，尤在于講武焉。萬世深長計者，均之不可廢也。今日之會，殆躬逢其盛，而人心爲之快覩者矣。瞻彼洛水，瀍澗之所瀠也，而有以擅朝宗之勢；伊黎之所合也，而有以萃風氣之交。泱泱然，誠天造地設之宏規，而宅中圖大之勝槩也。我君子之至止也，藉累世發源之深，協萬國冠裳之會，上爲天之宗子，天所助順者也，而清時之純嘏綏矣；下爲民之元后，民所助信者也，而昭代之休徵集矣。若是乎福祿之如茨也，而君子之心豈恃此而忘備也哉！知武事不可以廢弛也，釋袞冕之儀，而身親夫甲胄之飾；知人心不可以玩愒也，御靺鞈之服，而儼示乎神武之威。于以比其什伍，則伍兩軍師之衆聚焉。是雖有司徒以籍之，而臨之以萬乘之尊，則威嚴之下，所以壯
translation_en:
The king’s arrival at the eastern capital gathers great blessings and rouses great martial power. If one does not forget danger amid peace, blessings can be preserved. When the assembly is held at the eastern capital and the six armies are mobilized, does this not show an understanding of this principle? This is why the feudal lords praise him. It is as though they were saying: “When our Zhou established Luo, cultivating civil accomplishments was certainly essential to uniting the purposes of all under Heaven; practicing military affairs was especially essential to guarding against dangers throughout the realm. In planning far ahead for countless generations, neither could be neglected. At today’s assembly, we have indeed personally encountered this flourishing spectacle, which gladdens people’s hearts to behold.
“Look at those waters of the Luo, around which the Chan and Jian wind: they command a configuration drawing waters toward them, like lords coming to court. Here the Yi and Li [?] converge, bringing together the currents of wind and vital energy. Vast indeed is this magnificent setting fashioned by Heaven and Earth, a splendid site for occupying the center and planning great undertakings. When our lord arrives, he draws upon the deep sources of successive generations and brings into harmony the assembly of the myriad states in their ceremonial caps and robes. In relation to Heaven above, he is its principal heir, whose obedience Heaven assists, and abundant blessings of a peaceful age settle upon him. In relation to the people below, he is their sovereign, whose trustworthiness they support, and auspicious signs of an illustrious age gather around him. So thickly do blessings and emoluments accumulate, like thatch! Yet how could our lord rely upon these and forget preparedness?
“Knowing that military affairs must not be neglected, he puts aside the ceremonial trappings of embroidered robe and crown and personally dons armor and helmet. Knowing that people’s hearts must not be allowed to lapse into idle ease, he wears the protective garments of war and solemnly displays his divine martial might. Thereby he marshals his men in tens and fives, and the assembled ranks of squads, companies, armies, and divisions gather. Although the Minister of Education maintains their registers, the ruler himself presides over them with the dignity of a sovereign of ten thousand chariots; beneath his imposing authority, the means by which he strengthens …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
六師之精采者在是矣仰王靈之丕振而六服
羣辟亦何者而非折衝之士乎于以明其誓戒
則進退坐作之法齊焉是雖有司馬以掌之而
申之以一王之命則激勸之餘所以倡六師之
勇敢者在是矣仰聖武之布昭而庶邦冢君亦
何者而非敵愾之師乎夫不恃其已然之福而
尤嚴其未然之防則今日之會佳兵固所以休
兵而講武實所以偃武也如茨之福祿不與洛
水相為無窮也哉抑是詩也深得人臣進規之
===
義也戎兵之詰張皇之訓周召所以告其君者
其慮遠矣洛水之會固有周家法而諸侯之美
而不諂亦周召遺意也吴功甫奏遂生侈心蔡
人方歸輒弛武備不足論矣而漠北之役驪山
之師則又何為也哉噫此又可為銷兵散卒者
道也
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
李廷謨
同考試官教諭沈批講中有發周王自陳法祖
punctuated:
六師之精采者在是矣。仰王靈之丕振，而六服羣辟亦何者而非折衝之士乎？于以明其誓戒，則進退坐作之法齊焉。是雖有司馬以掌之，而申之以一王之命，則激勸之餘，所以倡六師之勇敢者在是矣。仰聖武之布昭，而庶邦冢君亦何者而非敵愾之師乎？夫不恃其已然之福，而尤嚴其未然之防，則今日之會，佳兵固所以休兵，而講武實所以偃武也。如茨之福祿，不與洛水相為無窮也哉？抑是詩也，深得人臣進規之義也。戎兵之詰、張皇之訓，周召所以告其君者，其慮遠矣。洛水之會，固有周家法，而諸侯之美而不諂，亦周召遺意也。吴功甫奏，遂生侈心；蔡人方歸，輒弛武備，不足論矣。而漠北之役、驪山之師，則又何為也哉？噫！此又可為銷兵散卒者道也。

儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。
李廷謨
同考試官教諭沈批：講中有發，周王自陳法祖
translation_en:
…it is precisely this that invigorates the spirit of the Six Armies. Looking up to the mighty manifestation of royal power, which of the lords of the six zones of submission would not be a warrior capable of repelling the enemy? By making the oaths and admonitions clear, the king brings uniformity to the rules for advancing and retreating, sitting and rising. Although the Minister of War administers these matters, their reiteration through the command of the sole sovereign provides encouragement and exhortation: herein lies the means of stirring the courage of the Six Armies. Looking up to the radiant display of the sage king’s martial might, which of the rulers of the many states would not lead a force against the king’s enemies? He does not rely upon blessings already received, but takes still stricter precautions against dangers yet to come. Thus, at today’s gathering, esteeming arms is indeed a means of bringing warfare to rest, and practicing warfare is truly a means of laying arms aside. Will blessings and emoluments as abundant as thatch not endure without end, like the waters of the Luo?

Moreover, this poem profoundly embodies the duty of a minister to offer admonition. The injunctions to put military forces in order and to display their might show how far ahead the Dukes of Zhou and Shao looked when advising their sovereign. The gathering by the Luo certainly followed the established practices of the house of Zhou; and the feudal lords’ praise without flattery likewise preserved the intent of those dukes. Success against Wu had scarcely been reported before extravagant ambitions arose [?]; the men of Cai had only just returned when military preparations were relaxed. These scarcely merit discussion. But what, then, was the purpose of the campaign north of the desert and the army at Mount Li? Alas! This too is something that might be explained to those who melt down weapons and disband troops.

“Follow and emulate the statutes of King Wen, daily bringing peace to the four quarters.”

Li Tingmo

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The exposition contains illuminating insights. The king of Zhou himself sets forth his intention to emulate his ancestors…”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之意而辭內開明於意也非徒工舉業者比也錄之
同考試官敎諭唐批意婉而盡詞和而達讀之
鏗然有金玉聲深得頌體者
考試官學正吳批豐潤可式
考試官敎授顧批典麗
周王法典以安民而先王之心慰矣蓋文王以
安民爲心者也法其典斯安其民矣所以感格
之者其有本乎我將之詩及此意謂明堂啓而
將享行祀上帝亦所以祀文王也予之所賴以
===
格之者豈徒以其禮焉而已哉蓋必有其本矣
夫文王之心安天下之心也文王之典安天下
之典也文王往矣而不與之俱往者幸其典之
所在不可一日而廢焉者予也繼其統卽繼其
心而家法之可傳者奉之爲致治保邦之具世
其業卽世其德而成規之已試者率之爲綏民
和衆之猷典有禮樂載在周官者可考也非四
方之所繹思者乎我其儀而式之□□衣□□
宣之而光天海隅悉歸于寧謐之域典有政刑
punctuated:
之意，而辭內開明於意也，非徒工舉業者比也，錄之。
同考試官敎諭唐批：意婉而盡，詞和而達，讀之鏗然有金玉聲，深得頌體者。
考試官學正吳批：豐潤可式。
考試官敎授顧批：典麗。
周王法典以安民，而先王之心慰矣。蓋文王以安民爲心者也，法其典，斯安其民矣。所以感格之者，其有本乎！《我將》之詩及此，意謂明堂啓而將享，行祀上帝，亦所以祀文王也。予之所賴以格之者，豈徒以其禮焉而已哉？蓋必有其本矣。夫文王之心，安天下之心也；文王之典，安天下之典也。文王往矣，而不與之俱往者，幸其典之所在；不可一日而廢焉者，予也。繼其統，卽繼其心，而家法之可傳者，奉之爲致治保邦之具；世其業，卽世其德，而成規之已試者，率之爲綏民和衆之猷。典有禮樂，載在周官者可考也，非四方之所繹思者乎？我其儀而式之，□□衣□□宣之，而光天海隅悉歸于寧謐之域。典有政刑，
translation_en:
…the intention, while the wording makes that intention clear from within [?]. This is beyond comparison with the work of those merely skilled in examination composition. Record it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: The conception is subtle yet exhaustive; the language is harmonious yet expressive. Read aloud, it rings like metal and jade. It profoundly captures the form of the sacrificial hymn.

Comment by Examiner Wu, School Director: Rich and full, worthy of emulation.

Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: Classical and elegant.

The king of Zhou followed the established institutions to bring peace to the people, and thus comforted the heart of the former king. For King Wen set his heart upon bringing peace to the people. By following his institutions, one would bring peace to his people. Surely there was a foundation for thus moving his spirit to respond! When the poem “I Bring My Offerings” (Wo jiang) reaches this point, its meaning is this: the Hall of Enlightenment is opened and offerings are about to be presented; the sacrifice performed to the Lord on High is also the means of sacrificing to King Wen. Could what I rely upon to bring his spirit into communion be merely the ritual itself? Surely it must have a foundation.

King Wen’s heart was a heart set upon bringing peace to all under Heaven; King Wen’s institutions were institutions for bringing peace to all under Heaven. King Wen has passed away, but fortunately his institutions remain and have not passed away with him. I am the one who must not abandon them for a single day. To succeed to his line is to succeed to his purpose: I uphold the ancestral rules that can be transmitted as instruments for achieving good government and preserving the state. To inherit his undertaking is to inherit his virtue: I follow the established practices already proven effective as plans for pacifying the people and bringing harmony to the multitude.

Among these institutions are rites and music, whose record in the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan) can be examined. Are these not what the people of the four quarters continually ponder? I shall take them as my pattern and model, … clothing … proclaim them [?], so that all beneath the shining heavens, even to the farthest shores, enter a realm of peace and tranquility. Among these institutions are government and punishments …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
布在方策者可稽也非四方之所謳謌者乎我
其儀而刑之日與天下共遵之而羣黎百姓悉
納于怙冒之中雖因時立政不能不爲之潤色
也而宏綱大要一惟其創始之遺意焉蓋使文
王再興而損之益之以保乂斯民者猶之我而
已敢曰作聰明以自擅也而遂失其求寧之志
也哉雖與世宜民不能不爲之化裁也而良法
美意一惟其垂訓之初心焉蓋使文王再作而
變之通之以輯和斯民者猶之我而已敢曰任
===
私智以自用也而遂負其觀成之念也哉是典
之創于一時也莫非精神之運用而典之法于
今日也實爲意氣之流通矣神之格也不可自
信矣乎嘗謂明堂禮行所以配文王于上帝也
而侈之樂歌者乃曰靖四方焉其於祭之義何
哉蓋神無常享享于克誠誠者言乎其心之相
爲感也安民之心文王之心亦上帝求莫之心
也此其合于祭之義也不知此義而曰吾行吾
祀焉蒼璧黃琮越栗燔柴禮非不備也而陳之
punctuated:
布在方策者可稽也，非四方之所謳謌者乎？我其儀而刑之，日與天下共遵之，而羣黎百姓悉納于怙冒之中。雖因時立政，不能不爲之潤色也，而宏綱大要，一惟其創始之遺意焉。蓋使文王再興，而損之益之以保乂斯民者，猶之我而已。敢曰作聰明以自擅也，而遂失其求寧之志也哉？雖與世宜民，不能不爲之化裁也，而良法美意，一惟其垂訓之初心焉。蓋使文王再作，而變之通之以輯和斯民者，猶之我而已。敢曰任私智以自用也，而遂負其觀成之念也哉？是典之創于一時也，莫非精神之運用；而典之法于今日也，實爲意氣之流通矣。神之格也，不可自信矣乎？

嘗謂明堂禮行，所以配文王于上帝也，而侈之樂歌者乃曰「靖四方」焉，其於祭之義何哉？蓋神無常享，享于克誠。誠者，言乎其心之相爲感也。安民之心，文王之心，亦上帝求莫之心也。此其合于祭之義也。不知此義，而曰「吾行吾祀焉」，蒼璧黃琮，越栗燔柴，禮非不備也，而陳之
translation_en:
…those set out in written records can be examined. Are they not what people throughout the four quarters celebrate in song? I shall take them as my pattern and model, observing them daily together with all under Heaven, so that the entire populace may be brought under their protection. Although establishing government to suit the times inevitably requires some refinement, its broad principles and essential provisions must accord wholly with the intentions he left behind when first establishing them. Were King Wen to rise again and make reductions and additions to protect and govern these people, he would do just as I do. Would I dare to parade my cleverness and act on my own authority, thereby losing sight of his aspiration to secure peace? Although adapting to the age and meeting the people’s needs inevitably requires adjustments, sound laws and benevolent intentions must accord wholly with his original purpose in bequeathing his instructions. Were King Wen to return and adapt and develop these institutions to bring the people into harmony, he would do just as I do. Would I dare to rely on my private wisdom and act as I please, thereby betraying his hope of seeing his work brought to completion? When these institutions were first established, all embodied the workings of his spirit; when they are taken as models today, his intentions and aspirations truly flow through them. Can I not be confident that his spirit will come?

I have often reflected that the rites performed in the Hall of Light serve to associate King Wen with the Lord on High in sacrifice. Yet the ritual song that extols this declares, “Bring peace to the four quarters.” How does this relate to the meaning of sacrifice? Spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those offered with true sincerity. Sincerity means that hearts move one another in mutual response. The desire to bring peace to the people is King Wen’s desire, and also the Lord on High’s desire to secure repose [?]. This is what accords with the meaning of sacrifice. If one does not understand this meaning, but merely says, “I perform my sacrifices,” then, with blue jade discs and yellow jade tubes, yue and li [?], and the burning of firewood, the rites may indeed be complete; yet when these are presented…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
祝史有媿辭矣神其我歆乎故讀周禮者欲考
其尊尊親親之制當求其敬天法祖之心
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕春公會戎于潜〔隱〕
〔公二年〕
劉元卿
同考試官教諭張批〔尊周外夷聖人作經首義〕
〔也且王德王道尤體貼分曉宜錄以式〕
同考試官教諭侯批〔王者體用子能發揮明盡〕
〔非邃於經學者不能〕
考試官學正吳批〔明顯〕
考試官教授顧批〔嚴正〕
觀春秋尊周外夷之旨王者之體用備矣蓋王
者合體用而一之者也隆王正而謹交戎經世
之訓其深乎且帝王之御世也必囿天下以仁
而後其體立必辨天下以義而後其用行春秋
天子之事而體用咸備者也安得不於隱公之
編而首發之耶正月紀春明天時也而加王於
punctuated:
祝史有媿辭矣，神其我歆乎？故讀《周禮》者，欲考其尊尊親親之制，當求其敬天法祖之心。

春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕。春，公會戎于潜〔隱〕〔公二年〕。
劉元卿
同考試官教諭張批〔尊周外夷，聖人作經首義〕〔也。且王德王道，尤體貼分曉，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭侯批〔王者體用，子能發揮明盡，〕〔非邃於經學者不能。〕
考試官學正吳批〔明顯。〕
考試官教授顧批〔嚴正。〕

觀《春秋》尊周外夷之旨，王者之體用備矣。蓋王者合體用而一之者也。隆王正而謹交戎，經世之訓，其深乎！且帝王之御世也，必囿天下以仁，而後其體立；必辨天下以義，而後其用行。《春秋》，天子之事，而體用咸備者也，安得不於隱公之編而首發之耶？正月紀春，明天時也，而加王於
translation_en:
…the invocators and scribes have cause for shame in their words. Would the spirits accept my offerings? Thus, those who read the Rites of Zhou and wish to examine its institutions for honoring the honored and cherishing kin should seek the intention behind them: revering Heaven and taking the ancestors as models.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“Spring, the first month of the king’s calendar.” 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕 “In spring, the duke met the Rong at Qian.” 〔Second year of Duke Yin.〕
Liu Yuanqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Honoring Zhou and treating the Yi as outsiders constitute the foremost principle of the Sage’s composition of this classic. His treatment of kingly virtue and the kingly Way is especially perceptive and clear. This should be recorded as a model.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Hou, Instructor: 〔You have elucidated the substance and functioning of kingship clearly and fully. Only someone deeply versed in classical learning could accomplish this.〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: 〔Clear and manifest.〕
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: 〔Rigorous and correct.〕

Consider the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in honoring Zhou and treating the Yi as outsiders: the substance and functioning of kingship are fully present therein. For a true king unites substance and functioning as one. To exalt the king’s calendar and exercise caution in dealings with the Rong—how profound is this instruction for ordering the world! Moreover, when emperors and kings govern the world, they must embrace all under Heaven with benevolence before the substance of their rule can be established; they must distinguish among those under Heaven according to righteousness before its functioning can be put into effect. The Spring and Autumn Annals concerns the affairs of the Son of Heaven and fully embodies both substance and functioning. How could it fail to set these forth at the very outset of the annals of Duke Yin? Recording spring in the first month makes Heaven’s seasons clear; yet it adds the word “king” to…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
正焉是豈徒尊周而已哉蓋自乾坤覆載而萬
物竝育於其間矣王者參天兩地而可以自隘
其含弘之量乎以采甸則撫綏之不遺焉以荒
服則兼育之無外焉雖殊疆異域不無親疎之
等而有分土無分民王德之體固宜爾也苟於
正朔而不有以尊之則西周大統之業其何以
續好音於不墜也哉是故大一統以尊王庶乎
內而諸夏外而蠻貊莫敢不來享而帝王萬世
之業定矣其亦周官設懷方之意歟于潛書會
===
錄脩好也而戎舉其號焉豈徒抑夷而已哉蓋
自否泰攸分而陰陽消長於其間矣王者保泰
傾否而可以自弛其制禦之略乎以冠裳則捍
衞之孔固焉以左衽則防斥之惟嚴焉雖慕義
求通固有懷柔之道而治之以不治王道之用
固宜爾也苟於會戎而不有以外之則東郊旣
開之烈其何以繼先業於不忘也哉是故外戎
狄以譏魯庶乎內者不出外者不入莫不安其
所而中國萬世之防峻矣其亦周官別六服之
punctuated:
正焉，是豈徒尊周而已哉？蓋自乾坤覆載，而萬物竝育於其間矣。王者參天兩地，而可以自隘其含弘之量乎？以采甸則撫綏之不遺焉，以荒服則兼育之無外焉。雖殊疆異域，不無親疎之等，而有分土，無分民，王德之體固宜爾也。苟於正朔而不有以尊之，則西周大統之業，其何以續好音於不墜也哉？是故大一統以尊王，庶乎內而諸夏，外而蠻貊，莫敢不來享，而帝王萬世之業定矣。其亦《周官》設懷方之意歟？
于潛書會，錄脩好也，而戎舉其號焉，豈徒抑夷而已哉？蓋自否泰攸分，而陰陽消長於其間矣。王者保泰傾否，而可以自弛其制禦之略乎？以冠裳則捍衞之孔固焉，以左衽則防斥之惟嚴焉。雖慕義求通，固有懷柔之道，而治之以不治，王道之用固宜爾也。苟於會戎而不有以外之，則東郊旣開之烈，其何以繼先業於不忘也哉？是故外戎狄以譏魯，庶乎內者不出，外者不入，莫不安其所，而中國萬世之防峻矣。其亦《周官》別六服之
translation_en:
…to the first month. Could this merely be a matter of honoring Zhou? Ever since Heaven and Earth have covered and borne all things, the myriad beings have flourished together between them. The king takes Heaven as three and Earth as two: could he himself narrow his capacity for generous inclusion? Those in the appanage and royal domains he comforts and pacifies, neglecting none; those in the distant wilderness domain he nurtures together with the others, excluding none. Although distinct territories and different regions necessarily entail degrees of closeness and distance, land may be divided, but the people are not to be divided. Such, indeed, should be the substance of kingly virtue. If the royal calendar were not honored, how could the Western Zhou’s enterprise of unified rule perpetuate its good name without decline? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals exalts the great unity in order to honor the king, so that the various Xia peoples within and the Man and Mo peoples beyond might all venture nothing less than to come and present tribute. The imperial enterprise would thereby be secured for myriad generations. Is this not also the intent behind establishing the Office of Embracing Distant Regions in the Offices of Zhou?
The recording of the meeting at Qian records the cultivation of friendly relations, yet the Rong are designated by their collective name. Could this merely be a matter of disparaging the alien peoples? Ever since Obstruction and Peace were distinguished, yin and yang have waned and waxed between them. The king preserves Peace and overturns Obstruction: could he himself relax his strategies for restraint and defense? Those who wear caps and robes he protects with the utmost firmness; against those whose robes close to the left he guards and repels with the utmost strictness. Although there is certainly a way to conciliate those who admire righteousness and seek relations, governing them by not governing them is precisely how the kingly Way should operate. If, in recording the meeting with the Rong, the Annals did not treat them as outsiders, how could the meritorious achievement already established in the eastern suburbs perpetuate the ancestral undertaking without letting it be forgotten? Thus it treats the Rong and Di as outsiders in order to censure Lu, so that those within might not go out and those outside might not come in, and all might remain peacefully in their proper places. The defenses of the Central States would thereby stand firm for myriad generations. Is this not also the intent behind the Offices of Zhou’s differentiation of the six service domains …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
意歟吁王德體也體弘而用始不隘王道用也
用秩而體始不淆恩威兼濟其國家長乆之術
乎雖然廣土眾民先王懼焉夷狄雖或賓服其
欲逞之志未嘗忘也則夫仁賢以衛國德澤以
保民訓詰兵戎謹固疆圉者其可後歟此又順
治威嚴之道也詩曰勉勉我王綱紀四方書曰
無怠無荒四夷來王其亦春秋之意乎
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
===
伍惟忠
同考試官敎諭張批〔春秋不殊會宰孔正所以〕
〔尊王也此作得之〕
同考試官敎諭侯批〔明人臣之分處講得親切〕
〔錄之以式多士〕
考試官學正吳批〔得旨〕
考試官敎授顧批〔書法明白〕
聖經不殊重臣之與好尊王之義著矣蓋春秋
爲尊王而作也葵丘之會不殊宰孔其旨深哉
punctuated:
意歟？吁！王德，體也，體弘而用始不隘；王道，用也，用秩而體始不淆。恩威兼濟，其國家長乆之術乎？雖然，廣土眾民，先王懼焉。夷狄雖或賓服，其欲逞之志未嘗忘也。則夫仁賢以衛國，德澤以保民，訓詰兵戎，謹固疆圉者，其可後歟？此又順治威嚴之道也。《詩》曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」《書》曰：「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」其亦《春秋》之意乎？
夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
伍惟忠
同考試官敎諭張批〔春秋不殊會宰孔，正所以〕〔尊王也。此作得之。〕
同考試官敎諭侯批〔明人臣之分處，講得親切。〕〔錄之以式多士。〕
考試官學正吳批〔得旨。〕
考試官敎授顧批〔書法明白。〕
聖經不殊重臣之與好，尊王之義著矣。蓋《春秋》爲尊王而作也。葵丘之會不殊宰孔，其旨深哉！
translation_en:
…the intent? Ah! Royal virtue is the substance: only when that substance is broad can its application be unrestricted. The kingly Way is the application: only when that application is properly ordered can the substance remain unmixed. Might the combined exercise of benevolence and authority be the means of ensuring the state's enduring stability? Even so, extensive territory and a numerous population were causes of apprehension for the former kings. Although the Yi and Di may sometimes submit, they have never forgotten their ambition to have their way. Can one therefore defer employing humane and worthy men to defend the state, protecting the people through virtuous beneficence, training and inspecting the armed forces, and carefully securing the frontiers? This, too, is the way of orderly government and stern authority. The Book of Odes says: “Diligently our king orders and regulates the four quarters.” The Book of Documents says: “Be neither idle nor heedless, and the barbarians of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.” Is this not also the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals?
“In summer, the duke met with the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕
Wu Weizhong
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The Spring and Autumn Annals does not distinguish Steward Kong's participation in the meeting: this is precisely how〕〔it honors the king. This composition grasps that point.〕
Associate Examiner Hou, Instructor, comments: 〔The passage clarifying a subject's proper station explains it aptly and directly.〕〔Recorded here to serve as a model for the many scholars.〕
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: 〔Grasps the purport.〕
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: 〔The conventions of the Annals' wording are clearly explained.〕
The sage's classic does not distinguish the high minister's participation in this friendly gathering; thus the principle of honoring the king is made manifest. For the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed to honor the king. That it does not distinguish Steward Kong at the meeting at Kuiqiu has a profound significance indeed!

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
昔齊桓銳意尊周載締尋盟之好葵丘所由會
也宰孔肅將王命用申賜胙之儀西會所由與
也夫春秋之法分之尊者則殊其會王世子是
已孔以王臣出會宜亦在所尊矣而不殊會何
君子曰其聖人尊王之義乎蓋天下惟天子爲
獨尊下此皆臣也則皆媚于天子者也卑不可
踰尊也天下惟世子爲至貴下此皆臣也則皆
左右王躬者也賤不可妨貴也乃孔之在周何
如哉以作股肱固與天王爲一體矣而靖共之
===
節則有不可逃以寄心膂固與天子爲一德矣
而均勞之義則有不容已百官統焉四海均焉
職孰大乎職之大者責亦大進思盡忠亦自安
其天澤之分而要非可自多於君父也天工亮
焉帝載煕焉任孰重乎任之重者責亦重入而
輔相亦自率其論道之忠而要非可自侈於臣
工也噫爲司空而宅百揆禹也而祇承於舜孔
于襄王夫非禹之舜乎其爲帝臣之分則均矣
爲師傅而位冢宰周公也而篤棐於成王孔于
punctuated: 昔齊桓銳意尊周，載締尋盟之好，葵丘所由會也。宰孔肅將王命，用申賜胙之儀，西會所由與也。夫春秋之法，分之尊者則殊其會，王世子是已。孔以王臣出會，宜亦在所尊矣，而不殊會，何？君子曰：「其聖人尊王之義乎！」蓋天下惟天子爲獨尊，下此皆臣也，則皆媚于天子者也，卑不可踰尊也。天下惟世子爲至貴，下此皆臣也，則皆左右王躬者也，賤不可妨貴也。乃孔之在周何如哉？以作股肱，固與天王爲一體矣，而靖共之節則有不可逃；以寄心膂，固與天子爲一德矣，而均勞之義則有不容已。百官統焉，四海均焉，職孰大乎？職之大者責亦大，進思盡忠，亦自安其天澤之分，而要非可自多於君父也。天工亮焉，帝載煕焉，任孰重乎？任之重者責亦重，入而輔相，亦自率其論道之忠，而要非可自侈於臣工也。噫！爲司空而宅百揆，禹也，而祇承於舜。孔于襄王，夫非禹之舜乎？其爲帝臣之分則均矣。爲師傅而位冢宰，周公也，而篤棐於成王。孔于
translation_en:
…In former times, Duke Huan of Qi earnestly sought to honor Zhou and forged ties of friendship through renewed covenants; this was why the assembly at Kuiqiu took place. Minister Kong reverently carried out the king’s command, performing the ceremony of bestowing sacrificial meat; this was why he attended the western assembly [?]. Now, under the rules of the Spring and Autumn Annals, those of exalted status receive separate mention when attending an assembly: the royal heir apparent is a case in point. Kong attended as a minister of the king and should likewise have been among those accorded honor. Why, then, was his attendance not separately distinguished? The gentleman says: “Surely this expresses the Sage’s principle of honoring the king!” For throughout the realm, the Son of Heaven alone is supremely honored. All beneath him are subjects, and all must seek to please him: the lowly must not overstep the exalted. Throughout the realm, the heir apparent alone holds the highest nobility. All beneath him are subjects, and all attend upon the king’s person: the lowly must not encroach upon the noble.

What, then, was Kong’s position in Zhou? As the king’s limbs, he indeed formed one body with the Heavenly King; yet he could not evade the obligation of devoted, respectful service. Entrusted to act as the king’s heart and backbone, he indeed shared one purpose with the Son of Heaven; yet he could not set aside the duty to share in his labors. The hundred officials were brought under his direction, and the lands within the Four Seas were equitably ordered through him. What office could be greater? The greater the office, the greater its responsibilities. When advancing into service, he must think of giving his utmost loyalty, content with his allotted position in the distinction between heaven and marsh [?]; he certainly could not vaunt himself before his ruler and father. Heaven’s work was assisted through him, and the sovereign’s undertakings made to flourish. What charge could be weightier? The weightier the charge, the weightier its responsibilities. Entering court to assist the ruler, he must fulfill his loyalty by discoursing on the Way; he certainly could not exalt himself above his fellow officials.

Ah! It was Yu who, as Minister of Works, presided over the hundred offices, yet reverently served Shun. Was not Kong’s relationship to King Xiang like Yu’s to Shun? Their allotted status as subjects of the sovereign was the same. It was the Duke of Zhou who served as tutor and occupied the office of Chief Minister, yet devotedly assisted King Cheng. title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
襄王夫非周公之成王乎其爲王臣之分則均
矣聖人于其來會也不以世子殊會之文施之
豈不知尊孔哉蓋曰世子君也宰孔臣也臣不
可同于君故名不得殊於會不殊會孔者所以
尊君父也大分其嚴乎抑斯會也豈徒然哉儼
天威之邇不貪後命以爲榮切隕越之羞不忘
降階以循禮桓之霸事偉矣循是心也以進將
王道可幾何佚德遽彰而仲敎以遠略規模亦
僅止此太史公以桓旣賢而不勉之至王爲仲
===
責吾於是乎益信
禮記
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉

襄王，夫非周公之成王乎？其爲王臣之分則均矣。聖人于其來會也，不以世子殊會之文施之，豈不知尊孔哉？蓋曰：世子，君也；宰孔，臣也。臣不可同于君，故名不得殊於會。不殊會孔者，所以尊君父也。大分其嚴乎！抑斯會也，豈徒然哉？儼天威之邇，不貪後命以爲榮；切隕越之羞，不忘降階以循禮。桓之霸事偉矣！循是心也以進，將王道可幾。何佚德遽彰，而仲敎以遠略，規模亦僅止此？太史公以桓旣賢而不勉之至王爲仲責，吾於是乎益信。

translation_en:
…to King Xiang—was this not like the Duke of Zhou’s relationship to King Cheng? Their obligations as servants of the king were the same. When the Sage recorded Kong’s attendance at the meeting, he did not apply the wording that distinguished the heir apparent’s attendance. Could he have failed to understand that Kong deserved honor? His reasoning was this: the heir apparent is a ruler; Minister Kong is a subject. A subject cannot be treated as equal to a ruler, so his name could not receive distinctive treatment in the record of the meeting. Not distinguishing Kong’s attendance served to honor the ruler and father. How strict is this fundamental distinction!
Yet was this meeting without significance? Reverently conscious of the nearness of the Son of Heaven’s majesty, Duke Huan did not covet the honor of receiving the command afterward [?]; keenly ashamed at the prospect of failing in his duty, he did not forget to descend the steps in observance of ritual. Great indeed were Duke Huan’s achievements as hegemon! Had he advanced in this spirit, the Way of the True King might have been within reach. Why, then, did his moral laxity suddenly become manifest, while Guan Zhong instructed him in far-reaching strategies, so that the scope of his undertaking went no further than this? The Grand Historian faulted Guan Zhong for failing to encourage Duke Huan, already a worthy ruler, to attain true kingship. This makes me all the more convinced of that judgment.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
過一和而已孰謂聖人之樂而不肇於造化自
然之和也哉記者知樂之所由作也故爲之言
曰大樂之作也固創其制於聖人而實肇其端
於天地高下散殊人知禮制之行矣孰知樂之
所自來矣乎彼天以元氣溥萬物非徒確然上
浮也於穆之運旋者無停機而自極其循環之
盛地以元形育萬物非徒隤然下凝也神功之
流行者無止息而自妙夫混闢之機運而爲四
時之錯行也一闔一闢交而庶物由之露生焉
===
以敷以受見其竝育而不害也播而爲五氣之
順布也一動一靜交而品彙因之發育焉以煦
以嫗見其竝生而不匱也夫是之謂絪縕化醇
而不容以獨異孰非天地自然之和乎是和也
斂之雖若無聲而一元之周流於冲穆者實有
以涵聲氣之原運之雖若無形而順氣之充盈
於宇宙者實有以肇制作之本音律之相宣人
知聖人心術之流形也而不知所以爲之端者
一造化之宣洩焉洋洋乎氣機摩盪而大樂之
punctuated: 過一和而已，孰謂聖人之樂而不肇於造化自然之和也哉？記者知樂之所由作也，故爲之言曰：大樂之作也，固創其制於聖人，而實肇其端於天地。高下散殊，人知禮制之行矣，孰知樂之所自來矣乎？彼天以元氣溥萬物，非徒確然上浮也；於穆之運旋者無停機，而自極其循環之盛。地以元形育萬物，非徒隤然下凝也；神功之流行者無止息，而自妙夫混闢之機。運而爲四時之錯行也，一闔一闢交，而庶物由之露生焉；以敷以受，見其竝育而不害也。播而爲五氣之順布也，一動一靜交，而品彙因之發育焉；以煦以嫗，見其竝生而不匱也。夫是之謂絪縕化醇，而不容以獨異，孰非天地自然之和乎？是和也，斂之雖若無聲，而一元之周流於冲穆者，實有以涵聲氣之原；運之雖若無形，而順氣之充盈於宇宙者，實有以肇制作之本。音律之相宣，人知聖人心術之流形也，而不知所以爲之端者，一造化之宣洩焉。洋洋乎氣機摩盪，而大樂之
translation_en: …is no more than harmony. Who could say that the sages’ music does not originate in the spontaneous harmony of creation? The author of the Record of Rites understood how music arose, and therefore spoke of it thus: although the institutions of great music were first established by the sages, its beginnings truly originated in Heaven and Earth. Seeing the dispersed distinctions of high and low, people recognize the operation of ritual order; but who understands whence music comes? Heaven extends its primordial qi to all things; it does not merely float firmly above. Its profound and majestic revolutions never pause, and thus bring the fullness of its cycles to completion. Earth nourishes all things through its primordial form; it does not merely lie solidly massed below. The flow of its wondrous workings never ceases, and thus gives marvelous expression to the process of gathering together and opening out. This movement becomes the alternating progression of the four seasons: closing and opening interact, and through them the myriad things emerge into life. Through bestowal and reception, we see them nourished together without harming one another. This diffusion becomes the orderly distribution of the five kinds of qi: movement and stillness interact, and through them the various kinds of beings develop and grow. Through warming and nurturing, we see them living together without exhaustion. This is what is called the close intertwining of cosmic forces, transforming things into fullness, with none standing apart. What in this is not the spontaneous harmony of Heaven and Earth? When gathered inward, this harmony seems soundless; yet the primordial unity circulating in profound tranquility truly contains the source of sound and qi. When set in motion, it seems formless; yet the harmonious qi filling the universe truly provides the foundation for the establishment of musical institutions. As tones and pitch standards give expression to one another, people recognize the outward manifestation of the workings of the sages’ minds. They do not understand that what originates it is wholly an outpouring of creation. Vastly expansive are the mutual stimulation and surging of the forces of qi, and the great music’s…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
精彩於此乎橐籥之矣舞蹈之相成人知聖人
精神之運用也而不知所以為之基者一造化
之洋溢焉雍雍乎協氣嘉生而至樂之英華於
此乎根柢之矣夫以自然之樂情而興於造化
者如此聖人本之以作樂也樂非天地之和也
哉雖然天地聖人一而已矣惟聖人建中和之
極以參賛化育天人交會而淑氣薰蒸和樂興
矣唐虞如日中天堯舜應運而出故簫韶成而
鳳凰儀窮天壤間和氣致祥也世之論樂者求
===
之秬黍尺寸之間抑末矣樂云乎哉
子曰恭近禮儉近仁信近情敬讓以行此
雖有過其不甚矣夫恭寡過情可信儉
易容也以此失之者不亦鮮乎
詹事講
同考試官教諭潘批此題全重成仁過失二字
須要分明此作所云失仁而入於過題意豁然喚醒矣録之
考試官學正吳批詳整明健
考試官教授顧批體裁嚴密詞氣清雅
punctuated:
精彩於此乎橐籥之矣。舞蹈之相成，人知聖人精神之運用也，而不知所以為之基者，一造化之洋溢焉。雍雍乎協氣嘉生，而至樂之英華於此乎根柢之矣。夫以自然之樂情而興於造化者如此，聖人本之以作樂也，樂非天地之和也哉？雖然，天地聖人一而已矣。惟聖人建中和之極，以參賛化育，天人交會，而淑氣薰蒸，和樂興矣。唐虞如日中天，堯舜應運而出，故簫韶成而鳳凰儀，窮天壤間和氣致祥也。世之論樂者，求之秬黍尺寸之間，抑末矣，樂云乎哉？
子曰：「恭近禮，儉近仁，信近情，敬讓以行此，雖有過，其不甚矣。夫恭寡過，情可信，儉易容也。以此失之者，不亦鮮乎？」
詹事講

translation_en:
…the vital brilliance of great music is thus breathed forth as by a bellows. In the mutually complementary movements of dance, people recognize the workings of the sage’s spiritual powers, yet do not understand that their foundation is entirely the overflowing activity of creation. Harmonious indeed: concordant vital energy nurtures flourishing life, and here the finest essence of perfect music takes root. Such is the way that the innate spirit of music arises from creation; the sage draws upon it to make music. Is music not, then, the harmony of Heaven and Earth? Yet Heaven, Earth, and the sage are ultimately one. Only the sage establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, thereby assisting the transforming and nourishing work of creation. Heaven and humanity meet, beneficent vital energy spreads its warmth, and harmonious music arises. The ages of Tang and Yu were like the sun at the zenith: Yao and Shun emerged in response to their destined times. Thus, when the Shao music was completed, phoenixes came in stately attendance: harmonious vital energy throughout Heaven and Earth brought forth auspicious signs. Those of later ages who discuss music and seek it among black millet grains and measurements in inches and feet attend merely to its peripheral details. Can this truly be called music?
The Master said: “Respectfulness approaches ritual propriety; frugality approaches benevolence; trustworthiness approaches sincerity. Practise these with reverence and deference, and even if you commit faults, they will not be serious. Respectfulness brings few faults; sincerity can be trusted; frugality makes one readily acceptable to others. Are not those who go astray through these qualities few indeed?”
Zhan Shijiang 詹事講.
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: This topic places its entire emphasis on the two terms ‘attaining benevolence’ and ‘faults’; these must be clearly distinguished. This composition’s statement that one falls into error after losing benevolence suddenly brings the topic’s meaning vividly to light. Include it in the record.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: Detailed and orderly, lucid and vigorous.
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: The structure is rigorous and closely knit; the language and tone are clear and elegant.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
記者原行仁足以寡過而申著其意焉夫失仁
而後入於過也恭儉信則失之者鮮矣此所以
寡過而成仁也與記者述孔子之意若曰君子
以仁存心非不欲立身於無過之地但人人失
其所好而仁者之過始易辭於天下矣然過之
所以易辭者非矯飾以爲之也以其不甚過耳
蓋禮者心之制也近乎禮則恭而中節矣仁者
心之德也近乎仁則儉而不肆矣信不由衷信
無益也近情則勿之有欺矣集衆善之全而又
===
濟之以敬讓之道由是而之焉外焉可以寡尤
内焉可以寡悔君子慎斯以往故無咎也要之
小德出入雖一時之所不能無然君子而未仁
者容或有之使以細行之故而至爲大德之累
焉吾未之見也過何至於甚乎然過之所以不
甚者非襲取以致之也以其鮮有失爾蓋過常
起於驕恭而有禮過斯寡矣信易流於詐情本
中孚信可復矣侈而無節孰能容之儉則何所
不容也備諸德之美而得乎兼體之益由是而
punctuated: 記者原行仁足以寡過，而申著其意焉。夫失仁而後入於過也，恭儉信則失之者鮮矣，此所以寡過而成仁也與！記者述孔子之意若曰：君子以仁存心，非不欲立身於無過之地，但人人失其所好，而仁者之過始易辭於天下矣。然過之所以易辭者，非矯飾以爲之也，以其不甚過耳。蓋禮者，心之制也；近乎禮，則恭而中節矣。仁者，心之德也；近乎仁，則儉而不肆矣。信不由衷，信無益也；近情，則勿之有欺矣。集衆善之全，而又濟之以敬讓之道，由是而之焉，外焉可以寡尤，内焉可以寡悔。君子慎斯以往，故無咎也。要之，小德出入，雖一時之所不能無，然君子而未仁者，容或有之；使以細行之故，而至爲大德之累焉，吾未之見也。過何至於甚乎？然過之所以不甚者，非襲取以致之也，以其鮮有失爾。蓋過常起於驕，恭而有禮，過斯寡矣。信易流於詐，情本中孚，信可復矣。侈而無節，孰能容之？儉則何所不容也？備諸德之美，而得乎兼體之益，由是而
translation_en:
The recorder traces how practicing benevolence suffices to reduce faults and further elucidates its meaning. Only after departing from benevolence does one fall into error. Those who are respectful, frugal, and trustworthy seldom go astray. Is this not how one reduces faults and achieves benevolence? The recorder presents Confucius’s meaning as though saying: The gentleman preserves benevolence in his heart; it is certainly his desire to establish himself where he is free from faults. Yet everyone errs through what he favors, and the faults of a benevolent person can readily be excused before the world. Such faults are readily excused not because he contrives to disguise them, but because they are not very serious.

Ritual propriety is the regulating principle of the heart. When respect approaches ritual propriety, it accords with the proper measure. Benevolence is the virtue of the heart. When frugality approaches benevolence, it is free from self-indulgence. If trustworthiness does not come from within, it is of no benefit; when it accords with genuine feeling, there is no deception [?]. Gathering the full complement of good qualities and further supporting them with reverence and deference, one proceeds accordingly: outwardly one can incur less blame, and inwardly one can have fewer regrets. The gentleman proceeds with care in these matters and thus remains without culpability. In sum, although occasional deviations in minor virtues cannot be entirely avoided, and there may indeed be gentlemen who have not attained benevolence, I have never seen minor shortcomings of conduct become an encumbrance upon their greater virtue. How could their faults become serious?

Yet their faults are not slight because they have attained this condition by merely borrowing an outward form of virtue, but because they seldom go astray. Faults commonly arise from arrogance: with respect governed by ritual propriety, faults become few. Trustworthiness can easily degenerate into deceit; when genuine feeling is rooted in inward sincerity, one’s pledged word can be fulfilled. Who can tolerate extravagance without restraint? But where would frugality not be tolerated? Possessing the excellence of all these virtues and gaining the benefit of embodying them together, proceeding accordingly …
