同考試官教諭廖批 聖人與天為一只是無私
punctuated:
之焉，措之則無不正，施之則無不行。君子修此三者，故全也。要之，無心失理，雖人情之所不能免，然苟志於仁，則無惡矣。使以進德之心而復有悖德之愆，吾見亦罕也。夫其有不鮮乎？夫失而曰鮮，此仁者之過所以不甚也；過而曰不甚，此仁者之過所以易辭也。噫！聖人成仁之心甚殷矣！有志求仁者，亦自寡過始。抑論仁之難成久矣，聖人恐其引天下而入於畏，不敢必其安仁，而望之以勉仁，故以辭過歸仁者。聖如周孔，監殷諱君，人且訾之矣。觀過知仁之論，聖人原心之法也。雖然，寡過者仁之驗，改過者仁之功。不遠之復，顏氏所以稱庶幾也。安得不貳過者，與之語成仁之學？

第貳場

論

王者奉若天道

孫希夔

同考試官教諭廖批：聖人與天為一，只是無私。
translation_en:
…proceed in this way: whatever one undertakes will be correct, and whatever one puts into practice will succeed. The gentleman cultivates these three qualities and thus becomes complete. In sum, although inadvertent departures from principle are unavoidable in human life, if one sets one’s purpose on benevolence, one will do no evil. Those who, while intent on advancing in virtue, nevertheless commit offenses against virtue are also seldom seen. Could such failings be anything but few? That lapses are described as few explains why the faults of the benevolent are not serious; that their faults are described as not serious explains why they can readily be excused. Ah! How earnest is the sage’s desire that people attain benevolence! Those resolved to seek benevolence should likewise begin by reducing their faults. Yet the difficulty of attaining benevolence has long been discussed. The sage feared that this would lead everyone into apprehension. He dared not insist that they rest naturally in benevolence, but hoped that they would strive toward it. Thus he accorded the benevolent the benefit of having their faults excused. Even sages such as the Duke of Zhou and Confucius were criticized for taking Yin as a mirror and concealing a ruler’s faults [?]. The teaching that one can recognize benevolence by observing faults is the sage’s method of examining the underlying intentions. Nevertheless, having few faults is evidence of benevolence; correcting faults is the work of benevolence. Returning before straying far is why Yan Hui was said to have nearly attained it. Where can I find someone who never repeats a fault, with whom to discuss the learning by which benevolence is attained?

Second Session

Discourse

The King Reverently Follows the Way of Heaven

Sun Xikui

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: The sage is one with Heaven simply because he is free of selfishness.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
此作體認真切非有養者不能
考試官學正吳批議論雄渾發天道王道之
蘊殆盡
考試官敎授顧批發明王道同天之大甚悉
末復證以孔子春秋尤爲有見
論曰王道與天道一也王者以其心公天下而
已不與焉惟求端於天而已矣夫天何心也體
萬物皷氣機以順成之無心也王者奉天以出
治隨萬事而順應之其道與天合亦無心也天
===
惟無心故天下之物各取足於天之化而忘乎
其爲天王者惟無心故天下之人囿乎王者之
化而莫知爲之者猶之天也奚有所庸心於其
間哉是其端本于一心而至公達之天下王者
之心卽天之心而憲天之政配天之業斯其至
矣此王道之所以爲大與天合一豈若霸功之
小小者然哉今夫天函於太一混然而已矣及
分爲陰陽播於四時陽以舒之爲雨露爲風霆
而煦嫗覆育行焉斯萬物以生以長陰以慘之
punctuated:
此作體認真切，非有養者不能。
考試官學正吳批：議論雄渾，發天道、王道之蘊殆盡。
考試官敎授顧批：發明王道同天之大甚悉，末復證以孔子《春秋》，尤爲有見。
論曰：王道與天道一也。王者以其心公天下而已不與焉，惟求端於天而已矣。夫天何心也？體萬物，皷氣機，以順成之，無心也。王者奉天以出治，隨萬事而順應之，其道與天合，亦無心也。天惟無心，故天下之物各取足於天之化，而忘乎其爲天。王者惟無心，故天下之人囿乎王者之化，而莫知爲之者，猶之天也。奚有所庸心於其間哉？是其端本于一心，而至公達之天下。王者之心卽天之心，而憲天之政、配天之業，斯其至矣。此王道之所以爲大，與天合一，豈若霸功之小小者然哉？今夫天函於太一，混然而已矣。及分爲陰陽，播於四時，陽以舒之，爲雨露，爲風霆，而煦嫗覆育行焉，斯萬物以生以長；陰以慘之，
translation_en:
…This composition grasps the principle truly and keenly; only someone who has cultivated himself could achieve this.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: The argument is powerful and comprehensive, bringing out almost fully the underlying meaning of the Way of Heaven and the kingly Way.

Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: It explains in great detail the greatness that the kingly Way shares with Heaven. Its concluding appeal to Confucius’s Spring and Autumn Annals as further evidence is especially perceptive.

The discourse reads: The kingly Way and the Way of Heaven are one. The true king makes his mind impartial toward all under Heaven, without involving his private self [?], seeking its guiding principle only in Heaven. What deliberate intention does Heaven have? It embodies the myriad things and sets the workings of vital energy in motion, bringing them to fulfillment in accordance with their nature: it acts without deliberate intention. The king reverently follows Heaven in administering government, responding appropriately to the myriad affairs as they arise. His Way accords with Heaven, and he too acts without deliberate intention. Precisely because Heaven acts without deliberate intention, all things under Heaven find their full sufficiency in its transforming influence and forget that it is Heaven. Precisely because the king acts without deliberate intention, all people under Heaven dwell within his transforming influence without knowing who brings it about. He is just like Heaven. What need is there to interpose deliberate intention? This takes its origin in the single mind, and its supreme impartiality extends throughout all under Heaven. The king’s mind is Heaven’s mind; government that models itself on Heaven and achievements that match Heaven reach their utmost here. This is why the kingly Way is great and forms one unity with Heaven. How could it resemble the petty achievements of a hegemon?

Now Heaven is encompassed within the Supreme One, simply an undifferentiated whole. When it divides into yin and yang and spreads through the four seasons, yang causes things to unfold, becoming rain and dew, wind and thunder. Its warming, nurturing, sheltering, and fostering activity takes effect, and thus the myriad things are born and grow. Yin subjects them to severity…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
為隕霜為堅氷而嚴凝肅殺行焉斯萬物以收
以藏此固天之所以為天未甞私覆也主宰而
不居運行而不息渾淪溥博莫知其始孰究其
終何有心於物而為之耶而天下之物生者長
者收藏者咸各足其分願保合太和而天之化
於是乎不可測矣王者繼天立極而為天之子
固以父母天下為王道而代之以理物則凡天
下之親疎遠邇貴賤智愚賢不肖與夫蠢而動
者莫不紛然以聽令於我使役吾心之私智操
===
天下而束縛之馳驟之其誰與我王者事天如
事親善繼其志善述其事舉天下之大而治之
以天道是故煦嫗覆育天之盛德氣也仁也王
者奉之而温厚之政行焉故有賞以飾喜矣嚴
凝肅殺天之明威也義也王者奉之而奮厲之
政行焉故有罰以飾怒矣其喜也喜乎其所當
喜也其怒也怒乎其所不得不怒也然懼其或失
之僭而濫也則取必於國人之皆賢而後用之
國人皆可殺而後刑之猶不敢輕以自用也則
punctuated: 為隕霜，為堅氷，而嚴凝肅殺行焉，斯萬物以收以藏。此固天之所以為天，未甞私覆也。主宰而不居，運行而不息，渾淪溥博，莫知其始，孰究其終？何有心於物而為之耶？而天下之物，生者、長者、收藏者，咸各足其分願，保合太和，而天之化於是乎不可測矣。王者繼天立極，而為天之子，固以父母天下為王道，而代之以理物。則凡天下之親疎遠邇、貴賤智愚、賢不肖，與夫蠢而動者，莫不紛然以聽令於我。使役吾心之私智，操天下而束縛之、馳驟之，其誰與我？王者事天如事親，善繼其志，善述其事，舉天下之大而治之以天道。是故煦嫗覆育，天之盛德氣也，仁也；王者奉之，而温厚之政行焉，故有賞以飾喜矣。嚴凝肅殺，天之明威也，義也；王者奉之，而奮厲之政行焉，故有罰以飾怒矣。其喜也，喜乎其所當喜也；其怒也，怒乎其所不得不怒也。然懼其或失之僭而濫也，則取必於國人之皆賢而後用之，國人皆可殺而後刑之。猶不敢輕以自用也，則
translation_en:
…producing falling frost and solid ice, and bringing into operation stern cold and killing severity; thus the myriad things are gathered in and stored away. This is indeed what makes Heaven Heaven: it has never bestowed its shelter with partiality. It presides without claiming credit and moves without ceasing, undivided, all-embracing, and vast. None knows its beginning; who can fathom its end? How could it act upon things with deliberate intent? Yet all things under Heaven—those that come to life, those that grow, and those that are gathered in and stored away—each find fulfillment in their allotted condition and aspirations, preserving and uniting in Supreme Harmony. Thus Heaven’s transforming influence is unfathomable.

The king succeeds Heaven in establishing the supreme standard and becomes the Son of Heaven. He therefore takes being father and mother to all under Heaven as the kingly Way, ordering things on Heaven’s behalf. All under Heaven—close and distant relations, those far and near, noble and humble, wise and foolish, worthy and unworthy, together with all creeping, moving creatures—come in their multitudes to heed my commands. Were I to employ my mind’s private cleverness to control all under Heaven, binding them and driving them hither and thither, who would stand with me? The king serves Heaven as he serves his parents, skillfully carrying forward its intentions and continuing its work. He takes all the vast realm and governs it by Heaven’s Way.

Thus warming, nurturing, sheltering, and sustaining are the vital force of Heaven’s abundant virtue: they are benevolence. The king follows this, and policies of warmth and generosity take effect; hence there are rewards to give expression to joy. Stern cold and killing severity are Heaven’s manifest awe-inspiring power: they are righteousness. The king follows this, and vigorous, stern policies take effect; hence there are punishments to give expression to anger. His joy is joy at what ought to occasion joy; his anger is anger at what he cannot but be angry at. Yet, fearing that he might err through unwarranted favor or excessive punishment, he insists that all the people of the state deem a person worthy before employing him, and that all deem a person deserving of death before punishing him. Still he does not dare lightly to act on his own judgment, and so…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
爵於朝而與眾共之刑於市而與眾棄之然豈
王者自任其賞罰而不奉天之時令也哉稽之
禮凡歲迎春於東郊也賞公卿大夫於朝行慶
於野至於萌芽毋折胎卵不殰以𠇗一陽舒之
仁焉其施禁令於秋冬也誅暴慢嚴斷刑祭禽
伐薪一陰慘之義焉然仁可過而義不可過故
陽常居大夏而以發育長養為事陰常居大冬
而置於空虛不用之地王者善善之速而惡惡
之緩猶之天也是其所居者天位所治者天民
===
命曰天命討曰天討始也天以陰陽鼓萬物而
以賞罰之權寄於王者繼而王者承天之權以
賞罰乎天下終而天下亦各自以其所賞罰者
而忘其所為賞罰善積而必彰惡積而必癉凡
為親疎者遠邇者貴賤者智愚賢不肖與夫蠢
而動者莫不自易其惡自至其中各遂其欲無
相假借各安於化不相陵躐此王道之合於天
也天以其心普萬物而無心王者以其情順萬
事而無情感之者無心而應之者亦無心帝則
punctuated: 爵於朝而與眾共之，刑於市而與眾棄之。然豈王者自任其賞罰，而不奉天之時令也哉？稽之禮，凡歲迎春於東郊也，賞公卿大夫於朝，行慶於野，至於萌芽毋折，胎卵不殰，以𠇗一陽舒之仁焉。其施禁令於秋冬也，誅暴慢，嚴斷刑，祭禽伐薪，一陰慘之義焉。然仁可過而義不可過，故陽常居大夏而以發育長養為事，陰常居大冬而置於空虛不用之地。王者善善之速而惡惡之緩，猶之天也。是其所居者天位，所治者天民，命曰天命，討曰天討。始也，天以陰陽鼓萬物，而以賞罰之權寄於王者；繼而王者承天之權，以賞罰乎天下；終而天下亦各自以其所賞罰者，而忘其所為賞罰。善積而必彰，惡積而必癉。凡為親疎者、遠邇者、貴賤者、智愚賢不肖，與夫蠢而動者，莫不自易其惡，自至其中，各遂其欲，無相假借，各安於化，不相陵躐。此王道之合於天也。天以其心普萬物而無心，王者以其情順萬事而無情。感之者無心，而應之者亦無心。帝則
translation_en:
…he confers ranks at court, sharing their bestowal with the multitude, and carries out punishments in the marketplace, joining the multitude in rejecting the condemned. Yet could the king exercise rewards and punishments on his own authority without observing Heaven’s seasonal ordinances? Examining the ritual prescriptions, we find that each year, when spring is welcomed in the eastern suburbs, he rewards the dukes, ministers, and grand masters at court and bestows favors in the countryside. Even sprouts must not be broken off, nor unborn creatures and eggs destroyed: thereby [an unclear phrase, 𠇗一] expressing the benevolence of yang’s unfolding. When he promulgates prohibitions in autumn and winter, he punishes the violent and negligent and rigorously adjudicates punishments; the offering of birds in sacrifice and the cutting of firewood likewise embody [?] the righteousness of yin’s severity. Yet benevolence may exceed its measure, whereas righteousness must not. Thus yang regularly occupies high summer and devotes itself to generation, growth, and nourishment, while yin regularly occupies deep winter and is relegated to a vacant realm where it is not put to use. The king’s swiftness in honoring the good and slowness in condemning the wicked likewise follow Heaven. The position he occupies is Heaven’s position; the people he governs are Heaven’s people. His commands are called Heaven’s commands, and his punitive actions Heaven’s punitive actions.

At the outset, Heaven animates the myriad things through yin and yang and entrusts the authority to reward and punish to the king. The king then receives Heaven’s authority and uses it to reward and punish all under Heaven. Finally, all under Heaven, each through that for which they are rewarded or punished, come to forget the rewards and punishments themselves. Accumulated goodness is certain to be made manifest; accumulated evil is certain to meet punishment. Whether close or distant in kinship, far or near in location, noble or lowly, wise or foolish, worthy or unworthy—even the creatures that stir and move—all spontaneously reform their faults and attain their proper mean. Each fulfills its desires without borrowing from the others; each rests content within the transforming influence, without encroaching upon or overstepping the others. This is how the kingly Way accords with Heaven.

Heaven extends its mind throughout the myriad things yet has no deliberate intent; the king accords with the myriad affairs through his feelings yet has no partial feelings. That which moves others has no deliberate intent, and those that respond likewise have no deliberate intent. The sovereign’s rule…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
順焉帝力忘焉殆若雨露之施而萬物不知其
爲潤凄風隕霜而歸根復命者亦相忘之矣此
王道之大異乎霸功之小其辨不越於公私之
間而已孟子曰王者之民皞皞如也霸者之民
驩虞如也蓋造端於心術之微而徵於斯民之
氣象王則公霸則私公則天私則人其間不容
一髮而相去豈不遼絶哉是道也稽古帝王曆
數禪受元愷並舉爲懋官爲延賞彤弓之錫圭
瓚之釐是賞賞以天也戰涿鹿誅四凶爲胤征
===
===
爲伐崇南巢之放東山之討是罰罰以天也唐
虞三代之治行王道而王無有所謂霸者逮周
東遷王者迹熄平桓以來不能以其教令而賞
罰天下孔子志行周道故不得不假二百四十
二年南面之權繫王於天而奉天道以賞罰天
下之諸侯有德必褒而善者勸有罪必貶而惡
者懲邵子以爲聖人之刑書者是也當是時也
桓文之功可謂盛矣然召陵盟而濤塗見執君
子謂其濫矣陽穀會而侵衛不救君子謂其荒
punctuated: 順焉，帝力忘焉，殆若雨露之施，而萬物不知其爲潤；凄風隕霜，而歸根復命者亦相忘之矣。此王道之大異乎霸功之小，其辨不越於公私之間而已。孟子曰：「王者之民皞皞如也，霸者之民驩虞如也。」蓋造端於心術之微，而徵於斯民之氣象。王則公，霸則私；公則天，私則人。其間不容一髮，而相去豈不遼絶哉！是道也，稽古帝王，曆數禪受，元愷並舉，爲懋官，爲延賞，彤弓之錫，圭瓚之釐，是賞，賞以天也。戰涿鹿，誅四凶，爲胤征，爲伐崇，南巢之放，東山之討，是罰，罰以天也。唐虞三代之治，行王道而王，無有所謂霸者。逮周東遷，王者迹熄，平桓以來，不能以其教令而賞罰天下。孔子志行周道，故不得不假二百四十二年南面之權，繫王於天，而奉天道以賞罰天下之諸侯。有德必褒，而善者勸；有罪必貶，而惡者懲。邵子以爲聖人之刑書者，是也。當是時也，桓文之功可謂盛矣。然召陵盟而濤塗見執，君子謂其濫矣；陽穀會而侵衛不救，君子謂其荒
translation_en:
…is followed, while the sovereign’s power is forgotten. It is much like the bestowal of rain and dew: the myriad things do not know what moistens them. When chill winds blow and frost falls, those that return to their roots and fulfill their allotted course likewise forget the agency behind it. This is the difference between the greatness of the kingly Way and the smallness of hegemonic achievement. The distinction amounts simply to that between impartiality and private interest. Mengzi said: “The people of a true king are at ease; the people of a hegemon are full of delight.” The difference originates in the subtle workings of the heart and manifests itself in the disposition of the people. True kingship is impartial; hegemony serves private interests. Impartiality accords with Heaven; private interest proceeds from human contrivance. The initial distinction admits not even a hair’s breadth, yet how vast the eventual distance between them!

To examine this Way among the ancient emperors and kings: the succession of Heaven’s mandate and its transfer through abdication; the joint promotion of the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai; rewarding merit with office and extending rewards; the bestowal of vermilion bows and the grant of jade-handled libation ladles—these were rewards, bestowed in accordance with Heaven. The battle at Zhuolu, the punishment of the Four Evildoers, the expedition of Yin, the attack on Chong, the banishment to Nanchao, and the campaign in the eastern hills—these were punishments, inflicted in accordance with Heaven. Under the rule of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, rulers practiced the kingly Way and thereby ruled as true kings; there were no so-called hegemons.

When the Zhou moved east, the vestiges of true kingship died out. From Kings Ping and Huan onward, the kings could no longer reward and punish all under Heaven through their teachings and commands. Confucius aspired to put the Way of Zhou into practice. Thus he had no choice but to assume, in his account of 242 years, the authority of a south-facing sovereign, linking kingship to Heaven and upholding Heaven’s Way to reward and punish the feudal lords throughout the realm. Those with virtue were invariably praised, encouraging the good; those guilty of wrongdoing were invariably censured, chastening the wicked. This is what Master Shao called the sage’s book of punishments.

At that time, the achievements of Duke Huan and Duke Wen could indeed be called magnificent. Yet at the covenant of Shaoling, Tao Tu was seized, which the gentleman judged excessive. At the meeting at Yanggu, Wei was invaded and no aid was given [?], which the gentleman judged neglectful…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣桓且不免於聖人之譏曹衛侵伐而忿慾滋
城濮請戰而狙詐事文之譎奚足論焉此覇者
之心惟知飾其智巧以濟其私而欺乎人未若
王者之行所無事故其盟會侵伐誅執無一出
於天理之公固難逃乎誅心之典矣吾夫子雖
不得位而奉天之道以伸其大公於天下後世
其心即堯舜禹湯之心也孟子以春秋為天子
之事非獨觀其深也哉程子善學孔孟者而於
王覇之辨公私幾微之際審矣雖然王道固與
===
天合也易之乾象曰天行健君子以自強不息
蓋言聖人得天位行天道以致咸寧之治然必
本以學問之功存以乾乾惕厲之心極於閑邪
存誠之精此至德淵微而達之王道者故曰有
天德可以語王道乃程子互發之旨由程子而
益知聖人以天道自處著於易而備於春秋也
是為論
同前
萬邦獻
punctuated:
矣。桓且不免於聖人之譏，曹衛侵伐而忿慾滋，城濮請戰而狙詐事，文之譎奚足論焉？此覇者之心，惟知飾其智巧以濟其私而欺乎人，未若王者之行所無事。故其盟會侵伐誅執，無一出於天理之公，固難逃乎誅心之典矣。吾夫子雖不得位，而奉天之道，以伸其大公於天下後世，其心即堯舜禹湯之心也。孟子以《春秋》為天子之事，非獨觀其深也哉？程子善學孔孟者，而於王覇之辨、公私幾微之際審矣。雖然，王道固與天合也。《易》之乾象曰：「天行健，君子以自強不息。」蓋言聖人得天位，行天道，以致咸寧之治，然必本以學問之功，存以乾乾惕厲之心，極於閑邪存誠之精。此至德淵微而達之王道者，故曰：「有天德，可以語王道。」乃程子互發之旨。由程子而益知聖人以天道自處，著於《易》而備於《春秋》也。是為論。
同前。
萬邦獻。
translation_en:
…indeed. Even Duke Huan could not escape the Sage’s censure. In invading Cao and Wei, anger and desire grew unchecked; in requesting battle at Chengpu, cunning and deception were employed [?]. What more need be said of Duke Wen’s duplicity? The hegemon’s mind knows only how to embellish its clever schemes to serve private interests and deceive others. It falls short of the true king’s conduct, which proceeds without contrivance. Thus, among the hegemon’s covenants, assemblies, invasions, attacks, executions, and arrests, not one sprang from the impartiality of Heaven’s principle. Such conduct could hardly escape the canon that condemns underlying intentions.
Although our Master did not obtain the throne, he upheld Heaven’s Way, extending its supreme impartiality throughout the world and to later generations. His mind was precisely the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang. When Mengzi called the Spring and Autumn Annals the business of the Son of Heaven, was his insight not exceptionally profound? Master Cheng was skilled in learning from Confucius and Mengzi, and discerned clearly the distinction between kingship and hegemony and the subtlest boundary between impartiality and self-interest.
Nevertheless, the kingly Way is inherently in accord with Heaven. The Image commentary on the Qian hexagram in the Book of Changes says: “Heaven’s movement is vigorous; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without cease.” This means that the Sage obtains Heaven’s position and practices Heaven’s Way, thereby bringing about a government under which all enjoy peace. Yet this must be rooted in the work of learning and inquiry, sustained by a mind of unremitting diligence and vigilant caution, and brought to perfection in warding off evil and preserving sincerity. This is supreme virtue, profound and subtle, finding expression in the kingly Way. Hence the saying: “With Heaven’s virtue, one may speak of the kingly Way.” This is Master Cheng’s meaning in explaining each through the other. Through Master Cheng, we understand still better that the Sage’s taking Heaven’s Way as the standard for his own conduct is made manifest in the Book of Changes and fully expressed in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Thus concludes the discourse.
Same as the preceding.
Wan Bangxian.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批作此類多浮泛詞博而義
精未有踰此篇者
同考試官教諭陳批此作以賞罰立論理明詞
透深得本題肯綮
考試官學正吳批詞理精切意味深長
考試官教授顧批氣昌意婉
聖人之治天下憲天而已矣而己不與焉天之
道無私者也天以其無私覆萬物陰陽舒慘各
得其宜而天下萬物安于天之化而莫知其功
===
聖人者法天之無私以治天下生殺予奪莫非
陰陽自然之理是故慶賞焉而不以為恩刑戮
焉而不以為威天下囿于聖人之道而不知有
法聖人明乎天之道而不知有己是天王也一
或以己私與之即與天道不相似矣而豈所以
語王道乎程子曰王者奉若天道動無非天者
又曰盡天道者王道也嗚呼其亦洞觀乎治理
之本而深嚴王霸之辨者歟今夫天何為者也
一氣混沌萬有未分浮于沖漠為物之祖凡象
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：作此類多浮泛，詞博而義精，未有踰此篇者。
同考試官教諭陳批：此作以賞罰立論，理明詞透，深得本題肯綮。
考試官學正吳批：詞理精切，意味深長。
考試官教授顧批：氣昌意婉。
聖人之治天下，憲天而已矣，而己不與焉。天之道，無私者也。天以其無私覆萬物，陰陽舒慘，各得其宜，而天下萬物安于天之化，而莫知其功。聖人者，法天之無私以治天下，生殺予奪，莫非陰陽自然之理。是故慶賞焉，而不以為恩；刑戮焉，而不以為威。天下囿于聖人之道，而不知有法；聖人明乎天之道，而不知有己。是天王也。一或以己私與之，即與天道不相似矣，而豈所以語王道乎？程子曰：「王者奉若天道，動無非天者。」又曰：「盡天道者，王道也。」嗚呼！其亦洞觀乎治理之本，而深嚴王霸之辨者歟！今夫天何為者也？一氣混沌，萬有未分，浮于沖漠，為物之祖。凡象
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Compositions of this kind are mostly superficial and vague. For breadth of expression and precision of meaning, none surpasses this essay.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “This essay builds its argument upon rewards and punishments. Its reasoning is clear and its expression lucid; it penetrates deeply to the crux of the topic.”
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: “The expression and reasoning are precise and pertinent, and the implications profound and enduring.”
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: “Its spirit is vigorous and its thought subtly expressed.”
In governing All-under-Heaven, the sage does no more than take Heaven as his model, without allowing his own self to intervene. Heaven’s Way is impartial. Through its impartiality, Heaven shelters the myriad things; the genial and stern workings of yin and yang each find their proper application. Thus the myriad things under Heaven rest secure in its transforming influence, without knowing its achievement. The sage models himself upon Heaven’s impartiality in governing All-under-Heaven. Giving life and taking it, granting and withdrawing—all accord with the spontaneous principles of yin and yang. Hence he bestows honors and rewards without regarding them as personal favors, and imposes punishments and executions without regarding them as displays of his might. All-under-Heaven is encompassed within the sage’s Way, without being conscious of laws; the sage understands Heaven’s Way, without being conscious of himself. Such is a king who embodies Heaven. If he once allows his private interests to intervene, he ceases to accord with Heaven’s Way. How, then, could one speak of the Kingly Way? Master Cheng said: “The king reverently follows Heaven’s Way; none of his actions fails to accord with Heaven.” He also said: “Fully realizing Heaven’s Way is the Kingly Way.” Ah! Did he not see thoroughly into the foundations of government and draw a deeply considered and strict distinction between kingship and hegemony? Now, what does Heaven do? A single vital force, undifferentiated, before the myriad beings have separated, floats in emptiness and stillness and is the progenitor of things. All forms …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
息蠕動根著之類莫不藉以肇端蓁蓁芼芼紛
然待命而其化不能一律齊是故不孚甲則不
長嬴不長嬴則不斂藏不斂藏則不凝結不凝
結則不發生有宜于蕃育而蕃育者有宜于夭
折而夭折者物之情也天何心哉故言天道者
不過曰陰與陽陽之舒也道在生殖陰之慘也
道在肅殺一氣闔闢變化無端經而四時運而
五行布而七政少陽見春物始孚甲太陽見夏
物始長嬴少陰見秋物始斂藏太陰見冬物始
===
===
凝結各司其命以生殺萬物物亦熙熙然竝育
于太和之中無假借無侵奪蓋天道無私不言
而化成也王者承天命而爲之子以君長萬民
豈不欲與斯世斯民相忘於太平之治哉顧民
之不能齊亦猶物之蕃育夭折而勢之不可齊
者是故風氣有剛柔而五方異宜矣生質有强
弱而羣生異稟矣以異宜之氣加之以異稟之
習則知愚賢不肖出而善惡異類矣善則順天
而必福之惡則戾天而必禍之而吉凶之形判
punctuated:
息蠕動根著之類，莫不藉以肇端。蓁蓁芼芼，紛然待命，而其化不能一律齊。是故不孚甲則不長嬴，不長嬴則不斂藏，不斂藏則不凝結，不凝結則不發生。有宜于蕃育而蕃育者，有宜于夭折而夭折者，物之情也，天何心哉？故言天道者，不過曰陰與陽。陽之舒也，道在生殖；陰之慘也，道在肅殺。一氣闔闢，變化無端，經而四時，運而五行，布而七政。少陽見春，物始孚甲；太陽見夏，物始長嬴；少陰見秋，物始斂藏；太陰見冬，物始凝結。各司其命，以生殺萬物。物亦熙熙然竝育于太和之中，無假借，無侵奪。蓋天道無私，不言而化成也。
王者承天命而爲之子，以君長萬民，豈不欲與斯世斯民相忘於太平之治哉？顧民之不能齊，亦猶物之蕃育夭折，而勢之不可齊者。是故風氣有剛柔，而五方異宜矣；生質有强弱，而羣生異稟矣。以異宜之氣，加之以異稟之習，則知愚賢不肖出，而善惡異類矣。善則順天而必福之，惡則戾天而必禍之，而吉凶之形判
translation_en:
…all kinds that breathe, crawl, or take root depend upon it for their beginnings. Luxuriant and abundant, they await their allotted destinies in their multitudes, yet their transformations cannot follow one uniform pattern. Thus, without first breaking through their seed coverings, they cannot grow to fullness; without growing to fullness, they cannot gather in and store away; without gathering in and storing away, they cannot congeal; and without congealing, they cannot sprout and grow anew. Some are suited to flourishing and multiplying, and flourish and multiply; others are suited to dying prematurely, and die prematurely. Such is the nature of things. What deliberate intention does Heaven have? Thus, those who speak of the Way of Heaven speak of nothing beyond yin and yang. In yang’s unfolding, the Way lies in generation and growth; in yin’s severity, the Way lies in cutting down and killing. The single vital force closes and opens, transforming without limit: ordered, it forms the four seasons; circulating, the Five Phases; arrayed, the seven celestial regulators—the sun, moon, and five planets. Lesser yang manifests in spring, and things begin to break through their seed coverings; greater yang manifests in summer, and things begin to grow to fullness; lesser yin manifests in autumn, and things begin to gather in and store away; greater yin manifests in winter, and things begin to congeal. Each carries out its allotted charge, giving life to and killing the myriad things. Things, too, flourish joyfully together within this Great Harmony, without special indulgence or encroachment and deprivation. For the Way of Heaven is impartial: without speaking, it brings transformation to completion.
The king receives Heaven’s mandate and becomes its son, thereby ruling over the myriad people. Would he not wish to dwell with this world and its people in such peaceful order that each forgets the other? Yet the impossibility of making the people uniform is like the flourishing or premature death of things: their circumstances cannot be made uniform. Thus, climatic influences differ in hardness and softness, and conditions suited to life differ among the five regions; inborn constitutions differ in strength and weakness, and living beings receive different endowments. When the influences of differing local conditions are compounded by habits arising from differing endowments, distinctions between the wise and foolish, the worthy and unworthy emerge, and good and evil form distinct categories. Those who are good accord with Heaven, and Heaven must bless them; those who are evil oppose Heaven, and Heaven must bring calamity upon them. Thus the forms of good and ill fortune become distinct…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣天之禍福乎民也力之能及者天自爲之而
力所不能逮者又以其生殺予奪之權寄諸王
天下之聖人俾之立法定制用其賢者知者曲
成之以盡其善復以祛天下之邪惡而置之於
理此刑賞所由立也然善一而大小殊造惡一
而輕重異等度德論功原情定罪此五服五章
五刑五用所由分也是法也付于王者而王者
不能徇其情行于天下而天下不能測其用斟
酌劑量協于則焉民之情也天之經也一或不
===
===
順而私喜私惡于其間則賞僭刑濫其弊將至
無所勸懲人心乖而天道失矣嗚呼此豈王天
下之道哉聖人者憲天聰明不敢肆其臆見逞
其私知以拂天下故位曰天王典曰天敘禮曰
天秩政教號令率應天而時行之春令行于青
陽則勸農發粟繁芽恤幼諸政舉焉夏令行于
明堂則薄刑出囚治水脩塗諸政舉焉秋令行
于總章則簡兵詰暴脩法繕獄諸政舉焉冬令
行于玄堂則葺城固疆備邊築塞諸政舉焉而
punctuated:
矣。天之禍福乎民也，力之能及者，天自爲之；而力所不能逮者，又以其生殺予奪之權寄諸王天下之聖人，俾之立法定制，用其賢者知者，曲成之以盡其善，復以祛天下之邪惡而置之於理。此刑賞所由立也。然善一而大小殊造，惡一而輕重異等。度德論功，原情定罪，此五服五章、五刑五用所由分也。是法也，付于王者，而王者不能徇其情；行于天下，而天下不能測其用。斟酌劑量，協于則焉，民之情也，天之經也。一或不順，而私喜私惡于其間，則賞僭刑濫，其弊將至無所勸懲，人心乖而天道失矣。嗚呼！此豈王天下之道哉？

聖人者，憲天聰明，不敢肆其臆見、逞其私知以拂天下。故位曰天王，典曰天敘，禮曰天秩。政教號令，率應天而時行之。春令行于青陽，則勸農發粟、繁芽恤幼諸政舉焉；夏令行于明堂，則薄刑出囚、治水脩塗諸政舉焉；秋令行于總章，則簡兵詰暴、脩法繕獄諸政舉焉；冬令行于玄堂，則葺城固疆、備邊築塞諸政舉焉。而
translation_en:
…Thus it is. When Heaven brings calamity or blessing upon the people, it acts itself in matters within its power. In matters beyond its power, it entrusts its authority over life and death, giving and taking away, to the sage who rules All-under-Heaven. It has him establish laws and institutions and employ the worthy and wise, bringing them to fulfillment in ways suited to each so that their goodness may be fully realized, while also eliminating wickedness throughout the realm and bringing it under justice. This is the origin of punishments and rewards. Yet although goodness is one, achievements in it differ in magnitude; although evil is one, its degrees differ in gravity. Virtue is assessed and merit weighed; circumstances are examined and guilt determined. Hence the distinctions among the five grades of robes with their five kinds of insignia, and among the five punishments with their five applications. These laws are entrusted to the ruler, yet he may not indulge his personal feelings; they operate throughout All-under-Heaven, yet the people cannot fathom their application. Deliberation and careful weighing bring them into accord with the proper standard: this accords with human feelings and is Heaven’s constant principle. If there is any departure from this, and personal likes and dislikes intrude, rewards become excessive and punishments indiscriminate. The resulting abuses will eventually leave no means of encouraging good or deterring evil; human hearts will go astray, and Heaven’s Way will be lost. Alas! Can this be the way to rule All-under-Heaven?

The sage models himself upon Heaven’s clear hearing and sight. He dares not give free rein to his conjectures or flaunt his private understanding in defiance of All-under-Heaven. Thus his position is called “Heavenly King”; the established norms are called “Heaven’s ordering”; and ritual is called “Heaven’s ranking.” Government, instruction, proclamations, and commands all respond to Heaven and are carried out at the proper seasons. When the spring ordinances are implemented in Qingyang, the Azure Yang Hall, measures are undertaken to encourage agriculture, distribute grain, foster sprouting growth [?], and care for the young. When the summer ordinances are implemented in Mingtang, the Hall of Light, measures are undertaken to mitigate punishments, release prisoners, regulate waterways, and repair roads. When the autumn ordinances are implemented in Zongzhang, the Hall of Full Manifestation, measures are undertaken to inspect the troops, punish violence, put the laws in order, and repair prisons. When the winter ordinances are implemented in Xuantang, the Dark Hall, measures are undertaken to repair city walls, secure the territory, provide for frontier defense, and build fortifications. And…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
又因朝日以脩陽政習地德因夕月以治陰敎
糺天刑凡所以順四時一羣動歸之理道者王
者無爲也是故慶賞不以私勞用刑威不以私
怨行爵人于朝以旌善焉戮人于市以遏惡焉
命自我錫討自我出非故爲是威福也天也善
之不齊也爲之次第其服以章顯之惡之不齊
也爲之輕重其獄以懲創之賞必當功罰必當
罪非故爲是區別也天也而猶未也罪疑惟輕
焉殺之中而寓生之意也功疑惟重焉賞之施
===
而寓厚之道也天心仁厚吾奉以行法而已猶
未也賞不踰時賞延于世可祿則祿之罪不及
孥刑不逮士可宥則宥之天德好生吾奉以濟
法而已法之所麗猶日月也澤之所被猶雨露
也威之所擊猶雷霆也刑之所加猶霜雪也天
何甞物物而容心哉惟其蕃育夭折之類而已
矣王者何甞人人而用情哉惟其知愚賢不肖
之類而已矣不然有功不錄而濫賞是桃李冬
華而冬行春令矣有罪不誅而倖免是隕霜不
punctuated: 又因朝日以脩陽政、習地德，因夕月以治陰敎、糺天刑。凡所以順四時、一羣動、歸之理道者，王者無爲也。是故慶賞不以私勞用，刑威不以私怨行。爵人于朝，以旌善焉；戮人于市，以遏惡焉。命自我錫，討自我出，非故爲是威福也，天也。善之不齊也，爲之次第其服以章顯之；惡之不齊也，爲之輕重其獄以懲創之。賞必當功，罰必當罪，非故爲是區別也，天也。而猶未也，罪疑惟輕焉，殺之中而寓生之意也；功疑惟重焉，賞之施而寓厚之道也。天心仁厚，吾奉以行法而已。猶未也，賞不踰時，賞延于世，可祿則祿之；罪不及孥，刑不逮士，可宥則宥之。天德好生，吾奉以濟法而已。法之所麗猶日月也，澤之所被猶雨露也，威之所擊猶雷霆也，刑之所加猶霜雪也。天何甞物物而容心哉？惟其蕃育夭折之類而已矣。王者何甞人人而用情哉？惟其知愚賢不肖之類而已矣。不然，有功不錄而濫賞，是桃李冬華而冬行春令矣；有罪不誅而倖免，是隕霜不
translation_en:
…Furthermore, through the morning rite to the sun, he cultivates the governance of yang and practices the virtue of Earth; through the evening rite to the moon, he orders the teachings of yin and regulates the punishments of Heaven. All the means by which he follows the four seasons, brings the myriad moving beings into unity, and returns them to the way of orderly government constitute the king’s action through nonaction. Thus, favors and rewards are not bestowed for services rendered to him personally, nor are punishments and coercive power exercised out of private resentment. He confers rank upon men at court to commend goodness, and executes men in the marketplace to restrain evil. Appointments are bestowed by him, and punitive action proceeds from him; yet he does not deliberately wield these terrors and blessings on his own initiative: they are Heaven’s doing. Since good deeds differ in degree, he grades the recipients’ ceremonial dress to make their merit manifest. Since evil deeds differ in degree, he makes their sentences lighter or heavier to punish and chastise them. Rewards must match achievements, and punishments must match offenses. He does not deliberately make these distinctions on his own initiative: they are Heaven’s doing.

Nor is this all. When an offense is doubtful, he favors the lighter penalty, lodging an intention to preserve life even within the taking of life. When merit is doubtful, he favors the greater reward, lodging the principle of generosity within the bestowal of rewards. Heaven’s heart is benevolent and generous; I merely obey it in administering the law. Nor is this all. Rewards are not delayed beyond their proper time, and their benefits extend to later generations; those who may receive emoluments are granted them. Guilt does not extend to wives and children, and corporal punishment does not reach the shi, the gentlemen; those who may be pardoned are pardoned. Heaven’s virtue cherishes life; I merely obey it in tempering the law. The law’s reach is like that of the sun and moon; the spread of beneficence is like rain and dew; the blows of sovereign might are like thunder and lightning; the imposition of punishments is like frost and snow. Has Heaven ever harbored a particular intention toward each individual thing? It acts only according to their categories of flourishing growth or premature destruction. Has the king ever acted from personal feelings toward each individual person? He acts only according to their categories of wisdom or folly, worthiness or unworthiness.

Otherwise, if achievements go unrecognized while rewards are bestowed indiscriminately, this is like peach and plum trees flowering in winter: it is carrying out spring’s ordinances in winter. If offenses go unpunished and the guilty escape through undeserved favor, this is like frost falling without…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
殺而秋行夏令矣失五官之職傷兩間之和非
太平盛世所宜有也而謂王者爲之乎是故聖
人未甞福天下福有時而施卽其生長于春夏
奉若陽舒也聖人未甞威天下威有時而用卽
其肅殺于秋冬奉若陰慘也天以陰陽生成萬
物而無所偏故物皆各足于天之道王者以德
威刑賞萬民而無所狥故民皆取足于王者之
仁天下後世被其賞者曰非聖人作好也吾自
協于天命特爲天揚之耳蒙其罰者曰非聖人
===
作惡也吾自罹于天刑特爲天戮之耳賞一人
而天下莫不勸曰天監在兹吾何爲不協于極
以自外于長養之天乎罰一人而天下莫不懲
曰天威有赫吾何爲而復卽于淫以自蹈于肅
殺之天乎天下仰聖人之治如日月雨露雷霆
霜雪之不可欺而王者常以其天道治天下而
無負于天王之責王心純一王道大公王政熈
熈王民皞皞行帝道而帝行王道而王唐虞三
代其純王之化弗可及矣孔子具天道而不得
punctuated: 殺，而秋行夏令矣。失五官之職，傷兩間之和，非太平盛世所宜有也，而謂王者爲之乎？是故聖人未甞福天下，福有時而施，卽其生長于春夏，奉若陽舒也；聖人未甞威天下，威有時而用，卽其肅殺于秋冬，奉若陰慘也。天以陰陽生成萬物而無所偏，故物皆各足于天之道；王者以德威刑賞萬民而無所狥，故民皆取足于王者之仁。天下後世被其賞者曰：「非聖人作好也，吾自協于天命，特爲天揚之耳。」蒙其罰者曰：「非聖人作惡也，吾自罹于天刑，特爲天戮之耳。」賞一人而天下莫不勸，曰：「天監在兹，吾何爲不協于極，以自外于長養之天乎？」罰一人而天下莫不懲，曰：「天威有赫，吾何爲而復卽于淫，以自蹈于肅殺之天乎？」天下仰聖人之治，如日月雨露雷霆霜雪之不可欺，而王者常以其天道治天下，而無負于天王之責。王心純一，王道大公，王政熈熈，王民皞皞。行帝道而帝，行王道而王。唐虞三代，其純王之化弗可及矣。孔子具天道而不得
translation_en:
…does not kill, and thus summer’s ordinances are carried out in autumn. To disrupt the duties of the five offices and injure the harmony between Heaven and Earth is something that ought never to occur in an age of great peace and flourishing rule. Could one say that a true king would do this?

Thus the sage has never bestowed blessings upon the world at will: blessings are conferred at their proper times. In giving life and fostering growth in spring and summer, he reverently follows the expansive workings of yang. The sage has never imposed his might upon the world at will: might is exercised at its proper times. In bringing restraint and death in autumn and winter, he reverently follows the harsh workings of yin. Heaven produces and completes the myriad things through yin and yang without partiality; thus all things find their full provision in Heaven’s Way. The king employs virtue and might, punishments and rewards, toward the myriad people without favoritism; thus all the people find their full provision in the king’s benevolence.

Those throughout the world and in later generations who receive his rewards say: “The sage is not indulging a personal liking. I myself have accorded with Heaven’s mandate; he merely honors me on Heaven’s behalf.” Those who undergo his punishments say: “The sage is not indulging a personal aversion. I myself have incurred Heaven’s punishment; he merely punishes me on Heaven’s behalf.” When one person is rewarded, everyone in the world is encouraged, saying: “Heaven’s scrutiny is here. Why should I fail to accord with the supreme standard and thereby exclude myself from Heaven’s nurturing care?” When one person is punished, everyone in the world takes warning, saying: “Heaven’s might is awe-inspiring. Why should I again turn to excess and thereby expose myself to Heaven’s killing severity?”

All under Heaven look up to the sage’s government as something that can no more be deceived than the sun and moon, rain and dew, thunder, frost, and snow. The king constantly governs the world through this Way of Heaven and does not fail in his responsibilities as Heaven’s king. The king’s heart is pure and undivided; the kingly Way is utterly impartial; the king’s government brings concord and joy; the king’s people live in untroubled contentment. Practicing the Way of the ancient emperors, one becomes an emperor; practicing the Way of the kings, one becomes a king. The transforming influence of the pure kingly rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties could not be equaled. Confucius embodied the Way of Heaven but did not obtain…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
位于是乎作春秋繫王于天而曰元年春王正
月凡惇典庸禮命德討罪皆奉天立敎賞罰嚴
於褒貶不以一字傷天道之公其亦以天自處
者歟吁此王道也霸者未甞不知道而以己私
行其間如春秋紀桓文之事迹若討罪而意實
尊己假仁仗義以懾天下而心不純于王善不
本于心子犯曰示之義示之信示之禮皆有爲
而爲之非若王者無思無爲者也吁此王霸之
由辨也儒者論治必求于誠意正心其奉若天
===
道之本歟
表
擬
召輔臣徐溥劉健李東陽謝遷至
文華殿
面議章奏
賜茶謝表弘治十年
萬國欽
同考試官敎諭唐批讀此當時
punctuated:
位，於是乎作《春秋》，繫王于天，而曰：「元年春王正月。」凡惇典、庸禮、命德、討罪，皆奉天立敎，賞罰嚴於褒貶，不以一字傷天道之公，其亦以天自處者歟？吁！此王道也。霸者未甞不知道，而以己私行其間。如《春秋》紀桓文之事，迹若討罪，而意實尊己，假仁仗義以懾天下，而心不純于王，善不本于心。子犯曰：「示之義，示之信，示之禮。」皆有爲而爲之，非若王者無思無爲者也。吁！此王霸之由辨也。儒者論治，必求于誠意正心，其奉若天道之本歟？
表
擬召輔臣徐溥、劉健、李東陽、謝遷至文華殿，面議章奏，賜茶謝表。弘治十年。
萬國欽
同考試官敎諭唐批：讀此，當時
translation_en:
…office. Thus he composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, linking the king to Heaven, and wrote: “In the first year, in spring, in the first month of the king’s calendar.” In all matters of honoring the enduring norms, applying ritual, appointing the virtuous, and punishing the guilty, he established his teachings in obedience to Heaven. Through praise and blame he rigorously administered rewards and punishments, never allowing a single word to impair the impartiality of Heaven’s Way. Was he not also taking Heaven as his own standard? Ah! This is the kingly Way. The hegemons were not unaware of the Way, but allowed their private interests to intrude upon it. For example, in the deeds of Duke Huan and Duke Wen recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, their actions appeared to punish the guilty, but their actual intent was to exalt themselves. They borrowed benevolence and wielded righteousness to overawe the world, yet their hearts were not wholly devoted to the kingly Way, nor did their goodness spring from their hearts. Zifan said: “Show them righteousness; show them trustworthiness; show them ritual propriety.” All these were deliberate actions undertaken for an ulterior purpose, unlike the true king’s action without calculation or contrivance. Ah! This is the basis for distinguishing kingship from hegemony. When Confucian scholars discuss government, they must seek its foundation in making the intentions sincere and rectifying the heart. Is this not the root of reverently following Heaven’s Way?
Memorial
Draft memorial of thanks for the bestowal of tea when the grand secretaries Xu Pu, Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, and Xie Qian were summoned to the Hall of Literary Brilliance to discuss memorials to the throne in person. Tenth year of Hongzhi [1497].
Wan Guoqin
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “Reading this, that time’s …”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
泰交氣象猶可想見宜錄以彰盛美
同考試官教諭鄭批意懇詞工敘
明良一德處宛若躬逢可式
考試官學正吳批四六之佳者
考試官教授顧批駢驪典則
弘治十年某月某日
經筵講徹伏蒙
皇上
召臣溥臣健臣東陽臣遷至
===
文華殿
面議章奏
賜茶謹奉
表稱
謝者伏以
天啓泰交
黼扆廣諮詢之益
日隆晉接章縫荷
霑溉之榮渙
punctuated:
泰交氣象猶可想見，宜錄以彰盛美。
同考試官教諭鄭批：意懇詞工，敘明良一德處，宛若躬逢，可式。
考試官學正吳批：四六之佳者。
考試官教授顧批：駢驪典則。
弘治十年某月某日，經筵講徹，伏蒙皇上召臣溥、臣健、臣東陽、臣遷至文華殿，面議章奏，賜茶，謹奉表稱謝者。伏以：天啓泰交，黼扆廣諮詢之益；日隆晉接，章縫荷霑溉之榮。渙
translation_en:
…The atmosphere of harmonious intercourse between sovereign and ministers can still be imagined. This deserves to be recorded to display the splendid achievement.
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: The sentiments are earnest and the language skillful. Its account of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers united in virtue makes one feel personally present. It may serve as a model.
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: An excellent example of four-and-six-character parallel prose.
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: The parallel prose is classically grounded and conforms to proper standards.
On a certain day of a certain month in the tenth year of Hongzhi [1497], upon completion of the Classics Colloquium lecture, we reverently received Your Majesty’s gracious summons for your servants Pu, Jian, Dongyang, and Qian to come to the Hall of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua dian), discuss memorials face to face, and receive tea. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks.
We humbly reflect: Heaven has opened the way to harmonious intercourse between sovereign and ministers; from behind the embroidered throne screen, Your Majesty extends the benefits of consultation. Daily more gracious are the audiences you grant; we scholars in our ceremonial caps receive the honor of your nourishing favor. With the issuing forth…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
綸旨以中傳特勤
燕對淪
靈芽而下賚普被
鴻恩
寵遇非常對揚曷稱〔臣溥〕等誠惶誠恐稽首頓
首上言竊惟王者繼天立極彌綸日侈于
萬幾大臣以道事君靖獻先資于百辟燧
皇爰立四相軒后佐命六人唐虞一德相
孚都俞吁咈夏商二代以降左右疑丞古
===
昔惟論道以經邦近代且直廬而召見漢
開東觀趙喜明習朝章唐啓集賢張說預
叅機務逮于有宋尤藉休風晏見承明尚
謹朝衣之度召登便殿更隆納陛之儀事
豈無徵時如有待玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
聰明神授
仁孝性成
膺
punctuated: 綸旨以中傳，特勤燕對；淪靈芽而下賚，普被鴻恩。寵遇非常，對揚曷稱？〔臣溥〕等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟王者繼天立極，彌綸日侈于萬幾；大臣以道事君，靖獻先資于百辟。燧皇爰立四相，軒后佐命六人。唐虞一德相孚，都俞吁咈；夏商二代以降，左右疑丞。古昔惟論道以經邦，近代且直廬而召見。漢開東觀，趙喜明習朝章；唐啓集賢，張說預叅機務。逮于有宋，尤藉休風。晏見承明，尚謹朝衣之度；召登便殿，更隆納陛之儀。事豈無徵？時如有待。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聰明神授，仁孝性成，膺
translation_en:
…The imperial edict was transmitted from within the palace, with particular solicitude for an informal audience; choice tea was brewed [?] and bestowed from above, extending your vast favor to all. Such exceptional favor and treatment—how could our grateful acknowledgment be adequate? 〔Your servant Pu〕 and the others, in profound fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and submit these words:
We humbly reflect that a sovereign succeeds Heaven and establishes the supreme standard, his comprehensive governance daily expanding amid the myriad affairs of state. Great ministers serve their ruler according to the Way; devoted service depends first upon the assembled officials. Suihuang established four ministers, and the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan had six men to assist his rule. Under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, ruler and ministers trusted one another in a shared virtue, exchanging words of assent and remonstrance. From the Xia and Shang dynasties onward, counselors and assistants stood at the ruler’s sides. In antiquity they discoursed on the Way to order the realm; in later ages they also attended in duty quarters and were summoned to audiences. The Han opened the Eastern Library, where Zhao Xi was thoroughly versed in court regulations; the Tang established the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, where Zhang Yue participated in confidential affairs of government. By the Song dynasty, this admirable tradition was especially valued. At informal audiences in the Chengming Hall, the prescribed propriety of court dress was still carefully observed; when summoned into an informal palace hall, the ceremony of admission by the palace steps was further honored. Are these practices without historical evidence? It was as though they awaited their proper time.
Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, divinely endowed with intelligence and discernment, innately humane and filial, receiving…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
寶籙以御
天受命同符
太祖
撫玉衡而齊政成功遠過百王
總攬乾綱穆穆垂衣恭巳
重申巽命孳孳側席求言
身處九重而計先天下
運當累洽而戒切日中
納儒臣講學聽政之言虛同止輦
===
採冢卿召見專對之議速若轉圜逮臣葑菲
之瀆陳竝荷
乾坤之褒納
應門朝啓
宸聰兼聽於閭閻
講幄中開古訓聿收乎華實尤以明王好問
則裕而惟君子屢省乃成載講
午朝之規庸資
面對之益乃於
punctuated:
寶籙以御天，受命同符太祖；撫玉衡而齊政，成功遠過百王。總攬乾綱，穆穆垂衣恭巳；重申巽命，孳孳側席求言。身處九重而計先天下，運當累洽而戒切日中。納儒臣講學聽政之言，虛同止輦；採冢卿召見專對之議，速若轉圜。逮臣葑菲之瀆陳，竝荷乾坤之褒納。
應門朝啓，宸聰兼聽於閭閻；講幄中開，古訓聿收乎華實。尤以明王好問則裕，而惟君子屢省乃成，載講午朝之規，庸資面對之益。乃於
translation_en:
…the precious register of imperial destiny, thereby exercising Heaven’s rule; in receiving the mandate, Your Majesty matches Taizu. Grasping the jade armillary instrument to bring government into harmony, Your Majesty’s achievements far surpass those of the hundred kings. Holding together the guiding cords of sovereign authority, you rule with solemn serenity, robes hanging loose and person reverently composed [?]. Repeatedly issuing gracious commands, you diligently leave a place beside you and seek counsel. Though dwelling within the ninefold palace, your plans put the realm first; though your reign enjoys generations of accumulated peace, your vigilance is keenest at the sun’s zenith.
You accepted the Confucian officials’ proposal to pursue learning and attend to government, displaying humility like that of the ruler who halted his carriage to hear counsel. You adopted the chief minister’s proposal to summon officials for audiences and let them answer in person, acting as swiftly as a turning ball. Even my importunate submission, as humble as turnip greens, received the commendation and acceptance of your heaven-and-earth-like generosity.
The palace gate opens in the morning, and your sagely hearing takes in voices from the common people’s lanes. The lecture pavilion opens within, and the ancient teachings are gathered in both their flower and their fruit. Above all, recognizing that an enlightened king gains abundance by delighting in questions, and that a gentleman achieves fulfillment only through repeated self-examination, you have again considered the arrangements for the midday audience, to gain the benefits of face-to-face consultation. Thus, at…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
瑶篇之甫撤特披
玉匧以傳
宣日麗
龍旌
帝座時開乎左个雲移雉扇使華
寵賁於中樞
咨四輔之愚忠閱羣寮之封事衣冠旅進俄
驚身上星辰階戺同升遥聽語傳
閶闔
===
天顏日霽親承下濟之光明
睿藻春溫共識太和之盎溢臣溥等才非命世
學謝匡時遭際
聖明
簡拔濫均于杞梓洊登華要職司竝玷于台衡
仰惟
一德主善之衷有出
累朝常制之外謂章奏乃
邦國大計當廣益於眾思而
punctuated: 瑶篇之甫撤，特披玉匧以傳宣。日麗龍旌，帝座時開乎左个；雲移雉扇，使華寵賁於中樞。咨四輔之愚忠，閱羣寮之封事。衣冠旅進，俄驚身上星辰；階戺同升，遥聽語傳閶闔。天顏日霽，親承下濟之光明；睿藻春溫，共識太和之盎溢。臣溥等才非命世，學謝匡時，遭際聖明，簡拔濫均于杞梓；洊登華要，職司竝玷于台衡。仰惟一德主善之衷，有出累朝常制之外。謂章奏乃邦國大計，當廣益於眾思，而
translation_en:
…As soon as the precious text had been put away, you specially opened the jade coffer to transmit your proclamation. Sunlight gleamed upon the dragon standards, and the imperial seat was opened at times in the eastern chamber; clouds moved beside the pheasant-feather fans, and the splendor of imperial envoys graciously adorned the central administration [?]. You consulted the simple loyalty of the Four Counsellors and read the sealed memorials of the assembled officials. The robed and capped officials advanced together, suddenly awed to find the stars above their very persons; ascending the palace steps together, they heard from afar words conveyed from the gates of Heaven. Your heavenly countenance cleared like the sun, and they personally received the radiance that you shed upon those below; your sagacious compositions were warm as spring, and all perceived the overflowing abundance of supreme harmony.
Your servants, Pu and the others, possess no talents fit to answer the needs of the age, and our learning falls short of what is required to set the times aright. Yet we have encountered Your Majesty’s sagacious and enlightened rule: through selection and promotion, we have undeservedly been ranked alongside men who are like precious timber. Repeatedly advanced to illustrious and important posts, we have all unworthily occupied the offices of chief ministers. We reverently consider how your single-minded devotion to goodness surpasses the established practices of successive reigns. You hold that memorials concern the great affairs of the realm and should benefit broadly from the deliberations of many, while…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
封駁則寅亮攸關貴協中于羣議爰厪
晝接共勅時幾蓋
皇極以剛柔正直參和而
天子乃禮樂征伐自出典秩有頒則
請旣詳宗伯之緘題罪讞雖細必矜尤悉撫臣
之奏記是曰是非曰非
廟謨宏遠豈羣臣敢望清光筆則筆削則削
睿筭周詳卽一字可垂金石迨
龍輿之戒蹕忽雀舌之
===
匪頒色瀉先春恍裒金莖于仙掌香浮
內苑驚傳雪乳自蓬萊方忻湛露之
恩私共效承雲之抃舞伏念臣等潤依江海曾
無勺水之裨味匪鹽梅奚取和羹之助昔
宣室前賈生之席祗聞問及鬼神彼祕閣
納仲淹之陳未見施諸政治顧慚朽質遘
此
殊榮臣敢不誓傾葵藿之誠勉效涓埃之報有
謀猷入告于
punctuated: 封駁則寅亮攸關，貴協中于羣議。爰厪晝接，共勅時幾。蓋皇極以剛柔正直參和，而天子乃禮樂征伐自出。典秩有頒，則請旣詳宗伯之緘題；罪讞雖細，必矜尤悉撫臣之奏記。是曰是，非曰非，廟謨宏遠，豈羣臣敢望清光？筆則筆，削則削，睿筭周詳，卽一字可垂金石。迨龍輿之戒蹕，忽雀舌之匪頒。色瀉先春，恍裒金莖于仙掌；香浮內苑，驚傳雪乳自蓬萊。方忻湛露之恩私，共效承雲之抃舞。伏念臣等潤依江海，曾無勺水之裨；味匪鹽梅，奚取和羹之助？昔宣室前賈生之席，祗聞問及鬼神；彼祕閣納仲淹之陳，未見施諸政治。顧慚朽質，遘此殊榮。臣敢不誓傾葵藿之誠，勉效涓埃之報？有謀猷入告于
translation_en: …As for returning edicts for reconsideration, this concerns the duty of respectfully assisting the sovereign: what matters is reaching a balanced judgment through collective deliberation. Thus Your Majesty graciously granted us an audience by day, that together we might attend diligently to the critical beginnings of affairs. For the sovereign standard harmonizes firmness, gentleness, and uprightness, while rites, music, punitive expeditions, and military campaigns issue from the Son of Heaven himself. When ceremonial regulations and ranks are promulgated, the requests have already been set out fully in the Minister of Rites’ sealed memorials; even in minor criminal adjudications, Your Majesty invariably exercises compassion, examining with particular care the provincial governors’ memorials. You pronounce right what is right and wrong what is wrong. So far-reaching are the court’s plans—how could your servants dare aspire to such luminous discernment? What should be recorded you record; what should be deleted you delete. Your sagacious deliberations are comprehensive and exact: even a single word deserves to be transmitted in bronze and stone. When the warning was sounded to clear the way for the imperial carriage, there suddenly came a bestowal of ‘sparrow’s-tongue’ tea. Its color poured forth the freshness of early spring, as though dew from the golden stalk had been gathered in an immortal’s palm; its fragrance drifted through the palace gardens, as we marveled at snowy froth brought from Penglai. Rejoicing in this personal favor, like the abundant dew, we all clapped and danced as though to the music of Chengyun, ‘Bearing the Clouds.’ Humbly we reflect that, though we depend upon your river-and-ocean bounty for nourishment, we have contributed not even a ladleful of water. Our flavor is neither salt nor plum: how could we help season the broth of government? In former times, when the emperor in the Xuanshi Hall drew Jia Yi’s mat closer, we hear only that he questioned him about ghosts and spirits; when Zhongyan’s offering was accepted in the Palace Library, we do not find that it was applied to the conduct of government. Ashamed of our own decayed capacities, we have nevertheless encountered this extraordinary honor. How could your servants fail to pledge the whole of our sunflower-like devotion, striving to repay you with even a drop of water or a speck of dust? Whenever we have plans or counsels, we shall enter and report them to…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
后必戒面從非堯舜不陳于前尚期心格伏願
政圖無逸
學懋有終
明四目達四聰益廣合宮之觀聽
慎五刑敷五敎用臻比屋之雍熙井渫求賢
介
明王之
景福鼎烹享
帝凝
===
峻命於
鴻圖臣溥等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策五道
punctuated:
后，必戒面從；非堯舜不陳于前，尚期心格。伏願政圖無逸，學懋有終；明四目，達四聰，益廣合宮之觀聽；慎五刑，敷五敎，用臻比屋之雍熙。井渫求賢，介明王之景福；鼎烹享帝，凝峻命於鴻圖。臣溥等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策五道。
translation_en:
…to the sovereign, we shall certainly guard against merely outward compliance; we shall present before you nothing that does not accord with Yao and Shun, hoping still to move your heart. We humbly wish that in governing you will resolve never to indulge in ease, and in learning strive diligently through to the end. Open your eyes to all four quarters and your ears to every direction, further broadening what is seen and heard in the ceremonial palace. Exercise care in the five punishments and disseminate the five teachings, thereby bringing every household into harmony and prosperity. Seek worthy men, like a well cleared of mud and ready for use, and augment the enlightened king’s great blessings; offer food cooked in the sacrificial cauldron to the Lord on High, and secure the exalted Mandate for your grand imperial undertaking.
Your servants Pu and the others, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain our intense emotion and utmost trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to you.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一問
李廷謨
同考試官教諭沈批作者多泛言文武我
皇上安夏攘夷鼓舞振作本意誰能發之是策述叙
二錄繹思崇儒閱武之實肆颺殆盡可誦可傳佳士也
同考試官教諭鄭批善形容我
皇上新政盛美錄中所載大槩備矣詞復典麗宜錄
考試官學正吳批敷對明悉無如此作
考試官教授顧批揚厲得體
===
聖皇正五位而首作人之化也於是乎儒道崇
而文教振
撫四夷而先立國之威也於是乎兵政肅而
武備修蓋大學賢士所關也而况
建極之初薄海章縫視之以易心者乎
京營本兵所集也而况
蒞政之始窮邊腥𦤺視之以懾志者乎一
崇儒焉而彬彬之文學出矣一
閱武焉而赫赫之兵威張矣
punctuated:
第一問
李廷謨

同考試官教諭沈批：作者多泛言文武，我皇上安夏攘夷、鼓舞振作本意，誰能發之？是策述叙二錄，繹思崇儒閱武之實，肆颺殆盡，可誦可傳，佳士也。
同考試官教諭鄭批：善形容我皇上新政盛美，錄中所載，大槩備矣。詞復典麗，宜錄。
考試官學正吳批：敷對明悉，無如此作。
考試官教授顧批：揚厲得體。

聖皇正五位而首作人之化也，於是乎儒道崇而文教振；撫四夷而先立國之威也，於是乎兵政肅而武備修。蓋大學賢士所關也，而况建極之初，薄海章縫視之以易心者乎？京營本兵所集也，而况蒞政之始，窮邊腥𦤺視之以懾志者乎？一崇儒焉，而彬彬之文學出矣；一閱武焉，而赫赫之兵威張矣。
translation_en:
First Policy Question
Li Tingmo

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: Writers mostly speak in generalities about civil and military affairs. Who can bring out our emperor’s underlying purpose in securing the Chinese realm, repelling foreign peoples, and inspiring renewed vigor? This policy essay recounts the two records and reflects upon the substance of honoring Confucian learning and reviewing the troops, giving almost full expression to their significance. It deserves to be recited and circulated. A fine scholar indeed.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: This essay aptly depicts the splendid achievements of our emperor’s new administration. It covers virtually all the main points contained in the records. Its language is also classical and elegant; it merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: No other essay equals this one in the clarity and thoroughness of its response.

Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: Its praise is fittingly expressed.

When the sagely emperor assumed his rightful fifth position—the sovereign’s place—he made the transformative cultivation of men his first concern. Thus the Confucian Way was honored and civil education invigorated. In pacifying the peoples of the four quarters, he first established the might of the state. Thus military administration became disciplined and military preparations were put in order. The Imperial University is, indeed, bound up with the cultivation of worthy scholars. How much more so at the beginning of the establishment of sovereign rule, when scholars in Confucian caps throughout the realm looked to it and changed their hearts! The capital garrisons are where the central military forces assemble. How much more so at the beginning of his administration, when the foul-smelling peoples [?] of the remotest frontiers looked to them and were cowed in spirit! Once Confucian learning was honored, scholars of refined literary cultivation emerged; once the troops were reviewed, resplendent military might was displayed.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖神作而文武竝用則順治威嚴而
中興之大業基矣此我
皇上文經武緯
洪謨駿烈不可得而揚厲之乎請敬陳之文教
何昉也自顓頊置樂正教胄子唐虞命后
夔典六樂造士育材之地肇于是矣而學
校之教周制始備師以賢得民儒以道得
民友以任得民而王國則通四方之學天
子特建之以爲辟雝在文則歌于靈臺在
===
武則建于鎬京二聖創述先後作人故其
詩曰鼉鼓逢逢矇瞍奏公又曰自西自東
自南自北無思不服文教其丕揆乎武衞
何昉也自軒轅設圃爲演武之場有夏甘
誓嚴左右之法選將治兵之制肇於斯矣
而教閲之法周禮莫詳中春教振旅中夏
教茇舍中秋教治兵而中冬則通三時之
教而天子大閲之以嚴賞罰其法掌於大
司馬而其禮統于大宗伯宣王中興車攻
punctuated:
聖神作而文武竝用，則順治威嚴，而中興之大業基矣。此我皇上文經武緯，洪謨駿烈，不可得而揚厲之乎？請敬陳之。
文教何昉也？自顓頊置樂正教胄子，唐虞命后夔典六樂，造士育材之地肇于是矣。而學校之教，周制始備：師以賢得民，儒以道得民，友以任得民。而王國則通四方之學，天子特建之以爲辟雝。在文則歌于靈臺，在武則建于鎬京。二聖創述，先後作人。故其詩曰：「鼉鼓逢逢，矇瞍奏公。」又曰：「自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。」文教其丕揆乎？
武衞何昉也？自軒轅設圃爲演武之場，有夏甘誓嚴左右之法，選將治兵之制肇於斯矣。而教閲之法，周禮莫詳：中春教振旅，中夏教茇舍，中秋教治兵，而中冬則通三時之教，而天子大閲之以嚴賞罰。其法掌於大司馬，而其禮統于大宗伯。宣王中興，車攻
translation_en:
When a sagely, divinely gifted ruler arises and employs both civil and military means, government becomes orderly and authority imposing, and the foundations of the great enterprise of restoration are laid. With civil governance as the warp and military affairs as the weft, our Emperor has devised grand plans and accomplished mighty deeds. May we not extol them? Allow me respectfully to set them forth.
Where did civil education begin? Zhuanxu appointed a Director of Music to teach the sons of the nobility, and the rulers of Tang and Yu commissioned Hou Kui to oversee the Six Musical Performances. Institutions for forming scholars and nurturing talent originated here. Yet the system of instruction in schools first became complete under the Zhou: teachers won the people through their worthiness, learned men through the Way, and friends through their trustworthiness. In the royal capital, the learning of the four quarters was brought together, and the Son of Heaven established a special institution, the Biyong. Under King Wen it was celebrated in “The Spirit Terrace”; under King Wu it was established at Haojing. These two sages, one founding and the other carrying forward, successively nurtured men of talent. Thus the poem says: “The alligator-hide drums resound; the blind musicians perform their work.” It also says: “From west and east, from south and north, none thought of withholding submission.” Was not civil education grand in its guiding principles [?]?
Where did military protection begin? Xuanyuan established a park as a place for military exercises, and under the Xia, the “Oath at Gan” sternly prescribed the duties of those on the left and right of the chariots. The system of selecting generals and ordering troops originated here. As for methods of training and inspection, none are more fully detailed than those in the Rites of Zhou: in mid-spring, troops were trained in assembling after a campaign; in mid-summer, in encampment; and in mid-autumn, in battle formations. In mid-winter, the training of the other three seasons was combined, and the Son of Heaven conducted a grand review to enforce rewards and punishments strictly. Its regulations were administered by the Minister of War, and its ceremonies were directed by the Minister of Rites. During King Xuan’s restoration, “The Chariots Are Sturdy” …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
復古故其詩曰四牡騯騯駕言徂東又曰
吉日維戊旣伯旣禱武衞其丕奮乎嗣是
而降祀大牢而闕里增榮臨辟雝而橋門
環聽此固兩漢盛事也而修文之實則未
見焉長川列陳而徒卒徵于驪山西郊講
武而軍營盛於興國此固唐宋盛舉也而
飭武之實則未講焉洪惟我
太祖迅掃腥羶
金陵定鼎建
===
國學于鷄鳴之麓分諸衞于
鳳闕之西法紀所議其創業垂統之宏範乎
成祖廓清沙漠
燕臺立極闢成均而益其員設營務而定其
制石畫所陳其繼體守成之要束乎建學
以崇文也而有八萬焉師儒有舍餼廩有
度祭祀有時佾舞有數
臨幸有期講讀有儀賓相有召
賜賚有等恢恢乎崇儒造士者其制大備矣列
punctuated:
復古，故其詩曰：「四牡騯騯，駕言徂東。」又曰：「吉日維戊，旣伯旣禱。」武衞其丕奮乎！嗣是而降，祀大牢而闕里增榮，臨辟雝而橋門環聽，此固兩漢盛事也，而修文之實則未見焉。長川列陳而徒卒徵于驪山，西郊講武而軍營盛於興國，此固唐宋盛舉也，而飭武之實則未講焉。
洪惟我太祖，迅掃腥羶，金陵定鼎，建國學于鷄鳴之麓，分諸衞于鳳闕之西。法紀所議，其創業垂統之宏範乎！成祖廓清沙漠，燕臺立極，闢成均而益其員，設營務而定其制。石畫所陳，其繼體守成之要束乎！建學以崇文也，而有八萬焉：師儒有舍，餼廩有度，祭祀有時，佾舞有數，臨幸有期，講讀有儀，賓相有召，賜賚有等。恢恢乎，崇儒造士者，其制大備矣！列
translation_en:
…restored ancient practices. Thus the ode says: “The four stallions are vigorous; we harness them and travel east.” Again it says: “Auspicious was the wu day; we had sacrificed to the Horse Ancestor and offered prayers.” Was not military defense greatly invigorated thereby! In subsequent times, offerings of the full complement of sacrificial animals brought added glory to Queli, and when the emperor visited the imperial academy, listeners encircled its bridge gate. These were indeed grand occasions under the Western and Eastern Han, yet the substance of cultivating civil learning was not evident. Troops were drawn up along the river, and foot soldiers were summoned to Lishan; military exercises were held in the western suburbs, and army encampments flourished in the Xingguo era. These were indeed grand undertakings under the Tang and Song, yet the substance of putting military affairs in order was not addressed.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu swiftly swept away the foul-smelling foe and established his capital at Jinling. He founded the Imperial University at the foot of Jiming and stationed the various Guards west of the palace’s phoenix towers. Were not the laws and regulations thus deliberated [?] his grand pattern for founding the dynasty and transmitting its rule? Chengzu cleared the desert of enemies and established the imperial seat at Yantai. He enlarged the Imperial University and increased its enrollment, established the administration of military camps, and fixed its regulations. Were not the enduring plans he set forth the essential rules for succeeding to the throne and preserving the achievements of his predecessors? He established schools to honor civil learning, with eight provisions [?; the transcription reads “eighty thousand”]: teachers had quarters; provisions and grain allowances had prescribed scales; sacrifices had appointed times; rows of ritual dancers had prescribed numbers; imperial visits had appointed occasions; lectures and readings had their ceremonies; ceremonial assistants were summoned; and gifts and rewards were graded. How comprehensive it was! The institutions for honoring Confucian learning and cultivating scholars were fully established. As for arraying …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
營以振武也而有八度焉主帥有權偏裨
有掌旌旆有辨殳矛有備番休有節演習
有法陣圖有紀賞罰有差秩秩乎簡衆治
兵者其制莫善矣
列聖相承
成憲不替迨我
皇上
睿質龍潛乆協
重華之望
===
昌期虎變日臻
光被之勳近宗
二祖遠法三王
洪猷大業見于
登極紀元之初者更僕未易數也其大者如起
忠諫之臣拔淹滯之士正文章之體無非
欲羅一世人材以弼成
至治迺
皇上兢業五位之心不遂已也謂成周多士皆
punctuated:
營以振武也，而有八度焉：主帥有權，偏裨有掌，旌旆有辨，殳矛有備，番休有節，演習有法，陣圖有紀，賞罰有差。秩秩乎，簡衆治兵者，其制莫善矣！
列聖相承，成憲不替。迨我皇上，睿質龍潛，乆協重華之望；昌期虎變，日臻光被之勳。近宗二祖，遠法三王。洪猷大業，見于登極紀元之初者，更僕未易數也。其大者，如起忠諫之臣，拔淹滯之士，正文章之體，無非欲羅一世人材，以弼成至治。迺皇上兢業五位之心不遂已也，謂成周多士皆……
translation_en:
…camps were established to strengthen military prowess, with eight regulations: chief commanders had authority; subordinate commanders had assigned responsibilities; banners and pennants had distinguishing marks; clubs and spears were kept ready; rotations of duty and rest followed a schedule; drills followed prescribed methods; battle formations had established patterns; and rewards and punishments were graded. How orderly! No system could surpass this one for selecting men and administering the troops.
Successive sage emperors inherited the throne, and the established statutes were never abandoned. When our present Emperor, endowed with sagely intelligence, was still a hidden dragon awaiting his accession, he had long fulfilled the hopes placed in him as another Shun. At the auspicious time, he underwent the tiger’s transformation into sovereign majesty, and daily advanced in achievements whose radiance reached everywhere. In the nearer past he revered the Two Progenitors; in the distant past he took the Three Kings as his models. The grand plans and great undertakings manifested at the very outset of his accession and new reign era could scarcely be enumerated, even if the attendants were relieved in shifts. Among the greatest were recalling loyal, remonstrating ministers, promoting men whose talents had languished in obscurity, and rectifying literary style. All these measures sought to gather the talented men of the age to help bring about perfect government. Yet the Emperor’s vigilant and conscientious concern in his sovereign station [?; the transcription reads “five positions”] did not rest content with this. He observed that the many worthy men of the Zhou all…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有譽于天下而成其儁乂者惟無斁作人
之功也鼓舞之機不在
今日乎於是
從禮臣之請而
幸學之典行焉其
奎章宸諭鴻儀大賚載在
臨雍錄者班班可攷爰
命司天候氣擇吉爰
命司空滌爵陳器示精禋也召芳胤于孔林徵
===
世胄于顏孟重先德也自宰輔以至百執
事罔不景從自學士以至經生靡不畢集
於勳裔而悉令習學焉復胄監之舊也於
陪臣而與之觀禮焉聳外國之瞻也駐
蹕而易
皮弁肅其儀也升廟而躬三獻致其虔也發
聖學于周易究帝德于禹謨道統治統續
矣
命坐賜茶有詔焉錦衣寶鈔有錫焉繁儀縟節
punctuated: 有譽于天下，而成其儁乂者，惟無斁作人之功也。鼓舞之機，不在今日乎？於是從禮臣之請，而幸學之典行焉。其奎章宸諭、鴻儀大賚，載在《臨雍錄》者，班班可攷。爰命司天候氣擇吉，爰命司空滌爵陳器，示精禋也。召芳胤于孔林，徵世胄于顏孟，重先德也。自宰輔以至百執事，罔不景從；自學士以至經生，靡不畢集。於勳裔而悉令習學焉，復胄監之舊也；於陪臣而與之觀禮焉，聳外國之瞻也。駐蹕而易皮弁，肅其儀也；升廟而躬三獻，致其虔也。發聖學于《周易》，究帝德于《禹謨》，道統治統續矣。命坐賜茶，有詔焉；錦衣寶鈔，有錫焉。繁儀縟節
translation_en: …had renown throughout the realm; what brought their outstanding talents to fruition was solely the unremitting work of nurturing men of worth. Is not today the moment to inspire and encourage them? Accordingly, His Majesty accepted the request of the ritual officials, and the ceremony of an imperial visit to the school was performed. His imperial compositions and instructions, the grand ceremonies and generous gifts, are clearly documented in the Record of the Imperial Visit to the Academy (Lin Yong Lu) and may be consulted there. He commanded the astronomical officials to observe the vital influences and select an auspicious time, and commanded the officials responsible for works to wash the sacrificial cups and arrange the vessels, thus manifesting the purity of the sacrifice. He summoned the worthy descendants of Confucius from Konglin and called for the hereditary descendants of Yan Hui and Mengzi, thus honoring the virtue of their forebears. From the chief ministers down to all the functionaries, none failed to follow reverently; from the academicians down to the students of the Classics, all assembled. He ordered all descendants of meritorious officials to pursue their studies, restoring the ancient practice of educating the sons of the nobility at the imperial academy. He allowed the envoys of tributary rulers to witness the rites, inspiring awe among foreign countries. When his carriage halted, he changed into the leather-cap ceremonial attire, lending solemnity to his deportment; he ascended into the temple and personally performed the three offerings, expressing his devotion to the utmost. Through the Changes of Zhou he expounded the learning of the sages, and through the Counsels of Yu he explored imperial virtue: the succession in the Way and the succession in rulership were thereby continued. An edict commanded those present to be seated and served tea; embroidered garments and paper currency were bestowed as gifts. The elaborate ceremonies and richly detailed observances…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
備矣觀
臨雍一錄我
皇上崇儒重道以作士類者何周至邪莊誦
敕諭有
曰五倫之道根於性命之自然而推極其用
則化成天下又曰六經垂憲炳如日星所以
發揮斯道者甚備會其旨要身體而力行之
以措諸事業大哉
王言眞有以開人心之迷而迪之趨豈徒爲視
===
學之虛文者歟愼本兵之任重督帥之選
厚邊戍之賞無非欲鼓中外士氣以奠安
宗社廼
皇上駕馭戎夷之心不遂已也謂宣王大業外
攘夷狄以復文武之境土者惟蒐狩教閱
之功也整飭之權不在
今日乎於是
納輔臣之奏而
閱武之禮舉焉其
punctuated:
備矣。觀《臨雍》一錄，我皇上崇儒重道以作士類者，何周至邪！莊誦敕諭，有曰：「五倫之道，根於性命之自然，而推極其用，則化成天下。」又曰：「六經垂憲，炳如日星，所以發揮斯道者甚備。會其旨要，身體而力行之，以措諸事業。」大哉，王言！眞有以開人心之迷而迪之趨，豈徒爲視學之虛文者歟？
愼本兵之任，重督帥之選，厚邊戍之賞，無非欲鼓中外士氣，以奠安宗社。廼皇上駕馭戎夷之心不遂已也。謂宣王大業，外攘夷狄以復文武之境土者，惟蒐狩教閱之功也。整飭之權，不在今日乎？於是納輔臣之奏，而閱武之禮舉焉。其

…were complete. Looking through the Record of the Imperial Visit to the National University (Lin yong), how comprehensive and thorough is our Emperor’s esteem for Confucian learning and reverence for the Way, through which he invigorates the scholars! Reverently reading his admonitory edict, we find these words: “The Way of the Five Relationships is rooted in the natural endowment of human nature and destiny; when its application is extended to the utmost, it transforms and perfects all under Heaven.” It also says: “The Six Classics hand down exemplary standards, brilliant as the sun and stars, and expound this Way most fully. Grasp their essential meaning, embody it in your own conduct, and diligently put it into practice, applying it to your undertakings.” Great indeed are these royal words! They truly can dispel the confusion in people’s hearts and guide their course. Could this have been merely the empty ceremony of an imperial visit to an educational institution?
Care in appointing the Minister of War, emphasis on selecting supreme commanders, and generous rewards for the frontier garrisons—all aim to rouse the morale of officers and men at court and beyond, thereby securing the ancestral temples and altars of state. Yet our Emperor’s resolve to control the Rong and Yi peoples did not stop there [?]. He held that King Xuan’s great achievement in repelling the Yi and Di peoples abroad and recovering the territories of Kings Wen and Wu resulted precisely from the training and reviews conducted during seasonal hunts. Does not the authority to restore military discipline rest with the present ruler? Accordingly, he accepted the memorial of his grand secretaries, and the ceremony of reviewing the troops was held. title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
綸音曠典雄略徽猷載在
大閱錄者歷歷可攷叅酌營務以昭武計處訓
練以飭規採
廷議也清世祿之豢養而收之營操查馬匹
之私占而歸之卒伍剗宿弊也順時氣以
申號令數軍實而明等威肅法紀也
允錫予之請而比之崇文示兼重也
敕軍士之苦而特令加賞憫獨勞也自將領以
至卒伍藝能罔不較焉自超擢以至降革
===
賞格罔不備焉
六駕擁雲而龍旌耀日矣萬騎騰驤而鼉鼓振
天矣奏武成之曲而樂和矣肅
內殿之儀而禮備矣觀
大閱一錄我
皇上詰戎講武以威天下者何創見邪莊誦
敕諭有
曰平時則講軍實遇警則壯國威居重馭輕
爲萬世之計又曰部伍充實士馬精强訓練
punctuated:
綸音曠典、雄略徽猷，載在《大閱錄》者，歷歷可攷。叅酌營務以昭武，計處訓練以飭規，採廷議也。清世祿之豢養而收之營操，查馬匹之私占而歸之卒伍，剗宿弊也。順時氣以申號令，數軍實而明等威，肅法紀也。允錫予之請而比之崇文，示兼重也。敕軍士之苦而特令加賞，憫獨勞也。自將領以至卒伍，藝能罔不較焉；自超擢以至降革，賞格罔不備焉。

translation_en:
…His imperial pronouncements and unprecedented ceremonies, his bold strategies and excellent plans, are recorded in the Record of the Grand Review, where each may be clearly verified. By weighing the affairs of the military camps to display martial strength, and planning training to put regulations in order, he adopted the court’s deliberations. By clearing out those who lived idly on hereditary emoluments and bringing them into camp drills, and investigating the private appropriation of horses and returning them to the ranks, he eradicated longstanding abuses. By issuing commands in accordance with the seasons, and taking stock of military resources while clarifying distinctions of rank and authority, he enforced discipline. By approving requests for rewards and placing these on a par with those honoring civil learning, he demonstrated that both were equally valued. By addressing the soldiers’ hardships in an edict [?] and specially ordering additional rewards, he showed compassion for those who alone bore the toil. From commanders down to the rank and file, none went without assessment of their skills; from exceptional promotion down to demotion and dismissal, the provisions governing rewards and penalties were complete.
The imperial six-horse carriage was wreathed in clouds, and dragon banners shone in the sun. Ten thousand mounted troops galloped forth, and alligator-hide drums shook the heavens. The tune “Martial Accomplishment” was performed, and the music was harmonious. The observances in the inner palace hall were solemn, and the rites were complete. Reading this single Record of the Grand Review, how unprecedented we find Our Sovereign’s ordering of the troops and practice of arms to overawe all under Heaven! Reverently reciting his edict, we find these words: “In ordinary times, attend to military preparedness; when an alarm arises, enhance the state’s might. Maintain a strong center to control the lesser outlying forces, making provision for ten thousand generations.” It further says: “The units are fully manned, the soldiers and horses select and strong; training …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不爲虛文征調皆有實用庶幾重根本之勢
消釁孽之萌大哉
王言眞有以起士心之靡而作其氣豈徒爲敎
閱之觀美者歟一時
右文之盛舉踴躍于章縫
奮揚之偉烈赫奕於武弁固宜薄海內外罔
不懾目而易心也猗歟休哉雖然文武之
道發於事業而統於一心惟
皇上
===
聖學運而不息
聖德久而益純
蘊之爲緝熙敬止是文治之精也
涵之爲英明果斷是武功之本也蓋經天緯
地之文不獨見於
臨雍之日而已煥然於
淵默之內安內攘外之武不獨見於
大閱之際而已毅然於
昭曠之原由是以之崇文則
punctuated: 不爲虛文，征調皆有實用，庶幾重根本之勢，消釁孽之萌。」大哉，王言！眞有以起士心之靡而作其氣，豈徒爲敎閱之觀美者歟？一時，右文之盛舉踴躍于章縫，奮揚之偉烈赫奕於武弁，固宜薄海內外罔不懾目而易心也。猗歟休哉！雖然，文武之道發於事業而統於一心。惟皇上聖學運而不息，聖德久而益純，蘊之爲緝熙敬止，是文治之精也；涵之爲英明果斷，是武功之本也。蓋經天緯地之文，不獨見於臨雍之日而已，煥然於淵默之內；安內攘外之武，不獨見於大閱之際而已，毅然於昭曠之原。由是，以之崇文，則
translation_en:
…training will not be an empty formality, and all troops called up will be of practical use. Thus may we strengthen the foundations of the realm and extinguish the first stirrings of strife and calamity.” Great indeed are these royal words! They can truly rouse the soldiers’ flagging spirits and awaken their courage. Could they merely be intended to make drills and reviews an impressive spectacle? At this time, the splendid undertaking of honoring civil learning makes the scholars in their cloth caps leap with joy, while the great achievements in displaying martial vigor shine brilliantly among those in military caps. It is surely fitting that throughout the realm and beyond, to the very seas, none should fail to be awed by the sight and undergo a change of heart. Ah, how glorious!

Yet the ways of civil and military government manifest themselves in deeds but are united in a single mind. Your Majesty’s sagely learning is continually active and never ceases; your sagely virtue grows ever purer with time. Stored within, it becomes constant illumination and an abiding reverence: this is the essence of civil governance. Nurtured within, it becomes perspicacity and resolution: this is the foundation of military achievement. For the civil virtue that orders Heaven and Earth is not manifested only on the day of your visit to the Imperial University; it shines within your profound stillness. The martial virtue that secures the realm internally and repels external enemies is not manifested only at the grand military review; it stands resolute at the clear and expansive source within your mind. Thus, when you apply this to honoring civil learning, then…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
文謨丕顯與雲漢同其昭回而順治之化可洽
以之飭武則
聖武布昭與雷霆同其震懾而威嚴之治可成
誠有上軼文武宣王而陋漢唐宋於不居
者矣此固二錄已載而未詳者敢以聞于
當宁
第二問
孫希夔
同考試官敎諭廖批〔惓惓擇官正學歸本〕
〔皇上之聖德聖政爲身敎忠愛之意藹然〕
考試官學正吳批〔發揚敎本殆盡〕
考試官敎授顧批〔知本之論錄之〕
帝王所以衍昌隆之祚者惟繼體之良而
已矣所以善裕後之謨者惟敎本之端而
已矣蓋儲君天下大本也上而天命下而
人心遠而國祚胥係焉是故養之宜愼也
望之宜仁也曲成之宜盡道也翊贊之宜
擇官而得人也毓德貴豫而身敎要也易
punctuated:
文謨丕顯，與雲漢同其昭回，而順治之化可洽；以之飭武，則聖武布昭，與雷霆同其震懾，而威嚴之治可成。誠有上軼文武宣王而陋漢唐宋於不居者矣。此固二錄已載而未詳者，敢以聞于當宁。
第二問
孫希夔
同考試官敎諭廖批〔惓惓擇官正學，歸本〕〔皇上之聖德聖政爲身敎，忠愛之意藹然。〕
考試官學正吳批〔發揚敎本殆盡。〕
考試官敎授顧批〔知本之論，錄之。〕
帝王所以衍昌隆之祚者，惟繼體之良而已矣；所以善裕後之謨者，惟敎本之端而已矣。蓋儲君，天下大本也。上而天命，下而人心，遠而國祚，胥係焉。是故養之宜愼也，望之宜仁也，曲成之宜盡道也，翊贊之宜擇官而得人也。毓德貴豫，而身敎要也。《易》
translation_en:
…his plans for civil government shine forth magnificently, matching the luminous sweep of the Milky Way, and the transforming influence of harmonious government can spread everywhere. Applied to the ordering of military affairs, his sagely martial power shines abroad, matching thunder in its awe-inspiring force, and government endowed with imposing authority can be established. Truly, he surpasses Kings Wen, Wu, and Xuan of old, making the Han, Tang, and Song seem paltry, yet claiming no credit for himself. These matters are already recorded in the two records but have not been fully explained; I venture to bring them to Your Majesty’s attention.
Second Question
Sun Xikui
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: 〔He earnestly advocates selecting officials and rectifying learning, grounding everything in〕〔His Majesty’s sagely virtue and sagely government as teaching by personal example. His loyal devotion is abundantly evident.〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Director: 〔He expounds the foundations of education almost exhaustively.〕
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: 〔An argument that understands the fundamentals. Include it in the record.〕
The means by which emperors and kings perpetuate the blessings of flourishing rule lie solely in the excellence of their successors. The means by which they perfect their plans to provide for posterity lie solely in setting the foundations of education right. For the heir apparent is the great foundation of all under Heaven. Above, Heaven’s mandate; below, the hearts of the people; and far into the future, the dynasty’s enduring good fortune—all depend upon him. Therefore, care must be exercised in nurturing him; expectations for him should be humane; every proper means should be employed to bring him to full maturity; and officials who assist him must be selected so that suitable men are obtained. In nurturing virtue, an early start is prized, and teaching by personal example is essential. The Book of Changes…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰蒙以養正聖功也詩曰穆穆皇皇宜君
宜王教之功大矣哉執事發策惓惓以
國本為念至計也敢不述所聞以對胄子之
教昉于虞書備于周官而莫詳于文王世
子之篇古者天子之元子衆子皆入大學
蓋聖帝明君思深慮遠不欲愛養于深宮
富貴之中而得優游于禮義相先之地以
觀其學業無非以曲成之也爰宅后夔典
樂司教俾聲律宣暢性情交洽完其直溫
===
寬栗剛簡之德夫德治之基也導其和協
于中則聖功裕而王道備矣此教太子之
則也夏商立教無非禮樂禮樂交錯而恭
敬溫文之德發焉夏典之貽甘盤之學伊
訓之飭教法靡不詳翊贊靡不選而養成
儲德其道有繇也周官師氏教國子以六
德六行即教之以事而喻諸德者也保氏
養國子以六藝六儀即慎其身以輔翼之
而歸諸道者也三公八舍莫非弼亮九德
punctuated:
曰：「蒙以養正，聖功也。」《詩》曰：「穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。」教之功大矣哉！執事發策，惓惓以國本為念，至計也。敢不述所聞以對？胄子之教昉于《虞書》，備于《周官》，而莫詳于《文王世子》之篇。古者，天子之元子、衆子皆入大學。蓋聖帝明君思深慮遠，不欲愛養于深宮富貴之中，而得優游于禮義相先之地，以觀其學業，無非以曲成之也。爰宅后夔，典樂司教，俾聲律宣暢，性情交洽，完其直溫、寬栗、剛簡之德。夫德，治之基也。導其和協于中，則聖功裕而王道備矣。此教太子之則也。

夏商立教，無非禮樂。禮樂交錯，而恭敬溫文之德發焉。《夏典》之貽，甘盤之學，《伊訓》之飭，教法靡不詳，翊贊靡不選，而養成儲德，其道有繇也。《周官》師氏教國子以六德六行，即教之以事而喻諸德者也；保氏養國子以六藝六儀，即慎其身以輔翼之而歸諸道者也。三公八舍，莫非弼亮九德，
translation_en:
…says: “To nurture correctness in the untutored is the work of a sage.” The Book of Odes says: “Reverent and splendid, fit to be a lord, fit to be a king.” Great indeed is the achievement of education! In setting this policy question, you have shown an earnest concern for the foundation of the state: this is foresight of the highest order. How could I dare not recount what I have learned in reply? The education of the sons of the nobility first appears in the Documents of Yu, is fully provided for in the Offices of Zhou, and is described nowhere more thoroughly than in the chapter “King Wen as Heir Apparent.” In antiquity, the Son of Heaven’s eldest son and his other sons all entered the Grand School. Sage emperors and enlightened rulers gave this deep thought and considered its distant consequences. They did not wish their sons to be pampered amid the wealth and rank of the secluded palace, but to enjoy ample scope for learning in a place where each encouraged the others in ritual propriety and righteousness. They could thus observe their sons’ progress in learning; all of this served to bring them to full development through attentive guidance. Accordingly, Kui was appointed to direct music and oversee education, so that musical tones and measures might flow freely and their dispositions and feelings become harmonious, perfecting the virtues of being upright yet gentle, tolerant yet firm, and resolute yet unassuming. Virtue is the foundation of government. If they are guided toward inner harmony, the work of the sage will flourish and the kingly Way will be complete. This is the model for educating the heir apparent.

The Xia and Shang established their teaching entirely through ritual and music. As ritual and music worked together, the virtues of reverence, respect, gentleness, and refinement emerged. In the legacy of the Canons of Xia, the learning imparted by Gan Pan, and the admonitions of the Instructions of Yi, methods of teaching were invariably thorough, and those who assisted and guided were invariably carefully chosen. Thus there was a means by which the heir’s virtue could be nurtured to maturity. In the Offices of Zhou, the Preceptor taught the sons of the state’s nobility the six virtues and six forms of conduct: this meant teaching them through practical affairs and thereby bringing them to understand virtue. The Protector nurtured them through the six arts and six forms of deportment: this meant exercising care over his own conduct in order to assist and guide them, bringing them to the Way. The Three Dukes and the eight attendants [?] all assisted in fostering the nine virtues…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
四輔莫非儀刑郎衞之屬掌于宮正兵衞
之屬掌于宮伯內外宮府統于太宰此敎
之有其人也絃誦禮樂殊其事干戈羽籥
異其舞春夏秋冬隨其時庠序瞽宗別其
地撻以伯禽稽以國倅此敎之盡其法也
然其本則在由虞庠之樂嚴胄齒之禮觀
太傅之德行以篤父子君臣長幼之倫德
成而敎尊敎尊而官正官正而國治書曰
一人元良萬邦以貞詩曰下武維周世有
===
哲王此三代所以有道之長也歟漢唐而
下官非不備法非不具然失愼選之宜乏
貽謀之善是故法術數卷而刻薄基矣戒
子一書而典刑失矣帝範有篇元良有述
而實用則未聞矣此君德難成而治不唐
虞三代若也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
應天啓運開萬世不拔之基建
大本堂延訪儒彥以充輔導嘗伏讀
punctuated:
四輔莫非儀刑。郎衞之屬掌于宮正，兵衞之屬掌于宮伯，內外宮府統于太宰，此敎之有其人也。絃誦禮樂殊其事，干戈羽籥異其舞，春夏秋冬隨其時，庠序瞽宗別其地，撻以伯禽，稽以國倅，此敎之盡其法也。然其本則在由虞庠之樂，嚴胄齒之禮，觀太傅之德行，以篤父子、君臣、長幼之倫。德成而敎尊，敎尊而官正，官正而國治。《書》曰：「一人元良，萬邦以貞。」《詩》曰：「下武維周，世有哲王。」此三代所以有道之長也歟！
漢唐而下，官非不備，法非不具，然失愼選之宜，乏貽謀之善。是故法術數卷而刻薄基矣，《戒子》一書而典刑失矣。《帝範》有篇，《元良》有述，而實用則未聞矣。此君德難成，而治不唐虞三代若也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，應天啓運，開萬世不拔之基，建大本堂，延訪儒彥以充輔導。嘗伏讀
translation_en:
…The Four Assistants all served as models. The palace gentlemen and guards were under the Palace Rectifier; the armed guards were under the Palace Earl; and the inner and outer palace administrations were brought together under the Grand Steward. Thus education had the right men to conduct it. Playing strings, recitation, ritual, and music each had their distinct activities; shields and halberds, feathers and flutes distinguished the dances. Instruction followed the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, and took place in distinct institutions—the xiang and xu schools and the Hall of the Blind Musicians. Discipline was administered even to Bo Qin, and the sons of nobles were examined. Thus education employed its methods to the full. Yet its foundation lay in following the music of the Yu school, strictly observing the rites governing the precedence of age among noble scions, and looking to the Grand Preceptor’s virtuous conduct, thereby strengthening the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, and elder and younger. When virtue was perfected, instruction was honored; when instruction was honored, officials were upright; when officials were upright, the state was well governed. The Book of Documents says: “When the one man is supremely good, the myriad states are set right.” The Book of Odes says: “Continuing their predecessors’ achievements was Zhou; generation after generation it had wise kings.” Was this not why the Three Dynasties so long possessed the Way?
From the Han and Tang onward, offices were by no means lacking, nor were methods incomplete. Yet proper care in selecting men was lost, and sound plans for posterity were wanting. Thus a few volumes on laws and techniques of rule laid the foundation for harshness, while a single Admonition to a Son marked the loss of exemplary standards. There were chapters of the Model for Emperors and writings entitled The Good Heir, but we have heard of no practical application. This is why a ruler’s virtue was difficult to perfect, and government failed to equal that of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties.
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who responded to Heaven and inaugurated the dynastic destiny, establishing an unshakable foundation for ten thousand generations. He founded the Hall of the Great Foundation and invited distinguished Confucian scholars to serve as tutors and guides. I have reverently read …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇明祖訓而得七善焉防微一也持守二也治
道三也脩身四也齊家五也重民命六也
戒黷武七也有
曰輔導得賢人各盡職合抱之木必以授良
匠萬金之璧不以付拙工此嚴
命詹同者然也有
曰繼體之君生長富貴多忽而不務此申
敕李善長者然也
太祖儲貳之誨可謂萬世法程矣
===
成祖文皇帝
繼天紹統衍萬世靈長之業勉力學問之誨諄
諄于楊林文事武備之敎惓惓于瓦剌伏
覩
文華寶鑑而得五紀焉推昭鑒之意一也集
