前古之嘉言二也採昔人之善行三也備
脩已之要四也寓治人之理五也有
曰令德所成本于天賦養正之學實弘聖功
此見于學士楊榮之
punctuated:
《皇明祖訓》，而得七善焉：防微，一也；持守，二也；治道，三也；脩身，四也；齊家，五也；重民命，六也；戒黷武，七也。有曰：「輔導得賢，人各盡職。合抱之木，必以授良匠；萬金之璧，不以付拙工。」此嚴命詹同者然也。有曰：「繼體之君，生長富貴，多忽而不務。」此申敕李善長者然也。太祖儲貳之誨，可謂萬世法程矣。
成祖文皇帝繼天紹統，衍萬世靈長之業。勉力學問之誨，諄諄于楊林；文事武備之敎，惓惓于瓦剌。伏覩《文華寶鑑》，而得五紀焉：推昭鑒之意，一也；集前古之嘉言，二也；採昔人之善行，三也；備脩已之要，四也；寓治人之理，五也。有曰：「令德所成，本于天賦；養正之學，實弘聖功。」此見于學士楊榮之
translation_en:
…the Imperial Ming Ancestral Instructions (Huang Ming zuxun), and found seven excellent principles therein: first, guarding against troubles at their slightest beginnings; second, holding fast to what has been established; third, the way of government; fourth, cultivating oneself; fifth, ordering the family; sixth, valuing the lives of the people; and seventh, avoiding reckless warfare. One passage says: “Secure worthy men as guides, and let each fulfill his duties. Timber so large that it takes both arms to encircle it must be entrusted to a skilled carpenter; a jade disk worth ten thousand pieces of gold must not be handed to a clumsy craftsman.” Such was the stern command given to Zhan Tong. Another passage says: “A ruler who inherits the throne grows up amid wealth and rank, and often neglects this and fails to apply himself.” Such was the repeated admonition to Li Shanchang. Taizu’s instructions for the heir apparent may indeed be called a model for all generations.
Emperor Wen, Chengzu, succeeded to Heaven’s mandate and continued the imperial line, extending an imperial enterprise destined to endure for countless generations. His exhortations to diligent study were repeatedly delivered to Yang Lin [?]; his instruction concerning civil affairs and military preparedness was earnestly given in connection with Wala (the Oirats) [?]. I respectfully examined the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian) and found five guiding principles therein: first, developing the purpose of providing an illuminating mirror; second, assembling admirable sayings from antiquity; third, selecting the good deeds of men of the past; fourth, fully presenting the essentials of self-cultivation [?]; and fifth, embodying the principles of governing others. One passage says: “The attainment of excellent virtue has its basis in Heaven’s endowment; learning that nurtures rectitude truly enlarges the accomplishments of the sage.” This appears in Academician Yang Rong’s …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
敕也有
曰古人之治皆有其道生知之聖亦資問學
此見于翰林胡廣之
諭也
成祖儲貳之教可謂萬世蓍策矣
宣宗章皇帝親詞翰選文學留神儲教則有
帝訓之二十五篇昉於君德之奉天竟於馭夷
而安夏修齊治平之道備矣
憲宗純皇帝選儒臣充宮僚留心繼體則有
===
文華大訓之四卷始于進學養德終于厚倫
明治內外交脩之道詳矣
歷朝所重惟在儲養宜
聖子
神孫重光奕葉也我
皇上
中天履祚蚤建
元良海內忻忻歌麟趾之祥仰敬承之德三
載于茲矣然
punctuated:
敕也。有曰：「古人之治，皆有其道；生知之聖，亦資問學。」此見于翰林胡廣之諭也。成祖儲貳之教，可謂萬世蓍策矣。
宣宗章皇帝親詞翰，選文學，留神儲教，則有《帝訓》之二十五篇，昉於君德之奉天，竟於馭夷而安夏，修齊治平之道備矣。
憲宗純皇帝選儒臣充宮僚，留心繼體，則有《文華大訓》之四卷，始于進學養德，終于厚倫明治，內外交脩之道詳矣。
歷朝所重，惟在儲養，宜聖子神孫重光奕葉也。我皇上中天履祚，蚤建元良，海內忻忻，歌麟趾之祥，仰敬承之德，三載于茲矣。然
translation_en:
…in the edict. Another passage reads: “The ancients all had their proper ways of governing; even sages born with knowledge relied upon inquiry and study.” This appears in the instructions addressed to Hu Guang of the Hanlin Academy. Chengzu’s teaching of the heir apparent may indeed be called a divinatory guide for ten thousand generations.
Emperor Xuanzong Zhang personally attended to literary composition and calligraphy, selected men of literary learning, and devoted his attention to educating the heir apparent. Thus there were the twenty-five chapters of Imperial Instructions (Dixun), beginning with the ruler’s virtue in serving Heaven and ending with controlling the foreign peoples and bringing peace to the Chinese realm. The Way of cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world was fully set forth therein.
Emperor Xianzong Chun selected Confucian officials to serve as palace staff and gave careful thought to the succession. Thus there were the four juan of Grand Instructions of Literary Splendor (Wenhua daxun), beginning with advancing learning and nurturing virtue and ending with strengthening human relationships and making government enlightened. The Way of cultivating both the inner self and outward conduct was explained in detail therein.
What successive reigns prized above all was the nurturing of the heir apparent. It is fitting, therefore, that sage sons and divine grandsons should renew their brilliance generation after generation. Our emperor ascended the throne at the center of Heaven and early established the heir apparent. All within the seas rejoiced, singing of the auspicious sign celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hoofs” and looking up to the virtue of reverently carrying on the inheritance. Three years have now passed. Yet…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
岐嶷天表問學神功
緝煕淵源後先光裕固無容贊者第毓德貴
豫而作聖為難養之可不慎望之可不仁
乎我
朝設立
東宮官僚視古獨詳師保賓客多大臣兼之
而諸司職務掌於詹事賛相獻納職在庶
子而中允副之諭德隨事而諭于道也賛
善陳古以箴也司直司諫彈劾糾舉規諫
===
駁正也掌圖書備供進則有洗馬之職書
以正字禮以司儀官屬森森備矣記曰不
必備惟其人則慎選之道宜講也故坊局
庶官必得老成耆舊傅德保躬如周公之
多聞道順太公之誠立敢斷召公之廉潔
切直然後
睿學有資而日進人才難得而遴選惟公
今日可無豫擇乎我
朝教育
punctuated: 岐嶷天表，問學神功，緝煕淵源，後先光裕，固無容贊者。第毓德貴豫，而作聖為難，養之可不慎，望之可不仁乎？我朝設立東宮官僚，視古獨詳。師保賓客，多大臣兼之；而諸司職務，掌於詹事；賛相獻納，職在庶子，而中允副之；諭德隨事而諭于道也；賛善陳古以箴也；司直、司諫，彈劾糾舉，規諫駁正也。掌圖書，備供進，則有洗馬之職；書以正字，禮以司儀，官屬森森備矣。記曰：「不必備，惟其人。」則慎選之道宜講也。故坊局庶官，必得老成耆舊，傅德保躬，如周公之多聞道順、太公之誠立敢斷、召公之廉潔切直，然後睿學有資而日進。人才難得，而遴選惟公，今日可無豫擇乎？我朝教育
translation_en:
…His precocious bearing is Heaven-bestowed, and his achievement in inquiry and learning divinely endowed. The sources of his ever-brightening virtue, and the glory and abundance transmitted from predecessors to successors, assuredly admit of no further praise. Yet nurturing virtue must begin early, and becoming a sage is difficult. Can we be anything but careful in nurturing him, or anything but benevolent in our expectations of him?

Our dynasty’s establishment of officials for the Eastern Palace is exceptionally thorough compared with antiquity. The preceptors, guardians, and guest advisers are mostly senior ministers holding these posts concurrently. The Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent oversees the duties of the various offices. Assistance and the presentation of counsel are the responsibility of the Secretariat Supervisors, with the Secretariat Assistants as their deputies. The Admonishers instruct him in the Way as circumstances arise; the Counselors invoke antiquity to admonish him. The Directors of Rectitude and Remonstrators impeach and expose faults, offer corrective counsel, and challenge and rectify errors. The Librarians are charged with managing books and preparing them for presentation. For writing there are Proofreaders, and for ritual there are Directors of Ceremonial. The ranks of subordinate officials are fully arrayed.

The Record says: “There is no need to fill every post; what matters is finding the right men.” Thus the principles of careful selection deserve examination. The various officials of the secretariats and bureaus must therefore be mature and experienced men of long standing, able to guide his virtue and safeguard his person: men like the Duke of Zhou in his extensive learning and conformity to the Way, the Grand Duke in his steadfast sincerity and bold decisiveness, and the Duke of Shao in his integrity, purity, earnestness, and uprightness. Only then will the learning of the sagely prince have support and advance daily. Talented men are hard to find, and selection must be wholly impartial. Can we today dispense with choosing them in advance? Our dynasty’s education…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
太子程法視古特善中書令不復設而一切
軍國機務悉令啓聞
東宮僚不專設而特置諭德等官責令輔德
黜異端而進說六經去法術而商摧理道
郊廟有儀師傅有禮講讀有期春暖
東宮可出講書見于
宣宗之諭宮僚進講起立拱聽發于
憲宗之命出閤儀節彬彬盛矣書曰修厥身允
德協于下惟明后則教本之實宜講也故
===
深宮暇豫必防其習以正其趨而不徒爲
出閤講學之靡文如顧諟之訓無逸之警
敬義之戒時切切焉然後
令德有養而日成略儀文以求實學
今日可無豫定乎雖然有儀刑之道焉
皇太子聰明仁孝有成王之賢而所賴
文謨武烈垂範于上
躬行德教以督率之然後能
觀光揚烈以奉
punctuated:
太子程法視古特善，中書令不復設，而一切軍國機務悉令啓聞。東宮僚不專設，而特置諭德等官，責令輔德。黜異端而進說六經，去法術而商摧理道。郊廟有儀，師傅有禮，講讀有期。春暖，東宮可出講書，見于宣宗之諭；宮僚進講，起立拱聽，發于憲宗之命。出閤儀節，彬彬盛矣。《書》曰：「修厥身，允德協于下，惟明后。」則教本之實宜講也。故深宮暇豫，必防其習以正其趨，而不徒爲出閤講學之靡文。如顧諟之訓、無逸之警、敬義之戒，時切切焉，然後令德有養而日成。略儀文以求實學，今日可無豫定乎？

雖然，有儀刑之道焉。皇太子聰明仁孝，有成王之賢，而所賴文謨武烈，垂範于上，躬行德教以督率之，然後能觀光揚烈，以奉
translation_en:
…the regulations for educating the crown prince are especially good when compared with those of antiquity. The office of Director of the Secretariat is no longer established, yet all critical military and state affairs are ordered to be reported to him. A separate staff for the Eastern Palace is not maintained, but offices such as Admonisher are specially established and charged with assisting his moral development. Heterodox teachings are rejected, and the Six Classics are expounded; techniques of manipulation are discarded, and moral principles are discussed [?]. There are ceremonies for the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, proper courtesies toward his preceptors, and appointed times for lectures and readings. That the crown prince may come out to receive lectures on books when spring grows warm appears in Xuanzong’s instructions; that he should rise and listen with hands respectfully clasped when palace officials lecture derives from Xianzong’s command. The ceremonial forms for his emergence from the inner palace to study are splendidly refined. The Book of Documents says: “Cultivating his person, with virtue that truly brings harmony to those below—such is an enlightened ruler.” Thus the substantive foundation of education deserves consideration. During his leisure within the secluded palace, his habits must be guarded and his inclinations set right, so that his emergence for lectures does not become mere ornamental ceremony. Such teachings as keeping Heaven’s bright mandate constantly in view, the warning against ease, and the admonition concerning reverence and righteousness must continually be pressed upon him. Only then will his excellent virtue be nourished and develop day by day. Can we today fail to determine in advance how to give less weight to ceremonial forms and seek substantive learning?

Nevertheless, there is also the way of teaching through an exemplary model. The imperial crown prince is intelligent, humane, and filial, possessing the worthiness of King Cheng. Yet he depends upon the civil counsels and martial achievements that furnish an example from above, and upon personal practice of moral instruction to guide and direct him. Only then can he behold that glory and carry forward those achievements, so as to uphold…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天命甞攷
二祖悟唐虞精一之傳識人心虛靈之體實德
實學其見於
聖謨垂於
心法者皆儀刑之本然則
祖訓寶鑑諸書豈徒以言為訓者邪我
皇上日新
聖學休隆聖治清燕之暇仰窺
瑤函或標揭心得要㫖
===
命宮臣講解或摘取羣書大義俾
太子習讀而又體仁以教之愛修禮以教之
讓敦信以教之不欺勤政以教之不惰任
賢以教之不惑納諫以教之不拒明賞罰
而教之不僭不濫躬勤政而教之無怠無
荒則觀法乆而
文子文孫當克承
明德而
天命永凝人心永附
punctuated: 天命。甞攷二祖，悟唐虞精一之傳，識人心虛靈之體，實德實學，其見於聖謨、垂於心法者，皆儀刑之本。然則《祖訓》《寶鑑》諸書，豈徒以言為訓者邪？我皇上日新聖學，休隆聖治，清燕之暇，仰窺瑤函，或標揭心得要㫖，命宮臣講解；或摘取羣書大義，俾太子習讀。而又體仁以教之愛，修禮以教之讓，敦信以教之不欺，勤政以教之不惰，任賢以教之不惑，納諫以教之不拒，明賞罰而教之不僭不濫，躬勤政而教之無怠無荒。則觀法乆而文子文孫當克承明德，而天命永凝，人心永附，
translation_en:
…the Mandate of Heaven. I have examined how the two founding emperors comprehended the teaching of refinement and single-mindedness transmitted from Tang and Yu, and understood the empty and numinous constitution of the human mind. Their genuine virtue and genuine learning, manifested in their sagely counsels and handed down in their teachings concerning the mind, are all foundations for emulation. Thus, could such books as the Ancestral Instructions and the Precious Mirror provide instruction through words alone?

Our Emperor daily renews his sagely learning and brings his sagely governance to flourishing perfection. In moments of quiet leisure, he reverently studies the precious volumes. Sometimes he singles out essential points that he has personally grasped and orders the palace officials to expound them; sometimes he selects the principal meanings of various books for the Crown Prince to study and recite. Moreover, by embodying benevolence he teaches him love; by cultivating ritual propriety he teaches him deference; by strengthening trustworthiness he teaches him not to deceive; by attending diligently to government he teaches him not to be indolent; by employing the worthy he teaches him not to be misled; by accepting remonstrance he teaches him not to reject counsel. By making rewards and punishments clear, he teaches him neither to bestow rewards improperly nor to punish indiscriminately; by personally attending diligently to government, he teaches him neither slackness nor neglect. Then, through prolonged observation and emulation, his cultivated sons and grandsons will be able to carry forward his illustrious virtue, and the Mandate of Heaven will remain forever secure, the hearts of the people forever attached…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國祚其永昌矣草茅鄙見不識以爲何如
第三問
湯顯祖
同考試官教諭陳批世儒類以圖書說經此作
推原聖人本意反覆辯論足解千古之疑
同考試官教諭陳批據理析數考究精詳
考試官學正吳批是策大有功于聖經
考試官教授顧批得理學之奧宜錄
聖人之作經也不遺乎數而未甞倚于數
===
儒者之說經也貴依於理而不可鑿乎理
蓋天下之數莫非理也天下之理莫非天
也聖人默契乎天自能明天下之道而天
有所不必畀聖人神明乎理自能周天下
之數而數有所不足拘自世儒喜爲奇說
以神異聖人之事推象數以原經而經滯
務爲過求以自附聖人之學衍意見以傳
經而經離求愈奇故說愈鑿說愈鑿故旨
愈繁而聖人之道愈失其初矣雖其爲學
punctuated:
國祚其永昌矣。草茅鄙見，不識以爲何如？

第三問
湯顯祖

同考試官教諭陳批：世儒類以圖書說經，此作推原聖人本意，反覆辯論，足解千古之疑。
同考試官教諭陳批：據理析數，考究精詳。
考試官學正吳批：是策大有功于聖經。
考試官教授顧批：得理學之奧，宜錄。

聖人之作經也，不遺乎數，而未甞倚于數；儒者之說經也，貴依於理，而不可鑿乎理。蓋天下之數，莫非理也；天下之理，莫非天也。聖人默契乎天，自能明天下之道，而天有所不必畀；聖人神明乎理，自能周天下之數，而數有所不足拘。自世儒喜爲奇說，以神異聖人之事，推象數以原經，而經滯；務爲過求，以自附聖人之學，衍意見以傳經，而經離。求愈奇，故說愈鑿；說愈鑿，故旨愈繁，而聖人之道愈失其初矣。雖其爲學
translation_en:
…the dynasty’s fortunes will flourish forever. Such is the humble opinion of this unworthy man of the countryside; I do not know what you will think of it.

Third Question
Tang Xianzu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Scholars of the age generally explain the classics through the River Chart and the Luo Writing. This essay traces the sages’ original intentions and argues its case from every side, sufficiently resolving doubts that have persisted through the ages.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: It analyzes numbers on the basis of principle; its investigations are precise and thorough.

Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: This policy essay makes a substantial contribution to understanding the sages’ classics.

Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: It grasps the profundities of the Learning of Principle and merits selection.

In composing the classics, the sages did not neglect numbers, yet they never relied upon numbers. In explaining the classics, scholars should prize adherence to principle, yet must not force their interpretations of it. For all numbers under Heaven embody principle, and all principle under Heaven derives from Heaven. Through their tacit accord with Heaven, the sages could naturally illuminate the Way throughout the world, without Heaven necessarily having to bestow anything upon them. Through their spiritual insight into principle, the sages could naturally comprehend all numbers under Heaven, yet numbers could not fully constrain them.

Scholars of later ages have delighted in devising extraordinary explanations to make the sages’ deeds seem supernatural. They extrapolate from images and numbers to trace the origins of the classics, thereby encumbering the classics. They insist on pursuing inquiry to excess in order to affiliate themselves with the sages’ learning, elaborating their own opinions to transmit the classics, thereby estranging the classics from their meaning. The more extraordinary their inquiries, the more forced their explanations; the more forced their explanations, the more convoluted their interpretations. Thus the Way of the sages increasingly loses its original character. Although their learning…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
未必皆叛於聖人以是爲作經之本可乎
嗚呼吾獨怪夫六經之㫖如日中天未甞
托異徵祕以求信于天下而後世儒者亂
之也今夫易卦何昉乎伏羲畫之爲文字
之祖也當其時鴻濛未闢人文未啓天地
萬物之情陰陽鬼神之祕寓於法象而易
行乎其中矣伏羲神而明之以定畫焉故
易曰仰則觀象于天俯則觀法于地觀鳥
獸之文與地之宜于是始作八卦此作易
===
之本也洪範何昉乎箕子陳之是神禹之
傳也當其時玄圭告功文命未布立極綏
民之具事天治人之本藏于幾微而疇具
乎其中矣神禹會而通之以作範焉故書
曰禹乃嗣興天乃錫禹洪範九疇彝倫攸
敘此敘疇之本也二聖人者運而精神旣
有以丕隆休烈聚而心術又足以開先世
敎雖其聖德格天河洛效瑞圖書之數未
必不可通于經而聖人取義也大立敎也
punctuated:
未必皆叛於聖人，以是爲作經之本，可乎？嗚呼！吾獨怪夫六經之㫖，如日中天，未甞托異徵祕以求信于天下，而後世儒者亂之也。

今夫易卦何昉乎？伏羲畫之，爲文字之祖也。當其時，鴻濛未闢，人文未啓，天地萬物之情、陰陽鬼神之祕，寓於法象，而易行乎其中矣。伏羲神而明之，以定畫焉。故《易》曰：「仰則觀象于天，俯則觀法于地，觀鳥獸之文與地之宜，于是始作八卦。」此作易之本也。

洪範何昉乎？箕子陳之，是神禹之傳也。當其時，玄圭告功，文命未布，立極綏民之具、事天治人之本，藏于幾微，而疇具乎其中矣。神禹會而通之，以作範焉。故《書》曰：「禹乃嗣興，天乃錫禹洪範九疇，彝倫攸敘。」此敘疇之本也。

二聖人者，運而精神，旣有以丕隆休烈；聚而心術，又足以開先世敎。雖其聖德格天，河洛效瑞，圖書之數未必不可通于經，而聖人取義也大，立敎也
translation_en:
…their learning may not all depart from the sages, but can this be taken as the basis on which the classics were composed? Alas! What particularly perplexes me is that the purport of the Six Classics is like the sun at midday: they never relied on marvels or invoked mysteries to gain the trust of the world, yet later Confucian scholars threw them into confusion.

Now, where did the hexagrams of the Changes originate? Fuxi drew them, and they were the progenitors of writing. At that time, primordial chaos had not yet opened out, and human culture had not yet begun. The true circumstances of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, and the mysteries of yin and yang, ghosts and spirits, were embodied in patterns and images, with change operating within them. Fuxi apprehended them with spiritual insight and thereby fixed the lines. Thus the Book of Changes says: “Looking upward, he observed images in Heaven; looking downward, he observed patterns on Earth. He observed the markings of birds and beasts and what was suited to the land. Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams.” This was the basis for composing the Changes.

Where did the Great Plan originate? Jizi expounded it, but it was a transmission from the divine Yu. At that time, the dark jade tablet proclaimed his achievement, but his civil ordinances had not yet spread [?]. The means of establishing the supreme standard and bringing peace to the people, and the foundations of serving Heaven and governing humanity, lay concealed in the subtlest workings of things; the categories were already fully present within them. The divine Yu brought these together and comprehended their interconnections, thereby creating the Plan. Thus the Book of Documents says: “Yu then arose to succeed him. Heaven thereupon bestowed upon Yu the nine categories of the Great Plan, and the constant relationships were duly ordered.” This was the basis for setting out the categories.

These two sages, putting their spiritual powers into operation [?], already possessed the means greatly to advance their glorious achievements; concentrating their arts of the mind [?], they were also fully capable of inaugurating instruction for the world. Although their sagely virtue reached Heaven, and the Yellow River and the Luo River manifested auspicious signs, and although the numbers of the River Chart and Luo Writing might indeed be connected with the classics, the meanings the sages drew from them were grand, and the teachings they established were …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
正惟其理之可以信天下而不必乎象數
之模倣瑞應之撫飾也何至後世異說之
紛紛哉其謂龍馬出河伏羲遂則其文以
畫八卦神龜負文而列於背有數至九禹
遂因而第之以成九類此孔安國之說也
其謂伏羲繼天而王受河圖而畫之八卦
禹治洪水賜洛書法而陳之九疇此劉歆
之言也其謂河圖之文七前六後八左九
右洛書之文九前一後三左七右四前左
===
二前右八後左六後右此關朗之論也宋
儒邵子亦曰圓者河圖之數方者洛書之
文故羲文因之而造易禹箕敘之而作範
嗚呼信如是則易出于圖無圖卽無卦矣
範出于書無書卽無疇矣而聖人作經之
本不旣遠乎其訛起于緯候之書謂河以
通乾出天苞洛以流坤出地符聖人必有
神物以授之之說漢儒惑之牽合文致不
求聖人之實迨宋儒喜于附聖而輒取之
punctuated:
正。惟其理之可以信天下，而不必乎象數之模倣、瑞應之撫飾也，何至後世異說之紛紛哉？其謂龍馬出河，伏羲遂則其文以畫八卦；神龜負文而列於背，有數至九，禹遂因而第之以成九類：此孔安國之說也。其謂伏羲繼天而王，受河圖而畫之八卦；禹治洪水，賜洛書，法而陳之九疇：此劉歆之言也。其謂河圖之文七前六後，八左九右；洛書之文九前一後，三左七右，四前左，二前右，八後左，六後右：此關朗之論也。宋儒邵子亦曰：「圓者河圖之數，方者洛書之文。」故羲文因之而造易，禹箕敘之而作範。
嗚呼！信如是，則易出于圖，無圖卽無卦矣；範出于書，無書卽無疇矣。而聖人作經之本，不旣遠乎？其訛起于緯候之書，謂河以通乾出天苞，洛以流坤出地符，聖人必有神物以授之之說。漢儒惑之，牽合文致，不求聖人之實；迨宋儒喜于附聖，而輒取之，
translation_en:
…correct. It is their principles that can command the trust of all under Heaven; there is no need to imitate images and numbers or embellish auspicious portents. How, then, did so many divergent explanations arise in later ages? The claim that a dragon-horse emerged from the Yellow River and Fu Xi accordingly modeled the eight trigrams on its markings, and that a divine tortoise bore markings arrayed upon its back, with numbers reaching nine, which Yu accordingly arranged into nine categories—this is Kong Anguo’s explanation. The claim that Fu Xi succeeded Heaven as king, received the River Chart, and drew from it the eight trigrams, while Yu, in controlling the flood, was granted the Luo Writing and modeled upon it his exposition of the nine categories—these are Liu Xin’s words. The claim that the markings of the River Chart placed seven at the front, six at the back, eight on the left, and nine on the right, while those of the Luo Writing placed nine at the front, one at the back, three on the left, seven on the right, four at the front left, two at the front right, eight at the back left, and six at the back right—this is Guan Lang’s account. Master Shao, a Song Confucian, also said: “What is round is the numerical configuration of the River Chart; what is square is the pattern of the Luo Writing.” Thus Fu Xi and King Wen relied upon these to create the Changes, and Yu and Jizi set them in order to compose the Great Plan.
Alas! If this were indeed so, the Changes would derive from the Chart: without the Chart, there would be no trigrams. The Great Plan would derive from the Writing: without the Writing, there would be no categories. Would this not already be far removed from the foundation upon which the sages composed the classics? This error arose in apocryphal and prognostic writings, with their claim that the Yellow River, communicating with Qian, brought forth Heaven’s treasure, and the Luo River, channeling Kun, brought forth Earth’s token—that the sages must necessarily have had divine objects to impart these things to them. The Han Confucians were misled by this, forcing connections and straining interpretations without seeking the truth about the sages. By the time of the Song Confucians, they delighted in associating themselves with the sages and readily adopted these claims…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
復强證于易傳圖書之一言不知孔子甞
言河出圖矣而奇偶之象未詳也甞言洛
出書矣而九一之數未悉也甞言聖人則
之矣而因圖畫卦因書立範未及也諸家
之言何祖乎夫觀鳥跡而製字因規矩而
制器藝也聖人恒必詳之顧此經學禎符
秘訣不與本文同傳而千載之下山人野
士創爲之說不幾于詭誕而不可從矣乎
況以圖之數析補八卦拘合強同多所難
===
信如使揭圖而示之孰爲一六而下孰爲
二七而上孰爲三八四九而左右孰爲乾
兌離震孰爲巽坎艮坤天之告人也何其
瀆因其上而上因其下而下因其左右而
左右因其乾兌離震以爲乾兌離震因其
巽坎艮坤以爲巽坎艮坤聖人之效天也
何其拘易旣如是作矣然則仰觀俯察者
又何物通德類情者又何事而易書本體
不在此而在彼邪以書之數參合九疇則
punctuated: 復强證于易傳圖書之一言，不知孔子甞言河出圖矣，而奇偶之象未詳也；甞言洛出書矣，而九一之數未悉也；甞言聖人則之矣，而因圖畫卦、因書立範未及也。諸家之言何祖乎？夫觀鳥跡而製字，因規矩而制器，藝也，聖人恒必詳之。顧此經學禎符秘訣，不與本文同傳，而千載之下，山人野士創爲之說，不幾于詭誕而不可從矣乎？況以圖之數析補八卦，拘合強同，多所難信。如使揭圖而示之，孰爲一六而下？孰爲二七而上？孰爲三八四九而左右？孰爲乾兌離震？孰爲巽坎艮坤？天之告人也何其瀆！因其上而上，因其下而下，因其左右而左右，因其乾兌離震以爲乾兌離震，因其巽坎艮坤以爲巽坎艮坤，聖人之效天也何其拘！易旣如是作矣，然則仰觀俯察者又何物？通德類情者又何事？而易書本體不在此而在彼邪？以書之數參合九疇，則
translation_en: …They further force corroboration from the single statement about the River Chart and Luo Writing in the Commentary on the Changes. They fail to recognize that although Confucius spoke of the River bringing forth a chart, he did not describe its configurations of odd and even numbers; although he spoke of the Luo bringing forth a writing, he did not specify its numbers, nine and one; and although he spoke of the sages taking these as their models, he did not mention drawing the trigrams from the Chart or establishing the Great Plan from the Writing. What authority, then, underlies the claims of these various scholars? Observing birds’ tracks to create written characters and using compasses and squares to fashion implements are technical arts, yet the sages invariably explained them in detail. But these auspicious tokens and secret formulas of classical learning were supposedly not transmitted together with the original texts; instead, recluses and men outside official life devised explanations of them a thousand years later. Does this not verge on the fantastic and preclude our accepting it? Moreover, dividing up and supplementing the Chart’s numbers to construct the eight trigrams, forcing correspondences and imposing identities, involves much that is difficult to believe. Suppose the Chart were unfolded and displayed: what makes one and six belong below, and two and seven above? What makes three and eight, and four and nine, belong on the left and right? What makes Qian, Dui, Li, and Zhen what they are? What makes Xun, Kan, Gen, and Kun what they are? How tediously explicit Heaven would be in instructing humanity! To place above whatever is above, below whatever is below, and left and right whatever is left and right; to make Qian, Dui, Li, and Zhen from its Qian, Dui, Li, and Zhen, and Xun, Kan, Gen, and Kun from its Xun, Kan, Gen, and Kun—how rigidly the sages would be copying Heaven! If the Changes was indeed composed in this way, then what were the things they observed above and examined below? What was involved in comprehending the powers of things and classifying their inherent dispositions? Could the essential substance of the Book of Changes lie there, in the Chart, rather than here, in these activities? If the numbers of the Luo Writing are correlated with the nine divisions of the Great Plan, then…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
陰陽奇偶俱未相當按類而求之五行何
以居下五事何以居上五紀何以居前左
而皇極何以居中邪八政何以居左稽疑
何以居右三德何以居後右而庶徵福極
何各專一位邪書之方位實不同于疇一
三五七九奇也而五行八政皇極稽疑福
極何以屬之奇二四六八偶也而五事五
紀三德庶徵何以屬之偶疇之名數又不
同于書如謂大義無取姑摘其自一至九
===
之文則又奚必縱橫黑白秘傳神授重煩
聖人第之而後成邪先儒劉長民謂伏羲
兼取圖書又謂九爲河圖十爲洛書蔣得
之謂先天圖爲河圖五行生成數爲洛書
諸說紛雜皆無定據而獨孔劉之言爲信
謬矣程子有云孔子感麟而作春秋麟不
出春秋豈不作如畫八卦因見河圖洛書
果無圖書八卦亦須作朱子亦謂伏羲仰
觀俯察遠求近取安知河圖非其中一事
punctuated:
陰陽奇偶俱未相當。按類而求之，五行何以居下？五事何以居上？五紀何以居前左，而皇極何以居中邪？八政何以居左？稽疑何以居右？三德何以居後右，而庶徵福極何各專一位邪？書之方位實不同于疇。一三五七九，奇也，而五行八政皇極稽疑福極何以屬之奇？二四六八，偶也，而五事五紀三德庶徵何以屬之偶？疇之名數又不同于書。如謂大義無取，姑摘其自一至九之文，則又奚必縱橫黑白、秘傳神授，重煩聖人第之而後成邪？
先儒劉長民謂伏羲兼取圖書，又謂九爲河圖，十爲洛書。蔣得之謂先天圖爲河圖，五行生成數爲洛書。諸說紛雜，皆無定據，而獨孔劉之言爲信，謬矣！程子有云：「孔子感麟而作春秋，麟不出，春秋豈不作？如畫八卦，因見河圖洛書，果無圖書，八卦亦須作。」朱子亦謂：「伏羲仰觀俯察，遠求近取，安知河圖非其中一事？」
translation_en:
…yin and yang, and odd and even numbers, do not correspond in any case. If we examine them by category, why are the Five Phases placed below? Why are the Five Activities above? Why are the Five Regulators at the front left, and the August Ultimate in the center? Why are the Eight Affairs of Government on the left, and the Examination of Doubts on the right? Why are the Three Virtues at the rear right, while the Various Signs and the Blessings and Extremities each occupy a separate position? The spatial arrangement of the Luo Writing in fact differs from that of the Nine Categories. One, three, five, seven, and nine are odd numbers; why, then, are the Five Phases, Eight Affairs of Government, August Ultimate, Examination of Doubts, and Blessings and Extremities assigned to odd numbers? Two, four, six, and eight are even numbers; why, then, are the Five Activities, Five Regulators, Three Virtues, and Various Signs assigned to even numbers? The names and numerical ordering of the Categories likewise differ from the Luo Writing. If one says that their broader meaning is irrelevant and merely extracts the wording that runs from one to nine, why must there also be vertical and horizontal arrangements of black and white dots, secret transmission and divine bestowal, further troubling the sage to put them in order before the work could be complete?
The earlier scholar Liu Changmin maintained that Fu Xi drew on both the River Chart and the Luo Writing; he also maintained that the diagram with nine numbers was the River Chart, and that with ten was the Luo Writing. Jiang Dezhi maintained that the Diagram of the Prior Heaven was the River Chart, and that the numbers of generation and completion of the Five Phases constituted the Luo Writing. These various explanations are confused and conflicting, and none has firm evidence. To accept only the statements of Kong and Liu as trustworthy is mistaken! Master Cheng once said: “Confucius was moved by the appearance of the qilin to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals. Had the qilin not appeared, would the Spring and Autumn Annals therefore not have been composed? It is like drawing the Eight Trigrams upon seeing the River Chart and the Luo Writing: even if there had truly been no Chart or Writing, the Eight Trigrams would still have had to be made.” Master Zhu likewise said: “Fu Xi looked upward and observed, looked downward and examined, sought afar and drew upon what was near. How do we know that the River Chart was not merely one thing among these?”

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
二氏之論稍爲得之聖王達天明道而作
經禎符適見理固有然而謂必作于圖書
者非也蓋聖人之經主于理而後世擬之于
于數聖人之理得于天而後世擬之于怪
故不但原經者飾爲異說以誇世誣人也
世儒圖經傳經者往往惟新奇玄奧是務
分配離析以解經而經可明乎夫易者不
離象數而象數之理自不可窮然而有正
焉有變焉卦之明白較著者正也旁推而
===
衍之者變也伏羲八卦陰陽剛柔其理一
定變化盡于是矣故三代更帙易卦則同
而連山而歸藏而周易未嘗外伏羲所作
而别爲一易也乃邵子圖學以此爲周之
易而非伏羲之易别出横圖于前左右分
析以象天氣謂之圓圖于其中交加八宮
以象地類謂之方圖易於天氣地類蓋詳
矣奚俟夫圖而後見也且謂其必出於伏
羲旣規横以爲圓又填圓以爲方前列六
punctuated: 二氏之論稍爲得之。聖王達天明道而作經，禎符適見，理固有然，而謂必作于圖書者，非也。蓋聖人之經主于理，而後世擬之于于數；聖人之理得于天，而後世擬之于怪。故不但原經者飾爲異說，以誇世誣人也，世儒圖經傳經者，往往惟新奇玄奧是務，分配離析以解經，而經可明乎？夫易者，不離象數，而象數之理自不可窮，然而有正焉，有變焉。卦之明白較著者，正也；旁推而衍之者，變也。伏羲八卦，陰陽剛柔，其理一定，變化盡于是矣。故三代更帙，易卦則同，而連山，而歸藏，而周易，未嘗外伏羲所作而别爲一易也。乃邵子圖學，以此爲周之易，而非伏羲之易，别出横圖于前，左右分析以象天氣，謂之圓圖；于其中交加八宮以象地類，謂之方圖。易於天氣地類蓋詳矣，奚俟夫圖而後見也？且謂其必出於伏羲，旣規横以爲圓，又填圓以爲方，前列六
translation_en:
The arguments of these two masters come somewhat closer to the truth. The sage kings comprehended Heaven and illuminated the Way, and thus composed the classics. That auspicious signs should happen to appear was entirely consistent with principle; but to claim that the classics necessarily originated from the River Chart and the Luo Writing is wrong. The sages’ classics are grounded in principle, yet later generations interpret them through numbers; the sages derived their principles from Heaven, yet later generations interpret them through marvels. Thus it is not only those investigating the origins of the classics who embellish them with outlandish theories to impress the world and deceive others. Scholars of later ages who diagram and transmit the classics often devote themselves solely to novelty and abstruseness, assigning correspondences and splitting things apart to explain the classics. Can the classics be clarified this way?

The Changes is inseparable from images and numbers, and the principles of images and numbers are indeed inexhaustible. Nevertheless, there is the regular and there is the variant. What is plain and evident in the hexagrams is the regular; what is inferred by analogy and elaborated is the variant. In Fuxi’s eight trigrams, the principles of yin and yang, firmness and yielding, are fixed, and all transformations are encompassed within them. Thus, although the texts changed through the Three Dynasties, the hexagrams of the Changes remained the same. Neither the Linked Mountains (Lianshan), nor the Return to the Hidden (Guicang), nor the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi) departed from Fuxi’s creation to constitute a separate Changes.

Yet Master Shao’s study of diagrams treats this as the Changes of Zhou rather than the Changes of Fuxi, and separately presents a horizontal diagram at the front. He divides and analyzes it to the left and right to represent Heaven’s vital energies, calling this the circular diagram; within it he interlaces the Eight Palaces to represent the categories of Earth, calling this the square diagram. The Changes already treats Heaven’s vital energies and Earth’s categories in detail. Why should one have to wait for diagrams before these become apparent? Moreover, he claims that these must have come from Fuxi. Having curved the horizontal arrangement into a circle, he then fills out the circle to make a square. At the front he arrays the sixty-…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
十四卦于横圖後列一百二十八卦于圓
圖上古無言之易何若是紛紛哉易始于
一由太極而兩儀而四象而八卦生生之
序也未聞筆之圖以立卦天地山澤風雷
水火相合配偶此八卦對待之體乃別而
圖之爲先天由此行乎四時序于五方又
流行之用乃別而圖之爲後天何據也孔
子作傳于千百年之前邵子讀易而悟其
變推而衍之如此不應謂聖人之傳反爲
===
其圖說也近世黄東發著日抄極謂天地
定位一章必非先天卦位疑圖學之不可
從蓋彼謂先天在卦氣傳何爲舍而曰天
地定位彼謂後天在入用傳何爲舍而曰
帝出乎震繫辭一書語象變詳矣未甞一
及于圖且漢儒傳經近古未有以圖爲言
者圖學邵子之易也而可即謂聖人之易
也哉洪範者聖王治世大法其道盡于皇
極而終始意義聯貫而不可離是故有本
punctuated:
十四卦于横圖，後列一百二十八卦于圓圖。上古無言之易，何若是紛紛哉？易始于一，由太極而兩儀而四象而八卦，生生之序也，未聞筆之圖以立卦。天地山澤風雷水火，相合配偶，此八卦對待之體，乃別而圖之爲先天；由此行乎四時，序于五方，又流行之用，乃別而圖之爲後天，何據也？孔子作傳于千百年之前，邵子讀易而悟其變，推而衍之如此，不應謂聖人之傳反爲其圖說也。近世黄東發著《日抄》，極謂「天地定位」一章必非先天卦位，疑圖學之不可從。蓋彼謂先天在卦氣，傳何爲舍而曰「天地定位」？彼謂後天在入用，傳何爲舍而曰「帝出乎震」？《繫辭》一書，語象變詳矣，未甞一及于圖。且漢儒傳經近古，未有以圖爲言者。圖學，邵子之易也，而可即謂聖人之易也哉？

《洪範》者，聖王治世大法。其道盡于皇極，而終始意義聯貫而不可離，是故有本
translation_en:
…sixty-four hexagrams in the horizontal diagram at the front, followed by one hundred and twenty-eight hexagrams in the circular diagram. How could the wordless Changes of high antiquity have been so bewilderingly elaborate? The Changes begins with unity: from the Supreme Ultimate come the Two Modes, then the Four Images, then the Eight Trigrams. This is the sequence of generation upon generation. Never have we heard that a diagram was drawn to establish the hexagrams. Heaven and earth, mountain and lake, wind and thunder, water and fire join in corresponding pairs: this is the structure of the Eight Trigrams as opposed counterparts. Yet a separate diagram is made of this and called “Earlier Heaven.” From this they move through the four seasons and take their ordered places in the five directions: this, in turn, is their operation in circulation. Yet a separate diagram is made of this and called “Later Heaven.” What grounds are there for this? Confucius composed his commentaries hundreds and thousands of years earlier. Master Shao read the Changes, apprehended its transformations, and extrapolated and elaborated them in this manner. One should not claim that the sage’s commentaries were, on the contrary, explanations of Shao’s diagrams.

In more recent times, Huang Dongfa, in his Daily Notes (Richao), emphatically argued that the section beginning “Heaven and earth establish their positions” certainly did not describe the Earlier Heaven arrangement of the trigrams, questioning whether the learning of diagrams could be followed. For if, as its proponents say, Earlier Heaven concerns the vital energies of the trigrams, why does the commentary leave this aside and say, “Heaven and earth establish their positions”? If, as they say, Later Heaven concerns their coming into operation, why does the commentary leave this aside and say, “The Lord comes forth in Zhen”? The Appended Statements discusses images and transformations in detail, yet never once touches upon diagrams. Moreover, the Han scholars who transmitted the classics lived close to antiquity, yet none spoke in terms of diagrams. The learning of diagrams is Master Shao’s Changes; can it therefore simply be called the sage’s Changes?

The Great Plan (Hongfan) is the great law by which sage kings govern the world. Its Way is fully expressed in the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard, and its meaning is interconnected from beginning to end and cannot be separated. Thus there is a root…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉有枝焉前四疇皇極之體治天下之本
根也後四疇皇極之用治天下之枝葉也
讀洪範者當知天人合一至理聖人嚴感
應之機詳著五事修廢與五行徵應之論
特其理微妙不可迹拘耳劉向作洪範五
行傳其言某事致某災某災應某事捷若
形影破碎分析世以災異之學病之而遂
疑念用之疇或未可盡信夫人君事天如
孝子事親日候其顔色喜怒以為已之悖
===
順此所謂念也徵而休焉脩之當如是而
求其肅必時雨乂必時暘哲必時燠謀必
時寒聖必時風則難矣徵而咎焉廢之當
如是而求其狂必恒雨僭必恒暘豫必恒
燠急必恒寒蒙必恒風則舛矣聖人立教
論其理而奚必于類應之符邪惟其言理
故不祖于數而宋世蔡元定作皇極內篇
補洪範不傳之數以疇之目合書之九九
衍之而為八十一八十一衍之而為七百
punctuated:
焉，有枝焉。前四疇，皇極之體，治天下之本根也；後四疇，皇極之用，治天下之枝葉也。
讀洪範者，當知天人合一至理。聖人嚴感應之機，詳著五事修廢與五行徵應之論，特其理微妙，不可迹拘耳。劉向作《洪範五行傳》，其言某事致某災，某災應某事，捷若形影，破碎分析。世以災異之學病之，而遂疑念用之疇，或未可盡信。夫人君事天，如孝子事親，日候其顔色喜怒，以為已之悖順，此所謂念也。徵而休焉，脩之當如是，而求其肅必時雨，乂必時暘，哲必時燠，謀必時寒，聖必時風，則難矣。徵而咎焉，廢之當如是，而求其狂必恒雨，僭必恒暘，豫必恒燠，急必恒寒，蒙必恒風，則舛矣。聖人立教，論其理，而奚必于類應之符邪？
惟其言理，故不祖于數。而宋世蔡元定作《皇極內篇》，補洪範不傳之數，以疇之目合書之九，九衍之而為八十一，八十一衍之而為七百
translation_en:
…and there are branches. The first four categories constitute the substance of the August Norm, the roots of governing all under Heaven; the last four constitute its application, the branches and leaves of governing all under Heaven.
Readers of the Great Plan must understand the ultimate principle that Heaven and humanity form a unity. The sage took seriously the workings of stimulus and response, setting out in detail how the cultivation or neglect of the Five Activities corresponds to signs manifested in the Five Phases. Yet this principle is subtle and cannot be confined to observable traces. Liu Xiang composed the Commentary on the Five Phases of the Great Plan. His claims that a particular action causes a particular disaster, and that a particular disaster responds to a particular action, make the correspondence as immediate as that between a body and its shadow, fragmenting the subject through analysis. People criticize this as the study of disasters and anomalies, and consequently suspect that the category concerning mindful use may not be entirely trustworthy. Now, a ruler serves Heaven as a filial son serves his parents, daily observing their expressions of pleasure and anger as indications of his own disobedience or obedience. This is what is meant by mindfulness. When the signs are favorable, one's cultivation should indeed accord with this teaching. But to require that reverence invariably bring timely rain, good order timely sunshine, wisdom timely warmth, deliberation timely cold, and sagacity timely wind is difficult to sustain. When the signs are adverse, one's neglect should indeed be understood in these terms. But to require that unruliness invariably bring incessant rain, overstepping incessant sunshine, indolence incessant warmth, impatience incessant cold, and ignorance incessant wind is mistaken. In establishing his teaching, the sage discusses the principle: why must one insist on tokens of correspondence by category?
Precisely because it speaks of principle, it does not take numbers as its foundation. Yet Cai Yuanding of the Song composed the Inner Chapters on the August Norm to supply the numerical system of the Great Plan that had not been transmitted. He matched the headings of its categories to the nine numbers of the Luo Writing, expanded nine into eighty-one, and expanded eighty-one into seven hundred…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
二十九極之於六千五百六十一焉自元
至終猶易之卦也而六千五百六十一猶
卦之爻也其于天人妙理治世大法果皆
曲盡而無遺否乎洛書數之祖祖洛書而
推之于不可窮此元定之精于數學而有
功于書也若謂洪範之缺藉以推衍何其
敢于誣經也哉是故六經之道幾絶而復
明者諸儒傳經之力而使大義不盡明于
世者諸儒牽合擬附之罪也漢儒之失在
===
示天下後世之信而涉於誇宋儒之失在
求聖人之精而流於過或曰宋儒之學何
可非也曰何敢非也天下理與數而已矣
若惟其理數是精而不援經解附則邵子
之圖學蔡氏之數學豈可少哉此言蓋為
聖經立辨也折衷之以定論尚俟夫理學
之奧者焉
第四問
鍾士弘
punctuated:
二十九，極之於六千五百六十一焉。自元至終，猶易之卦也；而六千五百六十一，猶卦之爻也。其于天人妙理、治世大法，果皆曲盡而無遺否乎？洛書，數之祖；祖洛書而推之于不可窮，此元定之精于數學而有功于書也。若謂洪範之缺藉以推衍，何其敢于誣經也哉！是故六經之道幾絶而復明者，諸儒傳經之力；而使大義不盡明于世者，諸儒牽合擬附之罪也。漢儒之失，在示天下後世之信而涉於誇；宋儒之失，在求聖人之精而流於過。或曰：「宋儒之學何可非也？」曰：「何敢非也？天下理與數而已矣。若惟其理數是精，而不援經解附，則邵子之圖學、蔡氏之數學，豈可少哉？」此言蓋為聖經立辨也。折衷之以定論，尚俟夫理學之奧者焉。

第四問

鍾士弘
translation_en:
…[seven hundred and] twenty-nine, extending it ultimately to six thousand five hundred and sixty-one. From beginning to end, these are analogous to the hexagrams of the Book of Changes, while the six thousand five hundred and sixty-one are analogous to the lines of the hexagrams. But do they truly exhaust every subtle principle governing Heaven and humanity and every great rule for governing the world, leaving nothing out? The Luo Writing is the source of numbers. To take the Luo Writing as the foundation and extrapolate from it without limit demonstrates Yuanding’s mastery of numerical learning and his contribution to the Book of Documents. But to claim that this supplies what is missing from the “Great Plan” through numerical extrapolation—how could one dare so to misrepresent the Classic!

Thus, that the Way of the Six Classics, nearly severed, became clear once more is owing to the scholars’ work in transmitting the Classics; that their great meaning has not become fully clear to the world is owing to those scholars’ forced associations and contrived correspondences. The failing of Han scholars lay in seeking to establish credibility before the world and later generations, yet lapsing into exaggeration; the failing of Song scholars lay in seeking the sages’ most refined insights, yet going to excess. Someone asks: “How can the learning of the Song scholars be faulted?” I reply: “How would I dare to fault it? All that is under Heaven consists simply of principles and numbers. If they confined themselves to mastering those principles and numbers, without invoking the Classics to attach their interpretations to them, how could Master Shao’s study of diagrams or Master Cai’s numerical learning be dispensed with?” These remarks are intended to clarify distinctions in defense of the sages’ Classics. To weigh these matters and reach a definitive judgment, we must still await someone profoundly versed in the learning of principle.

Fourth Question

Zhong Shihong

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭沈批諸作談吏治類襲陳言
獨條悉問目不泛不拘佳士也
同考試官敎諭唐批語意脫套
考試官學正吳批力追古作
考試官敎授顧批剖析有識
君之設官分職凡以為民也自省之藩臬
而下裂其土而為之郡郡有守自郡而下
裂其土而為之邑邑有令以其土授之於
民而寄其治於郡邑之守令蓋守令於民
===
最近而其政最親守惟其人則郡之政朝
而出夕而民賴之非若人者其政為無實
也令惟其人則邑之政朝而出夕而民賴
之非若人者其政為無實也以是收錄之
道慎於擇人考核之道慎於採實慎於擇
人故試一功課一最必其利於民者也其
不在是雖善不錄矣慎於採實故建一事
剔一弊亦必其利於民者也其不在是雖
可以近名不為矣如此則守令皆其人守
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭沈批：諸作談吏治，類襲陳言，獨條悉問目，不泛不拘，佳士也。
同考試官敎諭唐批：語意脫套。
考試官學正吳批：力追古作。
考試官敎授顧批：剖析有識。
君之設官分職，凡以為民也。自省之藩臬而下，裂其土而為之郡，郡有守；自郡而下，裂其土而為之邑，邑有令。以其土授之於民，而寄其治於郡邑之守令。蓋守令於民最近，而其政最親。守惟其人，則郡之政朝而出，夕而民賴之；非若人者，其政為無實也。令惟其人，則邑之政朝而出，夕而民賴之；非若人者，其政為無實也。以是收錄之道，慎於擇人；考核之道，慎於採實。慎於擇人，故試一功，課一最，必其利於民者也。其不在是，雖善不錄矣。慎於採實，故建一事，剔一弊，亦必其利於民者也。其不在是，雖可以近名不為矣。如此，則守令皆其人，守
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: Most of the essays discussing local administration repeat stale formulations. This one alone addresses the points of the question fully and in order, neither rambling nor constrained. A fine scholar.
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: Both expression and meaning break free of conventional formulas.
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: Strives vigorously to emulate ancient compositions.
Comment by Examiner Gu, Professor: The analysis shows discernment.
The ruler establishes offices and assigns duties entirely for the people's sake. Below the provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, territory is divided into prefectures, each with a prefect; below the prefectures, territory is divided into counties, each with a magistrate. The land is allotted to the people, while responsibility for governing them is entrusted to the prefects and county magistrates. These officials are closest to the people, and their administration touches them most directly. If the prefect is the right man, a prefectural measure issued in the morning benefits the people by evening. If he is not such a man, his administration has no substance. If the magistrate is the right man, a county measure issued in the morning benefits the people by evening. If he is not such a man, his administration has no substance.
Thus, in recruitment and appointment, care must be taken to select the right men; in evaluating performance, care must be taken to ascertain actual results. Care in selecting men means that whenever an achievement is examined or a superior performance assessed, it must have benefited the people. If it does not meet this criterion, however good it may otherwise be, it receives no credit. Care in ascertaining actual results means that whenever an undertaking is initiated or an abuse eliminated, it too must benefit the people. If it does not meet this criterion, even if it might bring renown, it is not pursued. In this way, the prefects and magistrates will all be the right men, and the prefects …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
令之政皆其實政豈惟貽斯民以休哉
朝廷之惠澤流上大夫之績用章而天下登
諸理矣執事策士以吏治下詢舉古昔之
媺異者相與折衷焉豈以愚生將膺民社
之司而啓其尚友之志乎謹摭拾所聞以
對粤循之與良昉於誰乎傳曰守法治民
無所更改者曰循能以教化移民易俗者
曰良是固均謂之吏也愚於春秋而下得
數人焉治東阿而改道易行豈固爲是之
===
阿狥與蓋囑託不行貨賂不至晏子之盟
於心者舊矣吾行之而君不之信不可以
遽然君言之而吾不之省不可以徒然故
先容於左右借譽於豪家卒使片言之間
景公悔悟舉東阿而專寄焉則知嬰之改
易乃所以善守其故也治蜀郡而化行俗
美豈固爲是之矯激與蓋風俗辟陋俗尚
變夷文翁欲誘而進之久矣但無故而驟
見者其情駭有因而嘿奪者其勢便故□
punctuated:
令之政皆其實政，豈惟貽斯民以休哉？朝廷之惠澤流，上大夫之績用章，而天下登諸理矣。執事策士，以吏治下詢，舉古昔之媺異者，相與折衷焉。豈以愚生將膺民社之司，而啓其尚友之志乎？謹摭拾所聞以對。
粤循之與良，昉於誰乎？傳曰：「守法治民，無所更改者曰循；能以教化移民易俗者曰良。」是固均謂之吏也。愚於春秋而下得數人焉。治東阿而改道易行，豈固爲是之阿狥與？蓋囑託不行，貨賂不至，晏子之盟於心者舊矣。吾行之而君不之信，不可以遽然；君言之而吾不之省，不可以徒然。故先容於左右，借譽於豪家，卒使片言之間，景公悔悟，舉東阿而專寄焉。則知嬰之改易，乃所以善守其故也。
治蜀郡而化行俗美，豈固爲是之矯激與？蓋風俗辟陋，俗尚變夷，文翁欲誘而進之久矣。但無故而驟見者，其情駭；有因而嘿奪者，其勢便。故□
translation_en:
…the magistrates’ administration would all be administration of genuine substance. Would this merely bring well-being to the people? The court’s beneficence would spread, the achievements of its senior grand masters would become manifest, and all under Heaven would attain good order. You, sir, in examining candidates through policy questions, have condescended to inquire about local administration, citing outstanding examples from antiquity for joint consideration and judgment. Is this because this humble student will one day assume responsibility for a community and its altars, and you wish to awaken his aspiration to take the ancients as his friends? I respectfully gather what I have heard in reply.
Now, with whom did the categories of “law-abiding” and “good” officials originate? A transmitted account says: “Those who uphold the laws and govern the people without making alterations are called law-abiding; those who can transform the people and change their customs through moral instruction are called good.” Both, of course, are descriptions of officials. From the Spring and Autumn period onward, I find several such men. When the administrator of Dong’e changed his methods and conduct, was this really an act of flattery and favoritism? Yan Zi had long pledged in his heart that private solicitations should have no effect and bribes should find no entry. “If I put this into practice and my lord does not trust it, I cannot act precipitately; if my lord speaks and I do not reflect upon his words, I cannot simply let the matter rest.” Thus he first secured favorable introductions through the ruler’s attendants and borrowed the praise of powerful families. In the end, with only a few words, he brought Duke Jing to remorse and understanding, so that the duke entrusted Dong’e entirely to him. We may thus understand that Yan Ying’s changes were precisely his means of faithfully preserving his original principles.
When the administrator of Shu Commandery spread moral instruction and improved its customs, was this really an act of excessive zeal? Its customs were uncultivated and crude, and its customary preferences had become those of the Yi peoples [?]. Wen Weng had long wished to guide its people toward improvement. Yet something that appears suddenly without a reason alarms people’s feelings, whereas quietly displacing established habits by working through existing circumstances is readily accomplished. Therefore, [illegible]…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
羣吏於博士修學宮於成都至於經年之
間蜀人感化比齊魯而崇文雅則知文翁
之變俗乃所以善法其故也遷南陽而出
入阡陌者非召信臣其人乎彼其爲民興
利務在殷富故視水泉通溝瀆以廣灌漑
利之歲增者每至三萬頃焉況均水有約
嫁娶送終奢靡有禁此盜賊訟獄日爲之
清而民之稱召父者不衰也遷北海而反
歸桐鄕者非朱邑乎彼其爲桐鄕嗇夫廉
===
正不苟故問耆老恤孤寡減笞辱所部吏
民咸愛敬焉況居處有節遇九族鄕黨有
恩此北海司農治行第一而民之奉烝嘗
者不絕也合而觀之晏嬰齊之選也文翁
召信臣朱邑西漢之選也古今稱循良者
常互言之以是知循則未嘗不良良則未
嘗不循如數子者各指其事而已異同非
所計也廉之與能昉於誰乎傳曰勤政愛
民奉公潔己者曰廉剸繁治劇禁暴安民
punctuated:
羣吏於博士，修學宮於成都。至於經年之間，蜀人感化，比齊魯而崇文雅，則知文翁之變俗，乃所以善法其故也。遷南陽而出入阡陌者，非召信臣其人乎？彼其爲民興利，務在殷富，故視水泉，通溝瀆，以廣灌漑，利之歲增者，每至三萬頃焉。況均水有約，嫁娶送終奢靡有禁，此盜賊訟獄日爲之清，而民之稱召父者不衰也。遷北海而反歸桐鄕者，非朱邑乎？彼其爲桐鄕嗇夫，廉正不苟，故問耆老，恤孤寡，減笞辱，所部吏民咸愛敬焉。況居處有節，遇九族鄕黨有恩，此北海司農治行第一，而民之奉烝嘗者不絕也。合而觀之，晏嬰，齊之選也；文翁、召信臣、朱邑，西漢之選也。古今稱循良者，常互言之。以是知循則未嘗不良，良則未嘗不循，如數子者，各指其事而已，異同非所計也。

廉之與能，昉於誰乎？傳曰：「勤政愛民，奉公潔己者曰廉；剸繁治劇，禁暴安民
translation_en:
…the assembled officials under the Erudites, and built a school in Chengdu. Within a year, the people of Shu were transformed by his influence, matching those of Qi and Lu in their esteem for literary refinement. Thus we know that Wen Weng’s transformation of local customs was how he skillfully took established practices as his model. Was it not Shao Xinchen who, transferred to Nanyang, went out among the fields? In promoting benefits for the people, he aimed to bring them prosperity. He therefore inspected water sources and opened channels and ditches to extend irrigation; the additional land benefiting each year often amounted to thirty thousand qing. Moreover, he established agreements for equitable water distribution and prohibited extravagance in weddings and funerals. Consequently, robbery and litigation diminished daily, and the people never ceased calling him “Father Shao.”

Was it not Zhu Yi who, transferred to Beihai, returned in the end to Tongxiang? As bailiff of Tongxiang, he was incorruptible, upright, and conscientious. He consulted the elders, cared for orphans and widows, and reduced flogging and humiliation. The officials and people under his authority all loved and respected him. Moreover, he lived with restraint and treated his extended kin and fellow townspeople generously. Thus, in Beihai and as Chamberlain for the National Treasury, his administrative achievements ranked first, and the people continued without interruption to offer seasonal sacrifices to him.

Considered together, Yan Ying was an outstanding man of Qi; Wen Weng, Shao Xinchen, and Zhu Yi were outstanding men of the Western Han. From antiquity to the present, those praising officials as rule-abiding and good have regularly used these terms interchangeably. From this we know that the rule-abiding are invariably good, and the good invariably rule-abiding. In the case of these men, each designation merely points to particular deeds; similarities and differences are not what matters.

With whom did the distinction between incorruptibility and competence originate? The transmitted text says: “Those who attend diligently to government, love the people, serve the public, and keep themselves unsullied are called incorruptible; those who handle complex affairs, administer difficult matters, restrain violence, and bring peace to the people…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者曰能是固均謂之吏也愚於春秋而下
得數人焉劉寵之守會稽德在生民者甚
鉅也山陰之百錢惡足以爲報耶乃却而
不受非沽名也君子曰此足以見寵也舉
一事而寵之平生宛然一介不取之遺也
不然伯榮之除煩苛見信於父老乆矣顧
假是以愚之乎王遜之守上洛其持已者
甚嚴也私畜之駒犢豈足以爲汙耶乃還
而不有非要譽也君子曰此足以見遜也
===
舉一事而遜之平生宛然千駟弗視之遺
也不然邵伯之舉孝廉見信於當時乆矣
顧藉是以媚之乎投巫漳水則鄴郡震驚
此西門豹之所以爲智也蓋河伯娶婦之
說幻妄甚矣吾爲之令而與之明其誣焉
則投之非忍也前此之無罪而溺者非此
莫償也後此之無罪而溺者非此莫禁也
自是吏民震驚而不復有言豹之造福於
鄴者多矣曾何愛於一巫耶捕吏美陽則
punctuated:
者曰能。是固均謂之吏也。愚於春秋而下，得數人焉。劉寵之守會稽，德在生民者甚鉅也。山陰之百錢，惡足以爲報耶？乃却而不受，非沽名也。君子曰：「此足以見寵也。」舉一事而寵之平生宛然，一介不取之遺也。不然，伯榮之除煩苛，見信於父老乆矣，顧假是以愚之乎？王遜之守上洛，其持已者甚嚴也。私畜之駒犢，豈足以爲汙耶？乃還而不有，非要譽也。君子曰：「此足以見遜也。」舉一事而遜之平生宛然，千駟弗視之遺也。不然，邵伯之舉孝廉，見信於當時乆矣，顧藉是以媚之乎？

投巫漳水，則鄴郡震驚，此西門豹之所以爲智也。蓋河伯娶婦之說，幻妄甚矣。吾爲之令，而與之明其誣焉，則投之非忍也。前此之無罪而溺者，非此莫償也；後此之無罪而溺者，非此莫禁也。自是吏民震驚，而不復有言。豹之造福於鄴者多矣，曾何愛於一巫耶？捕吏美陽，則
translation_en:
…are called capable. These are, of course, all termed officials. From the Spring and Autumn period onward, I find several men who exemplify these qualities. When Liu Chong served as governor of Kuaiji, the benefits he bestowed upon the people were immense. How could the hundred coins offered at Shanyin adequately repay him? Yet he declined them and would not accept them; he was not fishing for fame. The gentleman says, “This suffices to reveal Chong’s character.” This single incident vividly reveals his entire life: he carried on the tradition of accepting not even the smallest thing improperly. Otherwise, Borong’s [?] abolition of vexatious and harsh measures had long since won the trust of the local elders; would he have used this gesture to fool them? When Wang Xun served as governor of Shangluo, he maintained extremely strict standards of personal conduct. How could privately raised foals and calves have been enough to stain his integrity? Yet he returned them and did not keep them; he was not seeking praise. The gentleman says, “This suffices to reveal Xun’s character.” This single incident vividly reveals his entire life: he carried on the tradition of not even casting a glance at a thousand teams of four horses. Otherwise, Shaobo’s recommendation as Filial and Incorrupt had long since won him the trust of his contemporaries; would he have used this gesture to curry their favor?

When the spirit-medium was thrown into the Zhang River, the commandery of Ye was struck with terror. This shows why Ximen Bao was considered wise. The story that the River Earl took a wife was utterly fantastical and false. As magistrate there, he would make its falsity clear to the people; thus, throwing the medium into the river was no act of cruelty. Without this, there could be no recompense for the innocent people previously drowned; without this, the future drowning of innocent people could not be stopped. From then on, officials and commoners were terrified, and no one spoke of the practice again. Bao brought many blessings to Ye. Why, then, should he have spared a single spirit-medium? When an official was arrested at Meiyang, then…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
吏民懾服此王遵之所以爲斷也蓋不孝
之律聖人所不忍言者吾爲之令而與之
明其法焉則誅之非忍也法不可以寛縱
不必泥於古法也情不可以姑息正以合
於人情也自是吏民驚駭而不敢爲惡遵
之感悟於美陽者深矣曾何愛一不孝耶
合而觀之西門豹魏之選也劉寵王遜王
遵漢與晉之選也古今稱廉能者常對言
之以是知廉者未必能能者未必廉如數
===
子者各舉所長而已優劣非所計也夫數
子所值皆非全盛之世而吏治之彬彬昭
於史冊者尚如此廼
國朝之人才容有不逮於數子者何哉將謂
收錄之未廣與然銓衡掄選之外復有明
揚彙薦之條不可謂不廣矣執事且云擇
官不擇人朋比者競奔走焉兹欲搜羅真
才野罔攸伏何道以致之說者曰鄉舉里
選之法可行也吁官浮於人以其僞也籍
punctuated:
吏民懾服，此王遵之所以爲斷也。蓋不孝之律，聖人所不忍言者。吾爲之令，而與之明其法焉，則誅之非忍也。法不可以寛縱，不必泥於古法也；情不可以姑息，正以合於人情也。自是吏民驚駭而不敢爲惡，遵之感悟於美陽者深矣，曾何愛一不孝耶？合而觀之，西門豹，魏之選也；劉寵、王遜、王遵，漢與晉之選也。古今稱廉能者，常對言之，以是知廉者未必能，能者未必廉。如數子者，各舉所長而已，優劣非所計也。
夫數子所值，皆非全盛之世，而吏治之彬彬昭於史冊者尚如此。廼國朝之人才，容有不逮於數子者，何哉？將謂收錄之未廣與？然銓衡掄選之外，復有明揚彙薦之條，不可謂不廣矣。執事且云：「擇官不擇人，朋比者競奔走焉。」兹欲搜羅真才，野罔攸伏，何道以致之？說者曰：「鄉舉里選之法可行也。」吁！官浮於人，以其僞也。籍
translation_en:
…the officials and common people were awed into submission: this is what demonstrated Wang Zun’s decisiveness. The law against unfilial conduct concerns something that the sages could scarcely bear to speak of. Yet when, as magistrate, one makes that law clear to the people, executing an offender is no act of cruelty. The law permits no indulgent laxity; one need not cling rigidly to ancient laws. Human feelings admit no misplaced leniency; this is precisely how one accords with human sentiment. Thereafter, the officials and common people were alarmed and dared not do evil. Profound indeed was the moral awakening Wang Zun brought about in Meiyang! Why, then, spare a single unfilial man? Taken together, Ximen Bao was an outstanding man of Wei, while Liu Chong, Wang Xun, and Wang Zun were outstanding men of the Han and Jin. From antiquity to the present, integrity and ability have regularly been paired in praise of officials. From this we know that a man of integrity is not necessarily capable, and a capable man is not necessarily upright. With men such as these, each is cited simply for his particular strengths; their relative superiority or inferiority is not at issue.
None of these men lived in an age of perfect flourishing, yet the excellence of their administration shines forth in the historical records to this degree. How, then, can there be talented men of our own dynasty who fall short of them? Shall we say that recruitment has not been sufficiently broad? Yet beyond the regular assessment and selection of officials, there are also provisions for publicly recognizing worthy men and recommending them collectively. Recruitment can hardly be called narrow. You, sir, further say: “They choose offices rather than men, and those who form self-serving cliques compete in running about to secure advancement.” If we now wish to seek out true talent so that none remains hidden outside official service, by what means can this be achieved? Some say: “The system of nomination by townships and selection by villages could be put into practice.” Alas! Official positions exceed the worth of those who occupy them because of their falsity. Supposing [?] …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
使鄉舉里選行而偽愈滋求之一人而不
當亦旣鑿矣由是而十人如之百人復如
之則開蹊徑以多倖進之途者不猶甚於
競奔走者哉是可見收錄之道不必外其
所謂擇人者慎其所擇而已矣不然積薪
臥治如汲黯催科政拙如陽城寧無遺憾
乎將謂考核之未精與然三載大計之外
復有不時黜陟之典不可謂不精矣執事
且云採名不採實智巧者爭速化焉茲欲
===
考憑政績朝無倖位何術以致之說者曰
久任超遷之法可行也吁名浮於實以其
偽也藉使久任超遷行而偽愈滋求之三
年而不效亦旣鑿矣由是而六年如之九
年復如之則遲歲月以取終南之捷者不
猶甚於爭速化者哉是可見考核之道不
必外其所謂採實者慎其所採而已矣不
然損名郡治如黃霸擅誅掾吏如張敞寧
無過舉乎嗚呼擇之採之其道不易言也
punctuated: 使鄉舉里選行而偽愈滋，求之一人而不當，亦旣鑿矣。由是而十人如之，百人復如之，則開蹊徑以多倖進之途者，不猶甚於競奔走者哉？是可見收錄之道，不必外其所謂擇人者，慎其所擇而已矣。不然，積薪臥治如汲黯，催科政拙如陽城，寧無遺憾乎？將謂考核之未精與？然三載大計之外，復有不時黜陟之典，不可謂不精矣。執事且云：「採名不採實，智巧者爭速化焉。」茲欲考憑政績，朝無倖位，何術以致之？說者曰：「久任超遷之法可行也。」吁！名浮於實，以其偽也。藉使久任超遷行而偽愈滋，求之三年而不效，亦旣鑿矣。由是而六年如之，九年復如之，則遲歲月以取終南之捷者，不猶甚於爭速化者哉？是可見考核之道，不必外其所謂採實者，慎其所採而已矣。不然，損名郡治如黃霸，擅誅掾吏如張敞，寧無過舉乎？嗚呼！擇之採之，其道不易言也。
translation_en:
…supposing recommendations by townships and selection by villages were implemented, yet fraud proliferated still further: if even one person sought out proved unsuitable, the method would already be misguided. If the same then happened with ten people, and again with a hundred, would opening such byways and multiplying routes to advancement through undeserved favor not be still worse than the competitive pursuit of office? This shows that the method of recruitment need not go beyond what you call “selecting people”: one need only exercise care over whom one selects. Otherwise, would there not be cause for regret over men like Ji An, who complained that promotion resembled piling up firewood, with later arrivals placed on top, yet could govern even while lying ill, or Yang Cheng, whose administration was deemed inept at collecting taxes?

Would you then say that official evaluations are insufficiently rigorous? Yet besides the triennial Grand Review, there are also provisions for demotion and promotion at irregular intervals; evaluation cannot be called insufficiently rigorous. You further say: “Reputation is accepted instead of actual achievement, and the clever and crafty compete for rapid advancement.” Now, if we wish evaluations to rest on administrative achievements, so that no one at court holds office through undeserved favor, by what means can this be accomplished? Some say: “The method of long tenure and exceptional promotion can be implemented.” Alas! Reputation exceeds actual achievement because of fraud. Suppose long tenure and exceptional promotion were implemented, yet fraud proliferated still further: if three years of seeking results produced none, the method would already be misguided. If the same then happened over six years, and again over nine, would prolonging the years only to gain the ‘Zhongnan shortcut’—a roundabout route to office—not be still worse than competing for rapid advancement? This shows that the method of evaluation need not go beyond what you call “accepting actual achievement”: one need only exercise care over what one accepts. Otherwise, would there not be mistaken decisions concerning men like Huang Ba, whose reputation declined from that earned in governing a commandery, or Zhang Chang, who executed a subordinate official without authorization? Alas! Selecting men and assessing their achievements—the proper way to do these things is not easily explained.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
媕婀辨給者名之曰聰慧詷伺獧媮者名
之曰才幹悃愊無華者名之曰遲鈍質直
不回者名之曰骩骳奈之何吏之不趨於
偽也然則竟無策乎其一曰重簡任漢制
刺史二千石下及郎官咸重厥選惟其稱
而已近或以地方之衝僻為趨避以吏事
之繁簡為欣戚無惑乎委頓而莫克自振
也我
國朝之建官實維銓衡其衝僻繁簡揀其才
===
而均停之用是不及者知懼而能者爭自
淬濯各供其職而無負乘之誚焉何也才
之有及有不及猶力之有勇怯也勇者藐
百鎰而輕焉一有所舉輒無難色其勇怯
半者雖賞而誘之强舉之不勝也其怯者
雖罰而治之强舉之不勝也然則擇人之
道豈必於他求哉量力而使則勇者非絕
力因人而授則怯者非棄人如斯而已矣
二曰準功過我
punctuated:
媕婀辨給者，名之曰聰慧；詷伺獧媮者，名之曰才幹；悃愊無華者，名之曰遲鈍；質直不回者，名之曰骩骳。奈之何吏之不趨於偽也？然則竟無策乎？
其一曰重簡任。漢制，刺史、二千石，下及郎官，咸重厥選，惟其稱而已。近或以地方之衝僻為趨避，以吏事之繁簡為欣戚，無惑乎委頓而莫克自振也。我國朝之建官，實維銓衡，其衝僻繁簡，揀其才而均停之。用是不及者知懼，而能者爭自淬濯，各供其職，而無負乘之誚焉。何也？才之有及有不及，猶力之有勇怯也。勇者藐百鎰而輕焉，一有所舉，輒無難色。其勇怯半者，雖賞而誘之，强舉之，不勝也；其怯者，雖罰而治之，强舉之，不勝也。然則擇人之道，豈必於他求哉？量力而使，則勇者非絕力；因人而授，則怯者非棄人。如斯而已矣。
二曰準功過。我
translation_en:
Those who temporize and speak glibly are called intelligent; those who pry and spy, who are cunning and unscrupulous, are called capable. Those who are sincere and unadorned are called slow-witted; those who are upright and unbending are called servile [?]. How, then, can officials help tending toward deceit? Is there, after all, no remedy?
The first is to attach importance to selection and appointment. Under the Han system, great care was taken in selecting Regional Inspectors, officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank, and down to the Gentlemen: all that mattered was their fitness for office. Recently, some have sought or avoided posts according to whether their locations were strategic centers or remote places, and have felt pleased or distressed according to whether official business was light or burdensome. It is no wonder that they become dispirited and cannot rouse themselves. In establishing offices, our dynasty relies fundamentally on personnel selection. Whether a locality is central or remote, and its business heavy or light, men should be selected for their abilities and assigned in due proportion. In this way, those whose abilities fall short become apprehensive, while the capable compete to refine themselves. Each fulfills his duties, escaping the reproach of a burden-bearer riding in a carriage—that is, occupying a position beyond his station. Why is this? That some have sufficient ability and others do not is like the difference between the strong and the weak in physical strength. A strong man regards a hundred yi in weight as trifling and light; whenever he lifts something, he shows no sign of difficulty. Someone midway between strong and weak cannot manage the weight when compelled to lift it, even if enticed with rewards. A weak man cannot manage it when compelled to lift it, even if subjected to punishment. Why, then, must the method of selecting men be sought elsewhere? Employ them according to their strength, and the strong will not exhaust their powers; assign offices according to the individual, and the weak will not be discarded. That is all.
The second is to assess achievements and faults. Our …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國朝初制內外咸有通考第其功過以相乗
除如以一歲爲準某也善某也未善量其
輕重而爲之差以一人爲準某政善某政
未善量其多寡而爲之差用是賢者愈奮
而不肖者無所逃歲月日時皆有可稽而
莫得以掩其瑕焉何也名實之易淆由於
疑似之弗辨也譬諸人有得燕石者藏以
爲玉或告之曰此燕石也則棄之有聞鬻
朴者慕以爲璞或告之曰此朴也則巳之
===
===
然則採實之道豈必於他求哉良工之目
不可欺以燕石良賈之耳不可亂以朴如
斯而已矣雖然吏治日僞則議法日詳勢
也不已尚有說焉曰嚴舉刺則勸懲無所
惑懲貪墨則苞苴無所入去鷹鸇則羅織
無所施拔卓異則資格無所限抑僥倖則
操切無所容兼是數者則吏治脩矣吏治
脩而民生遂民生遂而理道隆晏子諸人
之儔當爲之北面而齊東兩漢之治又惡
punctuated:
國朝初制，內外咸有通考，第其功過，以相乗除。如以一歲爲準，某也善，某也未善，量其輕重而爲之差；以一人爲準，某政善，某政未善，量其多寡而爲之差。用是賢者愈奮，而不肖者無所逃，歲月日時皆有可稽，而莫得以掩其瑕焉。何也？名實之易淆，由於疑似之弗辨也。譬諸人有得燕石者，藏以爲玉，或告之曰：「此燕石也。」則棄之。有聞鬻朴者，慕以爲璞，或告之曰：「此朴也。」則巳之。然則採實之道，豈必於他求哉？良工之目，不可欺以燕石；良賈之耳，不可亂以朴。如斯而已矣。
雖然，吏治日僞，則議法日詳，勢也。不已，尚有說焉。曰：嚴舉刺，則勸懲無所惑；懲貪墨，則苞苴無所入；去鷹鸇，則羅織無所施；拔卓異，則資格無所限；抑僥倖，則操切無所容。兼是數者，則吏治脩矣。吏治脩而民生遂，民生遂而理道隆。晏子諸人之儔，當爲之北面，而齊東兩漢之治，又惡
translation_en:
…At the founding of our dynasty, regulations provided for comprehensive evaluations of officials both at court and in the provinces, grading their merits and faults and weighing these against one another. Taking a single year as the basis, one would judge that this person had performed well and that person poorly, weighing the relative importance of their deeds to distinguish their grades. Taking a single person as the basis, one would judge that this administrative measure was good and that one poor, weighing their relative numbers to distinguish the grades. In this way, the worthy would strive still harder, while the unworthy would have nowhere to escape scrutiny. There would be records to consult for every year, month, day, and hour, and none could conceal their flaws. Why is this? Reputation and reality are easily confused because deceptive appearances are not clearly distinguished. Consider someone who acquires a stone from Yan and treasures it as jade. If someone tells him, “This is a stone from Yan,” he discards it. Or someone hears of unworked wood being sold and covets it, thinking it uncut jade. If someone tells him, “This is wood,” he gives up the pursuit. Must the means of ascertaining the facts, then, be sought elsewhere? The eyes of a skilled craftsman cannot be deceived by a stone from Yan; the ears of an expert merchant cannot be confused by talk of unworked wood. That is all there is to it.
Nevertheless, as official administration grows ever more dishonest, proposals for regulations grow ever more detailed: this is the natural tendency. If we are to pursue the matter further, there is still something to be said. Make recommendations and denunciations rigorous, and there will be no confusion in encouragement and punishment. Punish corrupt officials, and bribes will find no way in. Remove the hawks and falcons—the predatory officials—and there will be no opportunity to fabricate charges. Promote those of outstanding ability, and formal qualifications and seniority will impose no limits. Restrain those who seek advancement through undeserved good fortune, and harsh, overbearing conduct will find no place. Apply all these measures together, and official administration will be put in order. Once official administration is in order, the people's livelihoods will flourish; once their livelihoods flourish, good government will prosper. Even the likes of Yanzi and the other worthies would have to face north before such administrators as their pupils, and how could the government of Qi and of the Eastern and Western Han [?]…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
足以佐下風哉若夫轉移風動之機則本
原之地又在乎
朝廷而已愚生何與知焉
第五問
裴應坤
同考試官教諭潘批江藩利弊區畫無遺殆留
心時務者
考試官學正吳批四事根究詳悉末歸重於
任人尤爲有見
===
考試官教授顧批條答詳明
法未甞無敝也識其敝而捄之者計貴遠
民未甞無患也恤其患而防之者慮貴周
何謂計遠思其始必惟其終利害悉究若
握筭以籌之務脩其法而已何謂慮周謀
于此不遺于彼遐隱畢達若持準以平之
務安其民而已故百年之弊不可以目前
祛而見止眉睫者舛也四方之患不可以
一手援而獨執拘攣者鑿也執事終策諸
punctuated:
足以佐下風哉？若夫轉移風動之機，則本原之地又在乎朝廷而已，愚生何與知焉？

第五問
裴應坤
同考試官教諭潘批：江藩利弊，區畫無遺，殆留心時務者。
考試官學正吳批：四事根究詳悉，末歸重於任人，尤爲有見。
考試官教授顧批：條答詳明。

法未甞無敝也，識其敝而捄之者，計貴遠；民未甞無患也，恤其患而防之者，慮貴周。何謂計遠？思其始，必惟其終，利害悉究，若握筭以籌之，務脩其法而已。何謂慮周？謀于此，不遺于彼，遐隱畢達，若持準以平之，務安其民而已。故百年之弊，不可以目前祛，而見止眉睫者舛也；四方之患，不可以一手援，而獨執拘攣者鑿也。執事終策諸
translation_en:
…be worthy even of a subordinate place? As for the means of bringing about transformation and moving people by example, their ultimate source lies solely with the imperial court. How could an ignorant student such as myself presume to understand them?

Fifth Policy Question
Pei Yingkun
Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “His treatment of the benefits and drawbacks affecting Jiangxi Province leaves nothing out of account. He is evidently someone who pays attention to current affairs.”
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “He investigates the four matters thoroughly and in detail, concluding by placing particular weight on the appointment of suitable men. This shows exceptional insight.”
Examiner Gu, Professor, comments: “His answers to the individual points are detailed and clear.”

Institutions have never been free of defects. For those who recognize and remedy their defects, planning must above all look far ahead. The people have never been free of troubles. For those who take their troubles to heart and guard against them, deliberation must above all be comprehensive. What does it mean to plan far ahead? When considering a beginning, one must also reflect upon its outcome, examining every benefit and harm as though calculating with counting rods, striving simply to put the institutions in good order. What does it mean to deliberate comprehensively? In planning for this, one must not overlook that; one must apprehend everything remote or hidden, as though holding a leveling instrument to make things even, striving simply to bring peace to the people.

Thus, abuses accumulated over a hundred years cannot be eliminated through measures confined to the immediate present: those whose vision extends no farther than their own eyebrows and eyelashes are mistaken. Troubles throughout the realm cannot be relieved by a single hand: those who cling exclusively to narrow constraints are rigid and impractical. You, gentlemen in charge, conclude by putting a policy question to the…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
士以江藩屯田水利備荒弭盜四事其爲
地方慮至深遠也今夫四事者自古經國
者所必講而惟今爲最急海內願治者所
胥望而惟江藩爲最要在昔有周井田之
制兵農合一居則爲比閭族黨出則爲伍
兩卒旅而又有遂人以掌溝洫之政有大
司徒以掌十二荒政有士師以掌八成載
在周禮纖悉備具故當其時民安物阜道
洽政治中外禔福至今猶可考見歷代因
===
之互有失得周道蓋寢微矣我
朝稽古定制體國經野至詳至備其於屯田
水利備荒弭盜尤加意焉是故臬臣督治
專官分攝事有責成法無偏墜視周制加
隆宜萬世蒙庇也何治乆敝滋有司奉宣
者靡力其在江藩如四事實有當議者焉
夫江西爲衞者三爲所者十一而屯軍分
隷歲計屯糧八萬六千有奇以充衞所之
軍實當大有裨於
punctuated:
士以江藩屯田、水利、備荒、弭盜四事，其爲地方慮至深遠也。今夫四事者，自古經國者所必講，而惟今爲最急；海內願治者所胥望，而惟江藩爲最要。在昔有周井田之制，兵農合一，居則爲比、閭、族、黨，出則爲伍、兩、卒、旅。而又有遂人以掌溝洫之政，有大司徒以掌十二荒政，有士師以掌八成，載在《周禮》，纖悉備具。故當其時，民安物阜，道洽政治，中外禔福，至今猶可考見。歷代因之，互有失得，周道蓋寢微矣。
我朝稽古定制，體國經野，至詳至備，其於屯田、水利、備荒、弭盜尤加意焉。是故臬臣督治，專官分攝，事有責成，法無偏墜，視周制加隆，宜萬世蒙庇也。何治乆敝滋，有司奉宣者靡力？其在江藩，如四事，實有當議者焉。
夫江西爲衞者三，爲所者十一，而屯軍分隷，歲計屯糧八萬六千有奇，以充衞所之軍實，當大有裨於
translation_en:
…the candidates concerning four matters in Jiangxi: military agricultural colonies, water management, famine preparedness, and the suppression of banditry. Your concern for the region is indeed profound and far-reaching. These four matters have required the attention of those governing the state since antiquity, but never have they been more urgent than now. They are what all under Heaven who desire good government look for, but nowhere are they more important than in Jiangxi. In former times, under the Zhou well-field system, soldiers and farmers were one: at home they were organized into neighborhood groups—bi, lü, zu, and dang—and when mobilized into military units—wu, liang, zu, and lü. There was also the Director of Outlying Districts, who administered drainage ditches and channels; the Minister of Education, who administered the twelve measures for famine relief; and the Judicial Officer, who administered the eight established precedents. These are recorded in the Rituals of Zhou, complete in every detail. Thus, in that age, the people were secure and goods abundant; the Way prevailed and government was well ordered; those within and beyond the central realm enjoyed peace and prosperity. Even today this can still be verified. Successive dynasties followed these institutions, with varying successes and failures, but the Way of Zhou gradually declined.
Our dynasty consulted antiquity in establishing its institutions, organizing the capital and laying out the countryside with the utmost thoroughness and completeness. It devoted particular attention to military agricultural colonies, water management, famine preparedness, and the suppression of banditry. Accordingly, surveillance officials supervise their administration, and specially appointed officials divide responsibility for them. Every undertaking has someone accountable for its accomplishment, and no part of the established system is neglected. These arrangements surpass even those of Zhou and should shelter countless generations. Why, then, as this order has endured, have abuses multiplied, while the responsible officials lack vigor in carrying it out? In Jiangxi, these four matters indeed present issues that require discussion.
Jiangxi has three guards and eleven battalions, among which the agricultural garrison troops are distributed. The annual grain assessment of the military colonies amounts to eighty-six thousand and more, supplying the military stores of the guards and battalions. This ought to contribute greatly to…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國計者乃今一軍以上悉仰給於縣官軍未
贍而民已告病矣嘗求其弊則因冊籍廢
久轉相欺隱漫不可詰曰絕伍湮沒也曰
猾卒盜沽也曰民田棼錯也曰磽瘠鮮獲
也又其甚者有田與衞所勢不聯絡如南
昌錯落於東流建德撫州分布於安仁餘
干地遠業曠久無根柢也兼之督率者役
什伍於私門收屯租於己橐致使按圖索
糧僅如捕影或者以軍民株連告訐橫出
===
輒委之不問焉非計之得也昔唐韓重華
為營田使東起振武西逾雲州墾田三千
八百餘里歲收粟二十萬石省度支錢二
千餘萬緡彼時沿邊之地皆藩鎮所專猶
行之得利若此况江省列在中土清理見
在之田安得倡陳恕不測之言范睢括牛
之說乎是故按開屯之籍則欺隱之端可
求也勘原田之界則侵占之跡可檢也田
有肥瘠則履畝之稅不可以不別也卒有
punctuated:
國計者，乃今一軍以上悉仰給於縣官，軍未贍而民已告病矣。嘗求其弊，則因冊籍廢久，轉相欺隱，漫不可詰：曰絕伍湮沒也，曰猾卒盜沽也，曰民田棼錯也，曰磽瘠鮮獲也。又其甚者，有田與衞所勢不聯絡，如南昌錯落於東流、建德，撫州分布於安仁、餘干，地遠業曠，久無根柢也。兼之督率者役什伍於私門，收屯租於己橐，致使按圖索糧，僅如捕影。或者以軍民株連，告訐橫出，輒委之不問焉，非計之得也。
昔唐韓重華為營田使，東起振武，西逾雲州，墾田三千八百餘里，歲收粟二十萬石，省度支錢二千餘萬緡。彼時沿邊之地皆藩鎮所專，猶行之得利若此，况江省列在中土，清理見在之田，安得倡陳恕不測之言、范睢括牛之說乎？是故按開屯之籍，則欺隱之端可求也；勘原田之界，則侵占之跡可檢也；田有肥瘠，則履畝之稅不可以不別也；卒有
translation_en:
…the state’s finances; yet now every soldier depends upon the government for support. Before the troops have been adequately provided for, the people are already complaining of hardship. In seeking the causes of these abuses, I have found that the registers have long fallen into disuse, allowing successive acts of deception and concealment that have become impossible to investigate. Some lands have disappeared from the records when their military households died out; some have been illicitly sold by crafty soldiers; some have become hopelessly intermingled with civilian fields; and some are barren and yield little. Worse still, some fields are geographically disconnected from their guards and battalions. Those of Nanchang, for example, are scattered through Dongliu and Jiande, while those of Fuzhou are distributed across Anren and Yugan. The land is distant and its cultivation neglected, and its tenure has long lacked a firm basis. Moreover, those supervising the troops employ squads of soldiers in their private households and pocket the rents from military agricultural colonies. Consequently, consulting maps to collect grain is scarcely different from trying to catch a shadow. Some officials, because investigations implicate soldiers and civilians alike and provoke accusations on every side, simply abandon the matter without inquiry. This is no sound policy.
Formerly, under the Tang, Han Chonghua served as Commissioner for Agricultural Colonies. From Zhenwu in the east to beyond Yunzhou in the west, he brought land into cultivation over more than 3,800 li, annually harvesting 200,000 shi of grain and saving the government more than twenty million strings of cash in fiscal expenditure. At that time, the frontier lands were all under the exclusive control of regional military governors, yet his measures still produced such benefits. How much more should be possible in Jiangxi, situated in the country’s interior, where the task is to put existing fields in order! How could one invoke Chen Shu’s warnings of unforeseen consequences [?] or Fan Sui’s argument about requisitioning oxen [?]? Thus, by consulting the registers compiled when the agricultural colonies were established, one can discover the sources of deception and concealment; by surveying the original boundaries of the fields, one can detect encroachments. Since fields differ in fertility, taxation assessed by acreage must distinguish between them; since among the soldiers there are…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
老弱則番休之制不可以不明也嚴清勾
之法則逃亡之數可補也申占役之律則
私役之弊可革也擇賢吏焉假之歲月不
事摶擊以需漸理不撓浮議以責成功如
是而屯政不脩未之有矣江西列郡爲州
者一爲縣者七十有二陂塘無慮數萬有
奇以興一方之水利宜大有益於民事者
乃今脩濬方新而旋復壅決所在控告者
月無虛牘而民事無補矣推原其故則以
===
溝洫久廢互相因循莫爲脩舉曰富強自
爲封殖也曰貧瘠苦於資計也曰勢分而
眾心易蝓也曰利鉅而當事易撼也又其
大者則江湍湖匯勢易毀嚙如平豐等處
一決輒數百丈彭蠡四際一漲率爲巨浸
膏腴汙萊人謀無措也且職水利者奉上
官之檄至促里胥以文應致使旱乾水溢
待命於天或者歸諸氣數適然委之無可
奈何焉非民之利也昔唐韋丹爲江西觀
punctuated:
老弱，則番休之制不可以不明也。嚴清勾之法，則逃亡之數可補也；申占役之律，則私役之弊可革也。擇賢吏焉，假之歲月，不事摶擊以需漸理，不撓浮議以責成功。如是而屯政不脩，未之有矣。
江西列郡，爲州者一，爲縣者七十有二，陂塘無慮數萬有奇。以興一方之水利，宜大有益於民事者。乃今脩濬方新，而旋復壅決，所在控告者月無虛牘，而民事無補矣。推原其故，則以溝洫久廢，互相因循，莫爲脩舉。曰富強自爲封殖也，曰貧瘠苦於資計也，曰勢分而眾心易蝓也，曰利鉅而當事易撼也。又其大者，則江湍湖匯，勢易毀嚙。如平豐等處，一決輒數百丈；彭蠡四際，一漲率爲巨浸。膏腴汙萊，人謀無措也。且職水利者，奉上官之檄至，促里胥以文應，致使旱乾水溢，待命於天。或者歸諸氣數適然，委之無可奈何焉，非民之利也。昔唐韋丹爲江西觀
translation_en:
…are old or weak, the system of rotational rest must be clearly defined. Strict enforcement of the procedures for checking military registers and calling up replacements can make good the numbers lost through desertion; renewed enforcement of the laws against appropriating soldiers’ labor can eliminate the abuses of private service. Select worthy officials and allow them sufficient time. Rather than resorting to harsh punitive action, await gradual improvement; remain unshaken by idle criticism and require successful results. With these measures, it has never been the case that military agricultural administration could not be put in order.
Among the jurisdictions of Jiangxi’s prefectures are one subprefecture and seventy-two counties, with ponds and reservoirs numbering well over several tens of thousands. Developing these local water resources ought greatly to benefit the people’s livelihoods. Yet nowadays, scarcely have repairs and dredging been completed when blockages and breaches recur. Every month brings written complaints from the affected places, while the people’s livelihoods receive no benefit. Tracing the causes, we find that the irrigation channels have long been neglected; everyone follows others in letting matters drift, and no one undertakes their restoration. Some say that the wealthy and powerful seek only to enlarge their own holdings; others, that poor and unproductive localities struggle to find the necessary resources; others, that divided authority makes people’s resolve readily falter [?]; and others, that the profits are so great that the officials responsible are easily swayed. Still greater difficulties arise from rushing rivers and converging lake waters, whose force readily destroys and erodes the banks. At places such as Pingfeng, a single breach often extends several hundred zhang; around Pengli Lake, a single rise in the water commonly produces a vast inundation. Fertile lands become waterlogged wasteland, and human ingenuity finds no remedy. Moreover, when directives arrive from their superiors, those responsible for water management merely press the village functionaries to respond with paperwork. Thus, whether drought parches the land or floodwaters overflow, people are left awaiting Heaven’s decree. Some attribute these events to the workings of cosmic fortune and resign themselves to helplessness. This does not serve the people’s interests. Formerly, in the Tang dynasty, Wei Dan served as Jiangxi’s Surveillance Commissioner…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
察築隄捍江為陂塘五百餘所漑田萬有
二千頃功德被於八州玆江右之地皆當
時故址彼旣築以利民若此况於數百載
之後求其故智安得藉口於杜亞先事之
無功而竝棄賈讓之下策乎是故在高原
宜鑿渠引水以資其利也在下濕宜築隄
開港以殺其勢也門閘不復矣脩舉壩堰
之策猶可行也民力宜恤矣三時務農之
後亦可勞也專利之禁必嚴而曲防者有
===
罪也議貸之令必申而惰事者無赦也擇
賢吏焉專其委任俾利建百年而勿惜一
時之費計安萬姓而勿恤一人之讙如是
而水利不興未之見矣以備荒言之司計
者目擊時艱嘗建積穀之議矣
奏下有司制非不嚴也今倉庾設矣會計詳
矣而質諸例限尚未及半者非宿弊未盡
刬也蓋取諸訟牒則忿訐赴愬多十室九
空之民取諸勸貸則荒歉相仍非粒米狼
punctuated:
察，築隄捍江，為陂塘五百餘所，漑田萬有二千頃，功德被於八州。玆江右之地，皆當時故址。彼旣築以利民若此，况於數百載之後，求其故智，安得藉口於杜亞先事之無功，而竝棄賈讓之下策乎？是故在高原，宜鑿渠引水以資其利也；在下濕，宜築隄開港以殺其勢也。門閘不復矣，脩舉壩堰之策猶可行也；民力宜恤矣，三時務農之後亦可勞也。專利之禁必嚴，而曲防者有罪也；議貸之令必申，而惰事者無赦也。擇賢吏焉，專其委任，俾利建百年，而勿惜一時之費；計安萬姓，而勿恤一人之讙。如是而水利不興，未之見矣。
以備荒言之，司計者目擊時艱，嘗建積穀之議矣。奏下有司，制非不嚴也。今倉庾設矣，會計詳矣，而質諸例限，尚未及半者，非宿弊未盡刬也。蓋取諸訟牒，則忿訐赴愬，多十室九空之民；取諸勸貸，則荒歉相仍，非粒米狼
translation_en:
…as Surveillance Commissioner, he built embankments to hold back the river and constructed more than five hundred reservoirs and ponds, irrigating twelve thousand qing of farmland. His achievements and beneficence extended throughout eight prefectures. These lands in Jiangyou occupy the same sites as in his time. Since he built works that benefited the people so greatly, surely, several centuries later, we should seek out his earlier wisdom. How could we use the failure of Du Ya’s advance preparations as an excuse to abandon even Jia Rang’s lowest-ranked scheme?
On high ground, therefore, channels should be dug to bring in water and secure its benefits; in low, wet places, embankments should be built and drainage channels opened to diminish its force. Even if sluice gates cannot be restored, plans to repair and maintain dams and weirs can still be carried out. The people’s strength should indeed be spared, but after the three farming seasons they may also be put to work. Prohibitions against monopolizing benefits must be strictly enforced, and those who build embankments for private advantage must be punished. Orders concerning proposed loans must be reiterated, and those who neglect the work must not be pardoned. Select worthy officials and give them undivided responsibility. Have them establish benefits lasting a hundred years, without begrudging the expense of the moment; let them plan for the security of the whole population, without being troubled by one person’s outcry. I have never seen water management fail to flourish under such measures.
As for famine preparedness, those responsible for fiscal administration have witnessed the hardships of the times and have already proposed accumulating grain. Their memorial was referred to the responsible authorities, and the regulations were certainly stringent. Granaries have now been established and accounts carefully drawn up, yet, measured against the prescribed quotas, the amounts still fall short of half. This is not because longstanding abuses have yet to be completely eradicated. For if grain is collected through litigation, those who angrily accuse one another and bring complaints are mostly people from communities where nine households in ten are destitute. If it is obtained by encouraging loans, repeated crop failures mean that these are no days of abundant grain…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
戾之日間有操一切者民輒曰夕餐可備
朝饔不可奪也求如例限誠難矣無已則
有說焉曰政以時舉可也故室如懸罄追
呼且亟則蠲租之命不可以不請扶老攜
幼背棄鄉井則招徠之策不可以不行膏
脂已盡囊橐日盈則貪墨之吏不可以不
罷南畝不事逐末日多則勸農之政不可
以不脩出官帑以平市肆之糶明斂散以
嚴漁獵之禁復隨地制宜因時通俗如社
===
倉之法務得其人以行之每旬月令守宰
具豐歉之狀報積貯之數然後課其殿最
焉他若先有司奏行如劉晏察災傷賑濟
如司馬光者皆可法也如是而荒政庶乎
其有備乎以弭盜言之監司者念切民瘼
甞督行保甲法矣俾互相應援意非不善
也第本境之盜與他處異連湖湘以為上
游陸闊而奔竄為易控長江以為右腋舟
多而撲滅甚難且鄱湖之中尤便匿藏孤
punctuated:
戾之日。間有操一切者，民輒曰：「夕餐可備，朝饔不可奪也。」求如例限，誠難矣。無已，則有說焉，曰：「政以時舉可也。」故室如懸罄，追呼且亟，則蠲租之命不可以不請；扶老攜幼，背棄鄉井，則招徠之策不可以不行；膏脂已盡，囊橐日盈，則貪墨之吏不可以不罷；南畝不事，逐末日多，則勸農之政不可以不脩。出官帑以平市肆之糶，明斂散以嚴漁獵之禁，復隨地制宜，因時通俗。如社倉之法，務得其人以行之，每旬月令守宰具豐歉之狀，報積貯之數，然後課其殿最焉。他若先有司奏行如劉晏，察災傷賑濟如司馬光者，皆可法也。如是，而荒政庶乎其有備乎！
以弭盜言之，監司者念切民瘼，甞督行保甲法矣，俾互相應援，意非不善也。第本境之盜與他處異，連湖湘以為上游，陸闊而奔竄為易；控長江以為右腋，舟多而撲滅甚難。且鄱湖之中，尤便匿藏，孤
translation_en:
… a time of abundant grain.
