Occasionally someone adopts sweeping measures, and the people invariably say: “You may make provision for our evening meal, but you must not take away our morning food.” Meeting the prescribed quotas is indeed difficult. If something must be done, there is an approach: “Undertake governmental measures as circumstances require.” Thus, when homes are as empty as suspended chime stones and demands for payment grow urgent, remission of the land tax must be requested. When people support their elders and carry their children away, abandoning their native villages, measures to attract them back must be implemented. When the people’s resources have been exhausted while officials’ purses grow fuller daily, corrupt officials must be dismissed. When the fields lie untended and ever more people pursue commerce, measures to encourage farming must be put into effect. Release treasury funds to stabilize grain prices in the markets; make grain purchases and distributions transparent, strictly enforcing prohibitions against predatory profiteering. Further, adapt measures to local conditions and accommodate customary practices according to circumstances. For measures such as the community granary system, make every effort to obtain suitable people to administer them. Every ten days or month, require prefects and magistrates to submit accounts of harvest abundance or scarcity and report the quantities stored; then assess their relative performance. Other examples—such as Liu Yan, who memorialized for action ahead of the responsible authorities, and Sima Guang, who investigated crop damage and provided relief—can all be emulated. With such measures, might famine administration not approach a state of preparedness?
As for suppressing banditry, the regional supervisory officials, deeply concerned about the people’s suffering, have already supervised implementation of the baojia system of household organization, enabling households to support one another. Their intention is certainly good. Yet banditry in this territory differs from that elsewhere. It adjoins the Hu-Xiang region upstream, with broad stretches of land that make flight easy; it commands the Yangzi River on its right flank, where the multitude of boats makes eradication exceedingly difficult. Moreover, Lake Poyang offers particularly convenient hiding places, lone [?] …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
潛鼠伏不時竊發急之則未必殄殲緩之
則恐滋聚嘯捕盜之法誠難講矣無已則
有說焉曰多方以弭之可也夫衣食不足
教化不脩則致盜之原可忽乎陽為驅使
陰相締結則捕盜之役可濫乎魚澤之地
為其淵藪則川澤之禁可弛乎豪猾大姓
招匿而坐分其利則積窩之民可縱乎廣
招諭以開其路禁游食以絕其黨而又申
示賞格多張譏諜若保甲之令必得其人
===
實行之復隨事以考其功過焉如龔遂治
渤海勸課農桑而盜賊悉平趙廣漢治京
兆發奸擿伏而寇宄屏息皆可法也如是
則盜賊庶幾其可弭乎大抵此四事者法
各有敝也脩之而使不至於滋敝者人也
民共於患也安之而俾不終於患者亦人
也得人之說雖為常談而竟取其效莫此
為要天下咸曰任人矣但今之為有司者
期會毛舉公移蝟集僅僅足以逃責力既
punctuated:
潛鼠伏，不時竊發，急之則未必殄殲，緩之則恐滋聚嘯。捕盜之法誠難講矣。無已，則有說焉，曰：多方以弭之可也。夫衣食不足，教化不脩，則致盜之原可忽乎？陽為驅使，陰相締結，則捕盜之役可濫乎？魚澤之地為其淵藪，則川澤之禁可弛乎？豪猾大姓招匿而坐分其利，則積窩之民可縱乎？廣招諭以開其路，禁游食以絕其黨，而又申示賞格，多張譏諜。若保甲之令，必得其人實行之，復隨事以考其功過焉。如龔遂治渤海，勸課農桑而盜賊悉平；趙廣漢治京兆，發奸擿伏而寇宄屏息，皆可法也。如是，則盜賊庶幾其可弭乎？
大抵此四事者，法各有敝也，脩之而使不至於滋敝者，人也；民共於患也，安之而俾不終於患者，亦人也。得人之說雖為常談，而竟取其效，莫此為要。天下咸曰任人矣，但今之為有司者，期會毛舉，公移蝟集，僅僅足以逃責，力既
translation_en:
…lurking and hiding like rats, they emerge from time to time to plunder. Press them hard, and they may still not be annihilated; ease the pressure, and one fears that they will multiply and rally their bands. Methods for apprehending bandits are indeed difficult to formulate. If something must be proposed, there is this suggestion: employ a variety of measures to suppress them. When clothing and food are insufficient and moral instruction is neglected, can the sources of banditry be ignored? When men ostensibly serve the authorities but secretly collude with bandits, can those assigned to apprehend bandits be recruited indiscriminately? When fishing grounds and marshes [?] provide their haunts, can restrictions governing waterways and marshes be relaxed? When powerful, unscrupulous families take them in and conceal them, effortlessly sharing their profits, can habitual harborers be indulged? Widely proclaim offers of surrender to open a way out for them; prohibit idle living to cut off their associates. Further, make the schedules of rewards clearly known and deploy numerous scouts and informants. As for the regulations governing the baojia system of mutual household responsibility, suitable men must be found to put them into actual practice, and their merits and faults must then be assessed in each matter. When Gong Sui governed Bohai, he encouraged and supervised farming and sericulture, and all the bandits were pacified. When Zhao Guanghan governed Jingzhao, he exposed wrongdoing and uncovered concealed crimes, and robbers and malefactors were cowed into silence. Both offer examples to follow. By such means, might banditry perhaps be suppressed?
In general, the regulations concerning each of these four matters have their defects. It is people who reform them and keep those defects from multiplying. The common people share in these afflictions; it is likewise people who bring them security and prevent their suffering from lasting indefinitely. Although the argument for finding suitable men is commonplace, nothing is more essential to achieving results in the end. Everyone throughout the realm speaks of appointing suitable men. Yet those who now serve as local officials face a proliferation of petty deadlines and reporting requirements, while official correspondence piles up like the spines of a hedgehog. They can barely do enough to escape blame, and their strength already …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有所弗及智復有所弗專而當官之功過
又不專責於四事焉如之何事能就理耶
故得一韓重華則屯田脩墾得一韋丹則
水利興復有劉晏司馬光則荒不必言備
矣有龔遂趙廣漢則盜不必言弭矣況四
者之治恒相須焉屯政脩則軍儲可省而
益以豫備荒之資水利興則荒蕪可起而
益以廣脩屯之助社倉建則什伍相資而
聯比益密保甲行則遐邇相警而畎畝益
===
安屯田水利自可次第而兼舉矣噫治網
者順緒之則理倒持之則棼再棼之後不
可以措手愚故謂捄法之敝在序其施而
計遠者得之牧羝者驅之則行牽之則不
行一一從而牽之益不行愚故謂除民之
患在因其俗而慮周者得之此狂瞽之見
也不識執事者以為何如
punctuated:
有所弗及，智復有所弗專，而當官之功過又不專責於四事焉，如之何事能就理耶？故得一韓重華，則屯田脩墾；得一韋丹，則水利興復；有劉晏、司馬光，則荒不必言備矣；有龔遂、趙廣漢，則盜不必言弭矣。況四者之治恒相須焉：屯政脩，則軍儲可省，而益以豫備荒之資；水利興，則荒蕪可起，而益以廣脩屯之助；社倉建，則什伍相資，而聯比益密；保甲行，則遐邇相警，而畎畝益安。屯田、水利，自可次第而兼舉矣。
噫！治網者，順緒之則理，倒持之則棼，再棼之後，不可以措手。愚故謂捄法之敝，在序其施，而計遠者得之。牧羝者，驅之則行，牽之則不行，一一從而牽之，益不行。愚故謂除民之患，在因其俗，而慮周者得之。此狂瞽之見也，不識執事者以為何如？
translation_en:
…cannot reach everything, and their understanding likewise cannot remain focused; moreover, officials’ merits and faults in office are not assessed solely in terms of these four matters. How, then, can affairs be brought into good order? Thus, obtain a Han Chonghua, and the military agricultural colonies will be restored and cultivated; obtain a Wei Dan, and water-control works will be revived. With Liu Yan and Sima Guang, there need be no further talk of preparing against famine; with Gong Sui and Zhao Guanghan, there need be no further talk of suppressing banditry. Furthermore, the administration of these four matters always depends on their mutual support. When the administration of military agricultural colonies is put in order, expenditure on military provisions can be reduced, augmenting the resources available for famine preparedness. When water-control works flourish, wasteland can be brought into cultivation, providing further support for expanding and improving the colonies. When community granaries are established, households grouped in tens and fives can assist one another, and their associations become closer. When the baojia system of household organization is implemented, those near and far warn one another, and the fields become more secure. Military agricultural colonies and water-control works can then naturally be undertaken together, in due sequence.
Alas! Someone putting a net in order straightens it by following its threads, but tangles it by holding it upside down. Once it has been tangled again, there is nowhere to lay a hand. Thus, in my humble judgment, remedying the defects of institutions depends on ordering their implementation; those who plan for the long term will succeed. When tending rams, drive them and they move; pull them and they do not. If one goes after each and pulls it individually, they become still less willing to move. Thus, in my humble judgment, removing the people’s troubles depends on working with their customs; those whose deliberations are comprehensive will succeed. These are the views of an ignorant and presumptuous man. I do not know what you, the officials in charge, will think of them.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
皇上即阼之四年
詔天下所司大比士于鄉江右試
事御史劉思問監臨之區裁
規布貫行惟勑凡內外事事
者罔不協共故得士視往歲
爲盛旣考成錄以
===
獻魯聞從諸大夫之後受末簡
颺言曰於惟休哉
國家所以養士與士之自養者
斯明徵哉伏聞
聖祖高皇帝與儒臣論易頤卦天
地養萬物聖人養賢以及萬
民因言人主職在養民若所
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

皇上即阼之四年，詔天下所司大比士于鄉。江右試事，御史劉思問監臨之，區裁規布，貫行惟勑。凡內外事事者，罔不協共，故得士視往歲爲盛。旣考成，錄以獻。魯聞從諸大夫之後，受末簡，颺言曰：「於惟休哉！國家所以養士與士之自養者，斯明徵哉！」伏聞聖祖高皇帝與儒臣論《易》頤卦：「天地養萬物，聖人養賢以及萬民。」因言：「人主職在養民，若所
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the fourth year after His Majesty ascended the throne, he commanded the responsible authorities throughout the realm to conduct the triennial examinations of scholars in the provinces. In Jiangyou, Censor Liu Siwen supervised the examination. Responsibilities were apportioned, arrangements laid out, and implementation kept under strict direction. All those serving within and outside the examination precincts worked together cooperatively; consequently, the scholars selected surpassed those of previous years. When the examination was completed, a record was compiled for presentation to the throne. Lu Wen, following after the other gentlemen, was entrusted with the concluding pages and proclaimed: “Ah, how splendid! Here is clear evidence of how the state nurtures scholars and how scholars cultivate themselves!”

I have respectfully heard that the Sacred Progenitor, Emperor Gao, discussed with his Confucian ministers the hexagram Yi, Nourishment, in the Book of Changes: “Heaven and earth nourish the myriad things; the sage nourishes worthy men and thereby extends nourishment to the myriad people.” He then said: “The ruler’s duty lies in nourishing the people. If those whom …

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
養得賢與之共治則民皆得
所養至論文以明道德通世
務爲賢以險怪浮藻爲戒大
哉
聖謨立極陶型
列聖承休率遵彜憲逮我
皇上嗣服覃棫樸之化昭追琢之
===
章士在所養者咸澡濯迅發
矧江右乃
聖祖功先耆定
存神過化人士得於涵濡者不
旣悠乆而淵深乎譽聞濫兹
役初入疆仰觀乾苞天相昭
回躔台聯耀天精洩其祕矣
punctuated: 養得賢，與之共治，則民皆得所養。至論文，以明道德、通世務爲賢，以險怪浮藻爲戒。大哉，聖謨！立極陶型，列聖承休，率遵彜憲。逮我皇上嗣服，覃棫樸之化，昭追琢之章，士在所養者咸澡濯迅發。矧江右乃聖祖功先耆定，存神過化，人士得於涵濡者，不旣悠乆而淵深乎？譽聞濫兹役，初入疆，仰觀乾苞，天相昭回，躔台聯耀，天精洩其祕矣。
translation_en:
…if those whom he nurtures are worthy, and he governs together with them, then all the people will receive the nurture they need. As for evaluating writing, he esteemed work that elucidated the Way and virtue and showed an understanding of worldly affairs, and warned against strained oddity and empty ornament. Great indeed were these sagely counsels! They established the supreme standard and molded men of talent. Successive sage emperors inherited this blessing and all observed these enduring statutes. Since our present Emperor succeeded to the throne, he has extended the transforming influence celebrated in “The Oak and the Thorn” and displayed the refinement achieved through carving and polishing. All the scholars receiving this nurture have purified themselves and advanced with vigor.
Moreover, Jiangyou was where the Sagely Progenitor first secured his achievements in pacification. His presence worked spiritual wonders, and wherever he passed he transformed the people. Has not the nurturing influence received by its scholars been both enduring and profound? I, Yuwen 譽聞 [?], have undeservedly been entrusted with this assignment. On first entering the province, I looked upward to observe the portents of Heaven: celestial signs shone in their circuits, and the stars of the Three Terraces glittered together [?]. Heaven’s essence had revealed its mysteries.

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
俯察坤符匡廬磐礴彭蠡洽
泓地道毓其靈矣載稽儒先
往籍太極有圖鹿洞有規人
文啓其端矣爰徵星紀歲在
庚午夫庚爲金萬物斂更於
庚計然所謂金穰之候咢布
于午而午爲火爲一元中數
===
===
文華象也多士應
更化文明之運育名邦承諸儒
道學大明之後充所養發爲
文章其體粹以融其氣浩以
嚴幡然而龍文炘然而鳳藻
風灑露沐霧滃雲蒸崇巖絶
獻壁立萬仞湍瀾驚濤勢瀉
punctuated: 俯察坤符，匡廬磐礴，彭蠡洽泓，地道毓其靈矣。載稽儒先往籍，太極有圖，鹿洞有規，人文啓其端矣。爰徵星紀，歲在庚午。夫庚爲金，萬物斂更於庚，計然所謂金穰之候，咢布于午，而午爲火，爲一元中數，文華象也。多士應更化文明之運，育名邦，承諸儒道學大明之後，充所養，發爲文章。其體粹以融，其氣浩以嚴，幡然而龍文，炘然而鳳藻，風灑露沐，霧滃雲蒸，崇巖絶獻，壁立萬仞，湍瀾驚濤，勢瀉
translation_en:
…Looking down to examine the auspicious signs of earth: Kuanglu rises in massive grandeur, and Pengli spreads deep and broad; the Way of earth has nurtured its numinous potency. Examining, moreover, the writings of earlier Confucian masters, we find a Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and Rules of the White Deer Grotto Academy: here human culture found its beginnings. Turning to the celestial reckoning, the year is gengwu. Geng corresponds to metal; under geng, the myriad things gather in and renew themselves. What Ji Ran called the season of “abundance under metal” unfolds in wu [?]. Wu corresponds to fire and is the central number of a primordial cycle, an image of cultural brilliance.

The many scholars respond to this era of renewed governance and flourishing culture. Nurtured in this renowned region, they inherit the legacy of the Confucian masters’ great illumination of the Learning of the Way. Bringing what they have cultivated to fullness, they express it in literary compositions. Their substance is pure and harmonious; their vital force, vast and dignified. They unfurl like dragon patterns and shine like phoenix ornament; washed by wind and bathed in dew, they billow like mist and rise like clouds. Lofty crags and sheer heights [?] stand like walls ten thousand fathoms high; rushing currents and startling waves pour forth with a force that…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
千里反刓以樸統眞於一以
古聖賢爲宗模弗越于引筆
行墨之外殆萃天地山川眞
精以呈奇瑞者乎蓋養之豫
渾龐有本斯敷之言文質適
中𪘏𪘏乎
聖訓所謂明道德通世務之文而
===
險怪浮藻弗庸也言足以興
誠不世之遇行且釋蹻通籍
尚思
朝廷所以作養之意自靖自獻
大而建上宰司調燮以輔養
君德次而職羣牧撫字休養不失
民望培元氣壽
punctuated:
千里，反刓以樸，統眞於一，以古聖賢爲宗模，弗越于引筆行墨之外，殆萃天地山川眞精以呈奇瑞者乎！蓋養之豫，渾龐有本，斯敷之言，文質適中，𪘏𪘏乎聖訓所謂「明道德、通世務之文」，而險怪浮藻弗庸也。
言足以興，誠不世之遇！行且釋蹻通籍，尚思朝廷所以作養之意。自靖自獻，大而建上宰司，調燮以輔養君德；次而職羣牧，撫字休養，不失民望，培元氣，壽
translation_en:
…for a thousand li. They turn from excessive carving to simplicity and unite the true in oneness, taking the ancient sages and worthies as their masters and models—all within the movement of brush and ink. Might their writing indeed gather the true essence of Heaven and Earth, mountains and rivers, to display extraordinary auspicious signs? Because their cultivation has been undertaken beforehand, their ample, integral substance has firm roots. Thus, when expressed in words, ornament and substance are properly balanced: 𪘏𪘏 [?], writings of the kind described in the sagely instruction as “illuminating morality and comprehending the affairs of the world,” with no use for the bizarre or for superficial embellishment.
Their words suffice to inspire; truly, this is an opportunity seldom encountered in an age! Soon they will put aside their straw sandals and enter the official registers. They should ever reflect upon the court’s intention in fostering and educating them, setting themselves right and offering themselves in service. At the highest level, they may be appointed to the offices of chief ministers, harmonizing affairs to assist in nurturing the ruler’s virtue; at the next level, they may serve as local administrators, caring for the people and allowing them rest and recuperation, without disappointing their hopes, nourishing the primal vitality and prolonging the life of…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國脉於無疆斯不負所舉矣苟
或屬厭温飽厚爲封殖計其
不辜
今日盛典蒙滓山川靦顏先哲乎
昔唐王勃序洪都物華謂劒
光見斗牛間夫劒金精也火
協其數久於藏蓄一旦發之
===
然必拭以華陰之土淬以西
平之泉越山之砥斯麗飭交
陳文縵駭目雄稜剸割爲天
下利器爾多士負丹霞之輝
青雲之制秉金乘火固利器
也由此益加辟灌砥礪成文
經武緯之具以利
punctuated:
國脉於無疆，斯不負所舉矣。苟或屬厭温飽，厚爲封殖計，其不辜今日盛典，蒙滓山川，靦顏先哲乎？

昔唐王勃序洪都，物華謂劒光見斗牛間。夫劒，金精也，火協其數，久於藏蓄，一旦發之。然必拭以華陰之土，淬以西平之泉、越山之砥，斯麗飭交陳，文縵駭目，雄稜剸割，爲天下利器。爾多士負丹霞之輝、青雲之制，秉金乘火，固利器也。由此益加辟灌砥礪，成文經武緯之具，以利
translation_en:
…the lifeblood of the state without end: thus you will not betray the purpose for which you were selected. But if, sated with warmth and full bellies, you devote yourselves to accumulating wealth for your own advantage, would you not betray today’s splendid ceremony, sully these mountains and rivers, and stand shamefaced before the sages of the past?

Long ago, Wang Bo of the Tang, in his preface on Hongdu, described the splendor of its natural treasures by saying that a sword’s radiance appeared between the Dipper and Ox constellations. A sword is the essence of metal; fire accords with its destined cycle. Long stored away, it is brought forth one day. Yet it must be polished with earth from Huayin, tempered in spring water from Xiping, and sharpened on a whetstone from the mountains of Yue. Only then do its splendid adornments appear together, its patterned surface dazzle the eye, and its mighty edge cut and cleave, making it a keen instrument for all under Heaven. You assembled scholars possess the radiance of rosy clouds and the stature of azure clouds; endowed with metal and aided by fire, you are indeed keen instruments. From this point, apply yourselves still further to cleansing [?], grinding, and honing, becoming instruments whose warp is civil accomplishment and whose weft is military achievement, so as to benefit…

title: 隆慶四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國家直劔云乎哉愼毋若鉛刀
頑缺爲人所訾也雖然江右
今昔爲文獻之都英才之伏
無盡而取之不竭今限於
制不能盡羅而致之者宜益充所
養蓄儲其材俾爲異時搜逑
索耦者需焉亦有司者所厚
===
望于諸士也
河南開封府許州儒學學正
吳譽聞謹序
punctuated:
國家，直劔云乎哉？愼毋若鉛刀頑缺，爲人所訾也。雖然，江右今昔爲文獻之都，英才之伏無盡，而取之不竭。今限於制，不能盡羅而致之者，宜益充所養，蓄儲其材，俾爲異時搜逑索耦者需焉，亦有司者所厚望于諸士也。
河南開封府許州儒學學正吳譽聞謹序。
translation_en:
…the state. Can this be said merely of swords? Take care not to resemble a leaden blade, dull and chipped, inviting others’ reproach. Nevertheless, Jiangyou has been, both past and present, a center of learning and worthy men. Its hidden talents are boundless, and drawing upon them cannot exhaust them. Those whom we cannot now gather in and recruit, owing to the limits imposed by regulation, should further deepen their cultivation and store up their abilities, so that they may meet the needs of those who will seek worthy companions and peers in times to come. This, too, is the earnest hope that we officials place in you scholars.
Preface respectfully written by Wu Yuwen, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.
